Problem: `HardwareThermalService` persisted two `VaultBufferHandle<T>` fields and refreshed them through `ResolveBuffer`. This kept Core runtime manager on pointer-bearing descriptors even though its thermal severity byte and blackbox ring are owned Vault buffers.
Solution: Replace both fields with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve local `NativeArray<T>` views through `TryResolveHandle`, allocate through `GetGenerationHandle<T>`, and release descriptors through `ReleaseBuffer` during teardown or DataVault hot-swap.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving this service on legacy bridge was rejected because it is small Core-owned manager with clear Vault ownership. Rewriting hardware policy/scalability behavior was rejected because task is pointer safety, not thermal policy redesign.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same thermal sampling cadence and blackbox size. Middle/high/ultra preserve thermal diagnostics without cached pointer state; no binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one O(1) generation compare when severity byte or 300-frame blackbox is touched. Cold teardown now returns two Vault references instead of leaking them across service reloads.
## Decision 021 - SignalBus frame snapshots are phase-local views
Problem: `SignalBus<T>` kept static `NativeArray<T> _frameSnapshot` alias and legacy `VaultBufferHandle<T>`. Because every closed signal lane can survive across frames, this was generic long-lived Vault alias at Core signal scale.
Solution: Remove static `NativeArray<T>` field, convert `_frameSnapshotHandle` to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve local snapshot view in each read/flush/filter/sort path, refresh descriptor with `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>` after generation churn, and release descriptor on lane disposal.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached view for speed was rejected because task is specifically to prevent stale relocatable aliases. Rewriting SignalBus policy, lane lists, or signal DTO layouts was rejected because those changes are outside pointer-safety lane and already have unrelated working-tree edits.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay only flat generation compare when signal snapshots are consumed or flushed. High/ultra keep deterministic snapshot sorting/coalescing and can tolerate Vault relocation stress without stale alias reuse.
Hardware Impact: One O(1) metadata compare replaces long-lived alias hazard across all typed signal lanes. No GC is added; no interface array hot dispatch is introduced by this pass.
## Decision 022 - Alignment telemetry proves faults without legacy handles
Problem: `Arm64AlignmentTelemetry` used static legacy Vault handle and three `.Resolve(vault)` routes for diagnostic ring that records alignment faults. stale diagnostic ring would weaken exact evidence path used to prove ARM64 layout violations.
Solution: Convert ring to `VaultGenerationHandle<AlignmentTelemetryEntry>`, resolve local views for record/read/dump, and release old descriptor if cached Vault instance changes before reacquiring ring.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving SHINOBU_204 diagnostic code untouched was rejected because it is Core memory telemetry route and small enough to migrate safely. Adding copied managed ring was rejected because diagnostics must remain Vault-backed and zero-GC in record/read paths.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same 300-entry ring and cold dump path. High/ultra/editor retain richer alignment fault proof without cached pointer handles.
Hardware Impact: Diagnostic record/read paths pay one flat generation compare and no GC. Vault hot-swap no longer leaks previous alignment telemetry descriptor.
## Decision 023 - Simulation bucketer tables use generation descriptors
Problem: `ModuloSimulationBucketer` persisted eight legacy `VaultBufferHandle<T>` fields for front/work bucket tables, EWMA cost/load tables, rebalance scratch, frame state, and 300-frame blackbox. Re-init/dispose cleared handles locally without returning Vault references.
Solution: Convert all eight fields to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, allocate through `GetGenerationHandle`, resolve method-local `NativeArray<T>` views through `TryResolveHandle`, and release all non-zero descriptors through `ReleaseBuffer` after pending rebalance job is completed.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping bucketer on legacy bridge was rejected because this service sits in Core dispatcher cadence path and is small enough to migrate safely. Rewriting bucketing math or unrelated existing quality-curve work was rejected because current pass is pointer safety.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous bucketing cadence and survival distribution behavior. Middle/high/ultra retain rebalance and blackbox telemetry while removing stale descriptor state; no binary hardware branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare when bucketing table is touched. Cold re-init/teardown now performs eight release calls and prevents Vault refcount leaks.
## Decision 024 - Lockstep hash sources validate resolved views, not cached ptr
Problem: `LockstepStateValidator.TryGetHashSourceBuffer` acquired local `VaultBufferHandle<T>`, checked `handle.ptr` for alignment, then called `handle.Resolve(vault)`. That route proved cached pointer, not generation-validated transient view actually hashed for determinism.
Solution: Use `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>` and `TryResolveHandle` to obtain local `NativeArray<T>` view first, then validate alignment through `buffer.GetUnsafeReadOnlyPtr()` before hashing.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping local legacy handle was rejected because rollback hash proof should not depend on any cached pointer field. Persisting hash-source descriptor was rejected because this method only needs phase-local view.
Scalability potential: lockstep hash cadence remains governed by existing continuous quality/stress curve. Low through ultra keep identical pointer safety semantics with no tier branch.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare only when hash-source buffer is requested; no GC and no additional persistent native state.
## Decision 025 - Input bridge facade writes through resolved NativeArray
Problem: `H8InputMappingFacade` wrote `BridgeInputFacadeBindings` through local `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and `ResolvePointer`, leaving bridge hydration on cached-pointer route.
Solution: Allocate or acquire buffer with `GetGenerationHandle`, resolve local `NativeArray<H8InputFacadeBindingEntry>` through `TryResolveHandle`, clear via transient `GetUnsafePtr()` on that view, and write entries through indexed `NativeArray` access.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointer writes was rejected because ScriptableObject bridge sync can run in Play Mode after Vault relocation. Introducing persistent facade-owned handle was rejected because mapping source is serialized facade list, not runtime buffer owner.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same bridge sync behavior; high/ultra get same data route without cached pointer state. No binary tier branch was added.
Hardware Impact: Sync path pays one flat generation compare and one transient MemClear; no additional GC beyond existing serialized editor list.
## Decision 026 - Prefab registry binder hydrates bridge DTOs through local views
Problem: `H8PrefabRegistryRuntimeBinder` hydrated prefab mapping and lore link buffers through local `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and `ResolvePointer` in both bind and clear paths.
Solution: Acquire `BridgePrefabMapping` and `BridgePrefabLoreLinks` with `GetGenerationHandle`, resolve local `NativeArray<T>` views through `TryResolveHandle`, clear through transient `GetUnsafePtr()` on those views, and write DTO entries by index.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointer hydration was rejected because prefab registry binding can run during Play Mode after Vault relocation. Persisting static binder handles was rejected because registry asset is authoring source and binder does not own runtime lifetime.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same registry bind route. Middle/high/ultra retain runtime acoustic/lore signal publication without cached Vault pointer state.
Hardware Impact: Bind path pays two flat generation compares and two transient MemClear calls; no added managed allocation.
## Decision 027 - Design bridge runtime avoids local pointer-bearing descriptors
Problem: `H8BridgeFacadeRuntime` used local `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and `ResolvePointer` for design value bytes, macro header persistence, and 300-frame facade telemetry dump ring. These are local variables, but they still route bridge live-tuning writes through obsolete cached-pointer API.
Solution: Convert each route to `GetGenerationHandle` or `TryGetGenerationHandle`, then resolve method-local `NativeArray<T>` through `TryResolveHandle`. Value writes use transient pointer derived from resolved byte view only for aligned float store; telemetry hash/dump now reads entries through resolved `NativeArray<T>`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy bridge because handles were local was rejected; source audit policy is to prevent new code from learning `ResolvePointer`. Persisting bridge handles was rejected because bridge facade asset, not runtime, owns authoring fact.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay one flat generation compare per bridge buffer touched. Middle/high/ultra keep live tuning, macro persistence, and blackbox dumps without cached Vault pointer state; no binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids stale pointer trust in live tuning and blackbox dump routes. extra O(1) generation compare is colder than existing facade iteration, signal publication, and dump IO.
## Decision 028 - Content authority ledgers use generation descriptors
Problem: `ContentRuntimeServices` persisted six `VaultBufferHandle<T>` fields across bundle ref counter and content runtime for resident bundle state, telemetry, and pending-load queues. These managers can survive DataVault replacement and were resolving raw pointers from pointer-bearing descriptors.
Solution: Convert all six fields to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add local resolve-or-acquire helpers that return `NativeArray<T>` views, derive pointers only from those views inside current method, and release descriptors on ref-counter vault rebind, runtime teardown, and DataVault hot-swap.
Rejected Alternatives: Ignoring content because it had unrelated Addressables/hot-swap changes was rejected; Vault handle edits are separable. Rewriting Addressables ownership was rejected because that is existing SHINOBU_203/ContentAuthority work and outside this pointer-safety pass.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same pending-load and telemetry cadence with one flat generation compare per access. Middle/high/ultra retain content blackbox evidence and live residency accounting without stale Vault aliases; no binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 loses persistent pointer-bearing descriptor fields in content manager. Teardown/hot-swap now returns six Vault references instead of leaking or leaving invalid descriptors after service replacement.
## Decision 029 - Base homeostasis buffers use generation descriptors
Problem: `HomeostasisBrain.cs` persisted three legacy handles for global hardware metrics, frame-time samples, and its 300-frame blackbox. This authority controls quality pressure and survives registry DataVault replacement, so stale handles here can poison global throttling.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors, resolve or reacquire method-local `NativeArray<T>` views through `TryResolveHandle`, avoid clearing existing moved buffers after generation churn by probing `TryGetGenerationHandle` before allocation, and release descriptors during shutdown or DataVault hot-swap.
Rejected Alternatives: Migrating larger `HomeostasisBrain.ScalabilityDictator.cs` in same pass was rejected because it owns additional job-fenced state and deserves separate review. Keeping base file on legacy handles was rejected because base migration is compact and directly protects global quality authority.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous `GlobalQualityWeight` path with one flat generation compare per buffer. Middle/high/ultra retain homeostasis blackbox evidence and visual-overkill pressure policy without cached Vault aliases.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes three persistent pointer-bearing descriptors from global pressure manager. Shutdown and hot-swap now return three Vault refs instead of clearing static fields only.
## Decision 030 - Scalability dictator buffers use generation descriptors
Problem: `HomeostasisBrain.ScalabilityDictator.cs` still persisted seven `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and used `.Resolve(vault)` / `GetElementAsRef` for health, quality state, tuning, mock load, mock terrain proof, CSV scratch, and 300-frame oscilloscope. This kept highest-level quality authority on pointer-bearing routes after base file was migrated.
Solution: Convert all seven buffers to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, reuse base `TryResolveOrAcquire` helper, and resolve only method-local `NativeArray<T>` views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Editor/test facades copy structs out of resolved view, sanitize/mutate, and write row back by index. DataVault hot-swap now releases scalability descriptors against previous Vault before `_dataVault` is replaced, after completing pending mock terrain sampler job.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping dictator on legacy bridge was rejected because it is Core-owned and controls `GlobalQualityWeight`. Holding `ref` rows from `GetElementAsRef` was rejected because ref access is derived from cached-pointer compatibility handle. Rewriting continuous scalability math was rejected because existing math already uses smooth weights and this pass is memory safety.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain cheap mock terrain proof and quality telemetry with one generation compare per buffer touch. Middle/high/ultra keep visual-overkill policy, oscilloscope, CSV tuning bridge, and shader-quality globals without any persistent Vault alias.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes seven pointer-bearing descriptors from global pressure dictator. Hot tick writes pay one flat metadata compare for state and telemetry views; teardown/hot-swap now returns seven Vault refs instead of leaking or clearing local descriptors only.
## Decision 031 - AUP origin-shift lanes use generation descriptors
Problem: `AupOriginShiftCoordinator` persisted eight `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and resolved AUP states, velocities, history, telemetry, runtime state, mock camera, CSV scratch, and padded counter through `.Resolve(vault)`. These buffers are direct targets for origin-shift and defrag relocation, so stale descriptors here undermine AUP precision contract.
Solution: Convert all eight descriptors to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add local `TryResolveOrAcquire` helper, and route tick/rebase/editor/CSV paths through method-local `NativeArray<T>` views from `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. On cached Vault replacement, release all non-zero descriptors against previous Vault before clearing local state.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping origin shift on legacy bridge was rejected because this file moves `double3` AUP payloads and can run during same maintenance windows that relocate Vault buffers. Rewriting origin-shift algorithms was rejected because existing AUP math already subtracts in double precision before float-local work; this pass is descriptor safety.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain time-sliced rebase batches from `GlobalQualityWeight`; middle/high/ultra keep larger batches and telemetry without cached Vault aliases. No binary tier branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare when AUP lanes are resolved. 64-byte padded counter remains false-sharing isolated; hot rebase jobs still receive phase-local pointers derived from validated `NativeArray<T>` views.
## Decision 032 - Crash blackbox no longer retains Vault aliases
Problem: `GlobalTelemetryBus.Blackbox.cs` persisted eleven legacy `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and eleven static Vault-backed `NativeArray<T>` aliases. buffers were lifetime-locked, but Core manager retaining native views still violates generation-handle contract and hides release/refcount leaks during crash-path shutdown.
Solution: Convert all blackbox lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add local `TryResolveBlackboxBuffer` helper, and resolve method-local `NativeArray<T>` views in event push, source registration, frame commit, dump writing, MMF flushing, watchdog probing, and editor copy routes. Binding failure and teardown now release every non-zero descriptor after unlocking relocation fences.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying on `TryLockBuffer` alone was rejected because it prevents relocation instead of proving manager can survive relocation-era handles. Keeping cached arrays only for speed was rejected because this is forensic infrastructure, not sub-0.1 ms gameplay solver.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same 300-frame blackbox and MMF cadence with descriptor validation only on touched lanes. Middle/high/ultra retain richer crash forensics and watchdog coverage without persistent Vault views. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare when blackbox lane is touched; shutdown now returns eleven Vault refs instead of leaking them. Long-lived manager-side `NativeArray<T>` aliases are removed from this file.
## Decision 033 - Memory sentinel validates targets under generation locks
Problem: `MemorySentinelRuntime` persisted ten `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and used `TryGetBufferHandle` / `ResolvePointer` to watch external targets. It also unlocked target buffers before consuming validation results and rollback copies, leaving relocation window around stored target pointers.
Solution: Convert owned sentinel lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` with `TryResolveOrAcquire`, resolve all owned buffers through local `NativeArray<T>` views, and acquire external target pointers from `TryGetGenerationHandle` plus `TryResolveHandle`. `CompleteValidationJob` now keeps locks active through `ConsumeResults` and releases them in `finally` after rollback/correction work.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `ResolvePointer` in memory sentinel was rejected because it audits stale pointers while using stale-pointer API. Removing target pointers from `MemorySentinelTargetDTO` in this pass was rejected because scheduled validation job still needs locked phase-local pointers; lock fence now covers their full use window.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing `GlobalQualityWeight` cadence collapse for validation frequency. Middle/high/ultra can validate more frequently without stale descriptor debt. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare for each sentinel lane or watched target view. rollback copy no longer races against Vault defrag after target unlock.
## Decision 034 - Input haptics tuner stops teaching legacy pointer APIs
Problem: `InputCurveHapticsTunerWindow.cs` was editor-only, but it still demonstrated `GetBufferHandle`, `VaultBufferHandle<T>`, and `GetElementAsRef` for deterministic input profile/state buffers. That keeps obsolete pointer-bearing access patterns alive in designer-facing code and makes future runtime copy-paste defects more likely.
Solution: Replace local profile/state handles with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve `NativeArray<T>` views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` inside `OnGUI`, read rows by index, mutate profile value locally, and write row zero back by index after `EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck`.
Rejected Alternatives: Ignoring editor code was rejected because Task 17/18 facades are part of SHINOBU_202 human-control surface. Releasing descriptors from window was rejected because this window is not owner of `ShinobuInputProfile` or `ShinobuInputCurrentDto`; it only observes or edits owner-created buffers through existing Vault route.
Scalability potential: Low devices see no runtime cost because this is editor-only. Middle/high/ultra editor sessions still get live curve/haptics visualization while resolving through same generation descriptor path as runtime managers.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime unchanged. Editor repaint pays two flat generation compares and copies 88 bytes of DTO data, removing all obsolete pointer-bearing source hits from this facade.
## Decision 035 - Input dispatcher resolves Vault views per phase
Problem: `InputDispatcher.cs` persisted twelve `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and used `.Resolve`, `GetElementAsRef`, `GetElementAsReadOnlyRef`, and background-thread `_inputReplaySnapshotHandle.ptr` path. Deterministic input, haptic commands, XR state, and replay snapshot buffers cross frame boundaries, so cached Vault pointers here can produce UAF during defrag or DataVault replacement.
Solution: Convert all input-owned Vault descriptors to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add resolve/acquire helpers that return method-local `NativeArray<T>` views, replace ref access with row index copies, release descriptors on shutdown and DataVault hot-swap, and move replay snapshot copying into `StageInputReplaySnapshot` while local view is valid. replay worker now flushes MMF only and does not dereference Vault memory.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping replay worker on cached Vault pointer was rejected because it is clearest stale-pointer race in file. Removing replay snapshot lane outright was rejected because deterministic bridge still expects Vault-backed snapshot audit row; safer minimal change is generation resolution plus phase-local copy.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay flat generation comparisons for input/haptic/XR lanes and keep existing continuous haptic throttle behavior under pressure. Middle/high/ultra preserve deterministic replay, richer haptic composition, and XR look-at state without storing Vault aliases.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes twelve pointer-bearing descriptors and one background stale-pointer path. replay path still copies same 12 KB payload at its existing cadence; hot input writes add only metadata generation checks.
## Decision 036 - System dispatcher owns phase fences through generation descriptors
Problem: `SystemDispatcher.cs` persisted legacy Vault handles for H8 time, dispatcher blackbox, master job/fence telemetry, presentation suppression, and static raycast command/hit buffers. dispatcher is also system that defines when Vault relocation is legal, so cached pointer-bearing descriptors in this file can invalidate entire "defrag only between phases" safety model.
Solution: Convert all dispatcher-owned descriptors to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add single generation resolve/acquire helper that returns method-local `NativeArray<T>` views, and release old descriptors during shutdown or DataVault service replacement. Scheduled raycast buffers keep their existing Vault lock fence while scheduled `RaycastCommand` job owns local views; handles themselves are pointer-free.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `ResolveBuffer` around domain fence array was rejected because AUP hard-fence cleanup can run during relocation pressure. Keeping static raycast handles as legacy pointers was rejected because raycast scheduling spans frames and can outlive compaction window. Rewriting dispatcher scheduler was rejected because this pass is descriptor safety, not topology refactor.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous `GlobalQualityWeight` behavior for frame pacing, temporal compression, and presentation suppression; middle/high/ultra keep richer master telemetry and raycast scheduling without cached Vault aliases. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays flat generation comparisons when dispatcher lanes are touched. expensive work remains job dependency combining, raycast scheduling, and ring writes; stale pointer access during Vault defrag is removed from phase owner.
## Decision 037 - Analytics exporter worker resolves locked buffers by generation
Problem: `AsynchronousTelemetryExporter.cs` persisted seventeen `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and `H8_Analytics_IO` worker created `NativeArray<T>` views directly from cached `handle.ptr` values. exporter also wrote hot ingress events through `_ingressCursorHandle.ptr` and selected ingress handle pointer, leaving both main-thread and background-thread UAF paths.
Solution: Convert every exporter-owned descriptor to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve main-thread and worker views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, and retain existing owner-tagged Vault locks only as compaction fence while worker is alive. Shutdown releases descriptors only after `StopWorker()` succeeds and worker locks are removed.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping worker-owned buffers on `VaultBufferHandle<T>.ptr` was rejected because lock is relocation fence, not permission for managers to persist pointer metadata. Releasing descriptors when `StopWorker()` fails was rejected because worker can still be alive and resolving handoff/dump buffers; preserving locks is safer failure mode.
Scalability potential: Low devices still shed routine analytics continuously through `GlobalQualityWeight`, backlog pressure, and deterministic AUP hashing. Middle/high/ultra keep richer route samples, heatmap debug, network batch size, and disk replay without cached Vault pointer route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks for event ingress and worker scratch resolution. expensive worker path remains RLE/network/disk I/O; stale Vault pointer dereference is removed from both main and background threads.
## Decision 038 - Acoustic echo static queue uses pointer-free Vault descriptors
Problem: `AcousticEchoLocationRuntime.cs` persisted four static `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and resolved pending taps, frame taps, job results, and 300-frame blackbox through cached pointer metadata. Echo tap queues can cross frame/defrag windows, so static queue was UAF candidate even though Burst tracking job itself only needs phase-local views.
Solution: Convert four AISensory lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add resolve/acquire/release helpers, and keep all queue drain/drop, job schedule, blackbox, and fault dump access on method-local `NativeArray<T>` views returned by `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Dispose and DataVault replacement release only descriptors owned by this static runtime; active tracking fence is completed before old descriptors are released.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `ReleaseOwnerBuffers(SystemID.AISensory)` was rejected because it can free unrelated AISensory buffers owned by neighboring static services. Replacing tracking job or acoustic scoring model was rejected because this pass is pointer safety; existing quality-weight scoring already gives continuous cheap/expensive behavior.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep direct echo breadcrumb scoring and quality-byte attenuation; middle/high/ultra preserve richer portal/movement/sonar tap density without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation compare when enqueueing, draining, scheduling, or writing blackbox rows. expensive path remains existing O(n) tap scan capped at 32 taps; stale Vault pointer metadata is removed from static sensory queue.
## Decision 039 - Path funnel navmesh resolves WFC invalidation lanes by generation
Problem: `PathFunnelNavmeshRuntime.cs` persisted five `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors, relied on legacy handle `Length` and `GenerationID`, and resolved mutation/telemetry/runtime-state views through `.Resolve(...)`. fast tick also used `TryGetBuffer` for WFC grid flags, bypassing generation descriptor route used by migrated consumers.
Solution: Convert path-funnel owned lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, derive actual lengths from transient resolved views, and route every active-path, cell-mask, invalidation, telemetry, runtime-state, and WFC-grid access through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Disable/hot-swap releases only this component's owned descriptors.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `TryGetBuffer` for external WFC grid was rejected because it normalizes direct Vault views outside generation descriptor contract. Releasing all `SystemID.AIPathfinding` buffers was rejected because other pathfinding systems can share owner ID.
Scalability potential: Low devices still use bounded 500-bit masks and ring cursors; middle/high/ultra can increase active path and invalidation capacities while retaining phase-local descriptor resolution. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays flat generation checks when path APIs or tick phases touch Vault lanes. dominant cost remains bounded scan of active corridors against WFC cell masks; stale pointer metadata is removed from path invalidation state.
## Decision 040 - WFC laser cut tool writes Vault progress through phase-local arrays
Problem: `WfcLaserCutRuntime.cs` persisted two static `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and converted their cached `.ptr` fields into raw `float*` progress and telemetry pointers. same file used `GlobalRegistry.ScalabilityTier` for visual overkill, producing hard tier branch in user-facing VFX path.
Solution: Convert cut progress and blackbox lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve local `NativeArray<T>` views per cut attempt, and rewrite progress clear/telemetry/dump paths to index those views instead of pointers. Replace tier branching with continuous smoothstep over `HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight`, modulated by system stress headroom.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointers as "short-lived" locals was rejected because they were derived from persistent pointer-bearing descriptors and used in gameplay truth writes. Keeping tier switch was rejected because quality-weight already supplies required continuous control scalar.
Scalability potential: Low devices collapse molten/spark overkill smoothly as quality/stress drops; middle/high/ultra regain richer cut visuals continuously without feature pop. No binary quality branch remains in this file.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation checks per active cut attempt and few scalar ops for visual curve. expensive work remains shader feedback and signal fanout; stale Vault pointer writes are removed from tool path.
## Decision 041 - Ladder climb IK schedules only generation-resolved views
Problem: `ProceduralLadderClimbRuntime.cs` persisted five `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and staged its IK solve job through `.Resolve(_dataVault)` views. Disable/destroy only cleared handles, leaving Vault refcount/generation state untouched.
Solution: Convert IK input/output, ladder AUP, telemetry ring, and telemetry cursor descriptors to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve method-local views before reads/writes/scheduling, and release five owned descriptors after completing any outstanding IK job during teardown or DataVault replacement/loss.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because this is presentation IK was rejected; job consumes Vault-backed AUP and telemetry data and can race relocation if manager keeps pointer metadata. Owner-wide release was rejected in favor of exact descriptor release.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cheap slide/grip solve cadence; middle/high/ultra retain richer IK targets and telemetry without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays five generation checks when staging or reading IK views. dominant cost remains Burst IK solve; stale Vault handle metadata is removed from animation locomotion.
## Decision 042 - Tool haptics front/back lanes stop refreshing legacy handles
Problem: `ToolHapticsRuntime.cs` persisted front/back `VaultBufferHandle<HapticCommand>` descriptors and called `ResolveBuffer(ref handle)` before every haptic buffer access, keeping pointer-bearing metadata alive in manager.
Solution: Convert both lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<HapticCommand>`, cache active `IDataVault`, resolve local `NativeArray<HapticCommand>` views per haptic operation, and release old descriptors on DataVault loss/replacement or teardown.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `ReadOnlySpan` snapshots as only change was rejected because stale descriptor route would still exist before span is created. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact front/back descriptors are known.
Scalability potential: Low devices still compact and decay 16-command buffer; middle/high/ultra keep richer command blending and sinusoidal feedback without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation compare per front/back lane access. dominant haptic work remains bounded command compaction/merge; stale Vault metadata is removed from tool rumble.
## Decision 043 - Procedural bone blender schedules only generation-resolved views
Problem: `ProceduralBoneBlenderRuntime.cs` persisted eleven `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and used `.Resolve(vault)` in editor, CSV, mock rig, telemetry, GPU upload, and Burst scheduling paths. Disable/destroy and DataVault replacement cleared descriptors without releasing owned Vault lanes.
Solution: Convert all fauna procedural bone lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add shared resolve/acquire helper that uses `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, resolve `NativeArray<T>` views only inside active method/phase, and release exact descriptors after completing outstanding solver jobs on disable, destroy, or DataVault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy descriptors for editor-only routes was rejected because those same handles feed runtime solver and telemetry paths. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact buffer IDs are known and broader release would cross another owner boundary if future lanes share `SystemID.AnimationFauna`.
Scalability potential: Low devices still collapse update cadence through existing continuous `GlobalQualityWeight`; middle/high/ultra keep GPU matrix upload and richer procedural bone response without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays eleven generation compares when staging fauna solve and few compares on editor/telemetry reads. dominant cost remains Burst solve and GPU buffer copy; stale Vault metadata is removed from animation path.
## Decision 044 - Kinetic character animator removes descriptor and direct-view debt
Problem: `KineticCharacterAnimatorRuntime.cs` persisted twelve `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors, resolved them through `.Resolve(vault)`, and also fetched `PlayerKinematicState` / `VoxelSdfTexture3D` through direct `TryGetBuffer` calls. Teardown and DataVault replacement cleared descriptor fields without releasing Vault lanes.
Solution: Convert all locomotion animation lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add generation-checked owned and external resolve helpers, route player and SDF reads through method-local `TryGetGenerationHandle` + `TryResolveHandle`, and release exact owned descriptors after solver completion on disable, destroy, and DataVault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `TryGetBuffer` for external read-only lanes was rejected because read-only does not make stale aliases safe after relocation. Releasing all `SystemID.AnimationLocomotion` buffers was rejected because adjacent locomotion runtimes can share owner ID.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain existing continuous quality-weighted locomotion/SDF degradation; middle/high/ultra keep richer IK and GPU matrix output without persistent Vault views. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays twelve generation compares for owned staging and two local external descriptor resolves on player/SDF frames. dominant cost remains Burst locomotion/matrix work; stale Vault descriptors and direct external Vault views are removed from manager.
## Decision 045 - Laser cutter scalability read uses generation descriptor
Problem: `LaserCutterDodRuntime.cs` had one remaining `TryGetBufferHandle` route for `ShinobuScalabilityState`, leaving legacy descriptor path inside otherwise generation-descriptor tool runtime.
Solution: Replace quality-weight read with `TryGetGenerationHandle<ScalabilityStateDTO>` and `TryResolveHandle`, keeping resolved `NativeArray<ScalabilityStateDTO>` local to `ResolveGlobalQualityWeight()`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping old route because it is read-only was rejected; relocation still invalidates pointer-bearing handle metadata regardless of write intent.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra visuals continue to use same continuous quality scalar; only descriptor acquisition route changed.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 cost is one generation handle resolve on quality reads. It removes final legacy handle API hit in this runtime without changing cut math.
## Decision 046 - Tool kinematics editor facade stops using legacy handles
Problem: `ToolKinematicsTunerWindow.cs` cached seven `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and used `ResolveBuffer(ref handle)` / `.Resolve(vault)` while Play Mode editor tuning can observe and mutate live Vault lanes.
Solution: Convert editor descriptors to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve local editor views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, and release exactly editor-acquired descriptors when window closes or Vault reference changes.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating editor windows as harmless was rejected because they run against Play Mode memory and can hold stale descriptors across defrag/rebind events.
Scalability potential: Runtime scalability is unchanged; editor facade now observes same quality-weighted tool kinematics state without preserving pointer-bearing handles.
Hardware Impact: No player-frame cost. Editor draws pay generation checks while tuner window is open; stale Vault metadata is removed from facade.
## Decision 047 - Tool kinematics runtime drops legacy handles and ref-return API
Problem: `ToolKinematicsRuntime.cs` persisted fifteen `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors, resolved them through `ResolveBuffer(ref handle)` / `.Resolve(vault)`, and exposed unused public `ToolKinematicsVaultAccess` class that returned refs via `GetElementAsRef`.
Solution: Convert all runtime lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve method-local `NativeArray<T>` views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, release exact descriptors on disable/destroy or Vault rebind, and remove unused ref-return accessor class.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping ref-return accessor with generation handles was rejected because returning refs from transient views invites callers to keep byref access beyond safe execution phase. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact ToolKinematics buffer IDs are known.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous LOD hold and beam raymarch limits; middle/high/ultra keep richer tool beam/IK/spark output without persistent Vault descriptors. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays fifteen generation compares while staging tool jobs. dominant cost remains Burst raymarch/beam jobs; stale Vault descriptor metadata and public byref mutation routes are removed.
## Decision 048 - Tool durability removes false-positive legacy naming
Problem: `ToolDurabilitySystem.cs` already used `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` and `TryResolveHandle`, but its local helper was named `TryResolveBuffer`, which caused broad legacy Vault scans to surface false-positive ResolveBuffer-like route.
Solution: Rename helper and callers to `TryResolveDurabilityView` without changing allocation, BufferID, DTO, or job behavior.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving name was rejected because audit noise slows detection of real stale pointer routes in tools and animation.
Scalability potential: Runtime scalability is unchanged; durability still uses existing generation-descriptor state lanes.
Hardware Impact: No runtime change. benefit is audit precision: broad scans now separate safe generation views from forbidden legacy resolve calls.
## Decision 049 - Vocal warning manager stops storing Vault aliases
Problem: `VocalWarningSystem.cs` persisted six Vault-backed `NativeArray<T>` aliases and six legacy `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors for queue, warning state, and telemetry lanes. Vault relocation after boot could leave manager indexing stale array metadata.
Solution: Replace all six descriptors with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add phase-local `VwsVaultViews` value, resolve views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` inside queue mutation, slow tick, telemetry, and dump paths, and release exact descriptors during teardown/rebind.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping aliases because VWS has no Burst job was rejected; UAF risk is independent of job scheduling. `ReleaseOwnerBuffers` was rejected because exact BufferIDs are known and owner-wide teardown hides descriptor ownership mistakes.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same small priority queue and cooldown cadence; middle/high/ultra keep full warning telemetry and radio-degrade presentation. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays six generation compares on VWS mutation/slow paths. This is below clip submission and subtitle routing cost and removes stale Vault metadata from audio warning manager.
## Decision 050 - Native audio frame ring resolves buffers per operation
Problem: `NativeAudioFrameRingBuffer.cs` persisted Vault-backed `_frames` and `_sharedState` aliases plus two `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors. native output ring also exports raw pointers to audio bridge, so cached manager aliases were direct relocation hazard.
Solution: Replace both handles with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve local `RingVaultViews` value for buffer state, writes, clearing, shared metadata access, and native descriptor creation, and release exact frame/shared-state descriptors on dispose.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `_frames`/`_sharedState` because ring is internal was rejected; internal managers still survive across defrag. Owner-wide release was rejected because ring owns exactly two known BufferIDs.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain same bounded SPSC copy and overflow drop reporting; middle/high/ultra keep larger ring capacities and native bridge output without retaining stale managed-side Vault aliases.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation compares for ring state/write/descriptor operations. hot cost remains sample copy and native plugin handoff; stale manager-resident Vault aliases are removed.
## Decision 051 - Dynamic music resolves DSP buffers from generation views
Problem: `DynamicMusicGranularSynthesizer.cs` persisted Vault-backed arrays for DSP voices, scalars, tuning, output buffers, biquad, telemetry, CSV scratch, preset rules, grain bank, shared state, and scalability state. It also cached output pointers. bounded Vault relocation would invalidate those aliases while manager, editor facade, audio callback, or scheduled jobs still believed metadata was stable.
Solution: Replace all owned descriptors with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add method-local `DynamicMusicVaultViews` resolver, pass local views into editor/cold CSV/audio/job/telemetry paths, take raw pointers only immediately before job scheduling or file/native copy, and release exact owned descriptors on teardown. external scalability state is borrowed through `TryGetGenerationHandle` and resolved transiently.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached aliases because this is audio system was rejected; audio paths are relocation-sensitive and must not retain stale manager-side Vault metadata. Releasing by owner was rejected because synth owns fixed BufferID set and exact release exposes descriptor drift.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous density/cutoff/sample cadence collapse through `GlobalQualityWeight`; middle/high/ultra keep full granular voices, telemetry, and stinger richness. No binary hardware branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation checks at scheduling/cold/editor/audio-copy boundaries. hot DSP loop still runs from phase-local pointers inside Burst jobs; stale persistent aliases are removed without adding GC.
## Decision 052 - Adaptive stem mixer stops retaining Vault aliases
Problem: `AdaptiveStemAudioMixer.cs` persisted eleven Vault-backed arrays and eleven legacy `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors for stem state, commands, rules, mock signal rows, telemetry, CSV scratch, and scalability state. mixer also used binary low/high scalability fallback after signal ingress.
Solution: Replace owned descriptors with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, add method-local `AdaptiveStemVaultViews` resolver, resolve views before editor/tick/job/telemetry/CSV operations, borrow scalability state through `TryGetGenerationHandle`, release owned descriptors exactly, and map `HectonQualityTier` through `Smooth01` into continuous 0.1..1.0 fallback weight.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping aliases because mixer is presentation-only was rejected; presentation systems still schedule Burst jobs and can crash after relocation. Binary `LowMx350 ? 0.1f : 1f` was rejected because it creates hard quality discontinuity.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep slow update cadence and cheap crossfade; middle/high/ultra smoothly restore faster cadence and richer stem blending without branch pop.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation checks on mixer phase boundaries, not per sample. gain is removing stale Vault aliases from adaptive-stem job scheduling and telemetry paths.
## Decision 053 - Player critical renderer first removes pointer-bearing ownership
Problem: `PlayerCriticalProceduralAudioRenderer.cs` is last large audio file with broad Vault debt. It held 50 persistent `NativeArray<T>` aliases and acquired them through pointer-bearing `VaultBufferHandle<T>` plus `handle.Resolve`; teardown used owner-wide release.
Solution: First isolate ownership from pointer metadata: add 50 `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors, make central `ResolveVaultBuffer` helper use `GetGenerationHandle` plus `TryResolveHandle`, and replace owner-wide release with exact release of known descriptors after outstanding audio/SDF/composite jobs are completed.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting entire 11k-line renderer in one pass was rejected because producer thread, sonar jobs, VWS double buffer, and reverb state share lifetime constraints. Keeping `VaultBufferHandle<T>` until final pass was rejected because it leaves highest-risk pointer-bearing API in largest audio owner.
Scalability potential: Runtime audio quality behavior is unchanged in this slice. Low/middle/high/ultra renderer math and existing perceptual audio fakes remain stable while ownership metadata becomes generation-checked.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays no new sample-loop cost. Bind/release paths pay O(buffer-count) generation descriptor work; remaining work is phase-local view migration for persistent aliases.
## Decision 054 - Player critical low-risk rings move to phase-local views
Problem: After descriptor ownership was fixed, PlayerCritical still kept 50 persistent Vault aliases. smallest safe runtime slice was isolated VWS double-buffer lane plus granular/prologue telemetry and prologue command rings; these are bounded and do not require rewriting full producer DSP graph.
Solution: Remove five persistent `NativeArray<T>` fields and resolve VWS clip buffers, granular telemetry, prologue transition telemetry, and prologue transition command rings through generation handles at operation boundaries. Keep producer sample loops free of per-sample resolve calls.
Rejected Alternatives: Attempting to migrate all frame scratch/reverb/sonar/granular voice arrays in one patch was rejected because those arrays cross audio producer loop and scheduled sonar jobs. Deferring all aliases was rejected because isolated rings were easy to harden immediately.
Scalability potential: No visual/audio quality behavior changed. Low-tier and high-tier renderer fakes keep their existing cadence; postmortem and VWS lanes now survive relocation more predictably.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks on VWS submit/playback, prologue queue, and telemetry operations. No inner DSP loop resolve was introduced.
## Decision 055 - Player critical granular SOA resolves once per producer block
Problem: PlayerCritical still retained metallic grain bank and eight granular voice SOA buffers as long-lived `NativeArray<T>` fields. Those arrays are mutated in audio-rate code, so resolving them per sample would be correct but too expensive; keeping them as fields preserved stale-alias UAF risk.
Solution: Remove nine persistent aliases, add `GranularVoiceVaultViews`, resolve view once in `CanProduceAudioBlock`, pass it through `RenderHullStressBlock`, `RenderStructuralGranularVoices`, and `MixAndFilterBlock`, and update voice arm/trim/slot helpers to mutate local NativeArray descriptors copied from phase view.
Rejected Alternatives: whole-renderer DSP view was deferred because sonar/reverb/frame scratch buffers cross scheduled jobs and require separate dependency pass. Per-voice/per-sample resolution was rejected because it burns audio-thread cycles without improving safety over block-scoped view.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain cheap granular voice budgets and linear envelopes; middle/high/ultra still unlock denser voice counts and interpolation through existing continuous tuning. migration does not add hardware binary branch.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays nine generation validations once per produced block. hot sample loop reuses local NativeArray descriptors and keeps existing O(active voices) granular fake instead of heavier structural simulation.
## Decision 056 - Player critical binaural and low-pass state resolves once per producer block
Problem: Binaural ITD delay, ear-shadow history, and final listener low-pass histories remained as long-lived `NativeArray<T>` fields. They are small, but they are mutated every producer block and are still invalid after Vault relocation.
Solution: Remove six aliases, add `BinauralFilterVaultViews`, resolve it once in `CanProduceAudioBlock`, pass it by ref through `MixAndFilterBlock` and `ApplyBinauralSpatializationBlock`, and resolve same view in `ClearLowPassState` for cold reset.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping histories as fields because they are tiny was rejected; UAF risk is independent of byte count. Resolving inside `SampleBinauralDelay` or `ApplyBinauralShadowEar` was rejected because those functions execute per sample/ear and would add avoidable validation branches.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous binaural mix, underwater shadow cutoff, narcosis chorus, and abyssal low-pass curves stay unchanged from low through ultra. change is pointer-lifetime only.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays six generation validations per produced block. per-sample binaural and low-pass loops use local descriptors and keep their existing arithmetic profile.
## Decision 057 - Player critical reverb state resolves once per producer block
Problem: Sabine reverb, cave convolution, and interior FDN delay buffers remained as persistent `NativeArray<T>` fields. These are among larger PlayerCritical buffers and are mutated in hot sample loops, so stale aliases can crash and per-sample resolution would be too expensive.
Solution: Remove four aliases, add `ReverbVaultViews`, resolve view once in `CanProduceAudioBlock`, pass local descriptors through Sabine comb, cave convolution, and interior FDN helpers, and resolve same generation view for cold impulse bake and reset clears.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping reverb fields because they are audio-private was rejected; Vault relocation can invalidate audio-private views exactly like cross-domain views. Resolving inside each comb/convolution tap was rejected because it would multiply handle validation by sample count and tap count.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous reverb DSP tier selection, wet mix, openness, and acoustic density curves remain unchanged. Low devices still fall back to cheaper Unity/profile-only paths; high/ultra keep native Sabine/convolution richness.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays four generation validations per produced block. Hot reverb loops keep local NativeArray descriptors and avoid new branches inside comb, convolution, and FDN tap math.
## Decision 058 - Player critical transient delay lines resolve once per producer block
Problem: Impact clang and thruster comb delay lines remained as persistent `NativeArray<T>` fields. Both are small compared with reverb, but they are audio-rate mutable delay lines and can become stale after Vault relocation.
Solution: Remove two aliases, add `TransientDelayVaultViews`, resolve it once in `CanProduceAudioBlock`, pass it through impact event consumption, hull stress rendering, and thruster rendering, and clear it through method-local view during reset.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping these fields until frame-scratch pass was rejected because they are isolated and cheap to harden now. Resolving in `RenderImpactClangSampleInternal` or each thruster comb iteration was rejected because it would add per-sample validation.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous thruster pressure/cavitation and impact metallic fakes stay unchanged across low/mid/high/ultra. migration changes lifetime only.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations per produced block. Hot Karplus/comb loops use local NativeArray descriptors.
## Decision 059 - Player critical frame scratch resolves once per producer block
Problem: Hull, sonar, impact echo, thruster, heartbeat, bubble, mix, and stereo scratch buffers were still manager-held `NativeArray<T>` aliases. These buffers are re-used every audio block, so stale aliases would survive Vault relocation and crash in producer path.
Solution: Remove nine scratch aliases, add `FrameScratchVaultViews`, resolve view once in `CanProduceAudioBlock`, and pass it by ref into render, mix, and binaural stages. Cold reset and prologue probe paths resolve same view only for duration of their clear/probe operation.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping scratch fields because they are short-lived data was rejected; alias lifetime was manager lifetime, not scratch semantic lifetime. Resolving inside each render function was rejected where producer already has block view.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous quality curves for granular FM, reverb tier, binaural blend, and bubble intensity remain unchanged. Low devices pay one block-level validation set and keep same cheap DSP fakes; high/ultra keep dense procedural output.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays nine generation validations per produced block. Hot sample loops use local descriptors and retain prior arithmetic profile.
## Decision 060 - Player critical sonar storage is split into phase-local Vault views
Problem: remaining sonar buffers were highest UAF risk: publish taps, worker taps, DSP echo delay/filter state, SDF hit cache, and composite coalescing scratch were all persistent `NativeArray<T>` fields. Some are touched from read accessors, some from audio producer blocks, and some from scheduled jobs.
Solution: Remove all 15 sonar aliases and split resolution into `SonarTapVaultViews`, `SonarDspVaultViews`, and `SonarSpatialVaultViews`. UI read accessors resolve only tap buffers, audio DSP resolves tap+DSP state once per block, and SDF/composite phases resolve spatial buffers at schedule/publish boundaries. editor smoke test now verifies handle/view usage instead of stale fields.
Rejected Alternatives: single `PlayerCriticalAudioVaultViews` blob was rejected because `TryGetCockpitSonarEchoTaps` must stay pure read accessor and must not over-resolve DSP or SDF buffers. Per-tap generation resolution was rejected because it would multiply validation by echo count inside sonar publish loop.
Scalability potential: Sonar keeps existing capped echo tap fake and continuous SDF probe budget. Low devices use fewer probes/ghost taps through existing quality weights; high/ultra can keep richer SDF returns without changing authority or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes all sonar manager-held native aliases. Validation cost is bounded to phase entry: four checks for tap views, six for DSP views, five for spatial views. Delay/filter loops use local descriptors.
## Decision 061 - Vocal warning pending queue is collapsed into Vault priority queue
Problem: `VocalWarningSystem.cs` still owned `_pendingWarningIds` as private `NativeQueue<byte>` allocated with `Allocator.Persistent`. It was tiny, but it was still manager-owned native allocation outside `GlobalDataVault`, and it duplicated Vault-backed `AudioVocalWarningQueue` fact.
Solution: Remove private `NativeQueue<byte>`, `_pendingNativeCount`, prewarm, drain, sentinel registration, and dispose path. `TryQueueWarning` now resolves `VwsVaultViews` once, writes cooldown/severity/source state, and inserts warning id directly into Vault-owned bounded priority queue via `InsertOrPromote`.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing queue with another Vault staging buffer was rejected because bounded priority queue already handles duplicate suppression, capacity, and priority replacement. Keeping staging queue because it is only 16 bytes was rejected because UAF and ownership violations are independent of capacity.
Scalability potential: Low devices skip extra staging dequeue pass on slow tick. Middle/high/ultra keep same warning priority behavior, telemetry ring, and radio-degrade presentation without changing DTO layout or authority route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes one persistent native allocation and one `TryDequeue` drain loop per slow tick. `TryQueueWarning` already paid six generation checks for VWS state; direct insert reuses same resolved view and does not add sample-loop or job-loop cost.
## Decision 062 - Spectrum sonar discovery and telemetry views move to Vault descriptors
Problem: `SpectrumSystem.cs` owned `_aupDiscoveryGrid` and `_activeSonarGeoTelemetryRing` as local persistent `NativeArray<T>` fields, manually allocated and registered with `NativeMemorySentinel`. editor smoke test also asserted that old ownership model, making unsafe route self-reinforcing.
Solution: Replace both fields with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors. AUP discovery grid uses BufferID `71030`; active-sonar telemetry ring uses BufferID `71031`. `TryGetAupDiscoveryGrid`, reveal stamping, telemetry writes, and dump code resolve local views from cached `IDataVault` and release exact descriptors on destroy.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping grid local because it is visor presentation was rejected; sonar reveal memory is read by UI/audio-facing systems and must survive Vault relocation without cached aliases. Resolving grid once per stamped cell was rejected because octant shell fake stamps nine cells and only needs one phase-local resolve.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cheap octant-shell discovery fake and 300-frame blackbox cadence. Middle/high/ultra can retain richer sonar shader presentation because CPU path still avoids full flood-fill or physics ray loops.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes two local persistent NativeArray allocation/disposal routes. Sonar reveal pays one generation validation per pulse shell, then writes up to nine grid cells through local descriptor.
## Decision 063 - Topographical sonar stops persisting pointer-bearing Vault handles
Problem: `TopographicalSonarSynthesizer.cs` persisted eleven legacy `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors for point cloud rows, hit masks, counters, mock SDF/material payloads, 300-frame telemetry, CSV scratch, indirect args, and shader globals. Even without explicit private `NativeArray<T>` fields, legacy descriptors carried pointer metadata and used `handle.Resolve`, so Vault relocation could leave stale lease path in UI sonar system.
Solution: Replace all eleven descriptors with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, cache `IDataVault` once through `ResolveDataVaultCold`, resolve method-local views with `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, and release each exact descriptor during teardown after outstanding scan/fade job fences complete. shutdown path now decrements Vault references instead of only defaulting local handles.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because system is visual-only was rejected; visual sonar still schedules Burst jobs and uploads GPU buffers from Vault data. Calling `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` at every resolve site was rejected because registry is cold identity and dependency injection only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous ray-count collapse, mock SDF fake, and GPU point rendering. Middle/high/ultra keep denser point clouds, material LUT color, indirect draw args, and shader globals without changing ownership or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks at scan/fade/upload/telemetry phase boundaries. Per-ray `SampleTopographicalSonarJob` and per-point fade loops use local `NativeArray<T>` descriptors and do not revalidate handles inside hot loop.
## Decision 064 - PDA frequency tuning resolves Vault waves through generation descriptors
Problem: `PDADecryptionSpectrogramPanel.cs` persisted six legacy `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and one shared helper used `handle.Resolve(vault)` for wave rows, GPU segments, stage targets, and 300-frame telemetry ring. It also cleared descriptors on teardown instead of releasing Vault references.
Solution: Convert six descriptors to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, make shared helper validate existing handles through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, reacquire descriptors through `GetGenerationHandle<T>` when absent or undersized, and release exact descriptors on teardown/DataVault replacement after completing scheduled wave job.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing inside resolve helper after transient resolve failure was rejected because compaction fence or temporary Vault unavailability must not decrement ownership from hot resolve path. Keeping old helper was rejected because `handle.Resolve` can use stale pointer metadata.
Scalability potential: Low devices continue to collapse spectrogram point count through continuous `GlobalQualityWeight` and VRAM clamp. Middle/high/ultra keep denser wave segments, GPU tube rendering, and telemetry without changing minigame truth route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays bounded generation checks at phase entry. Burst wave generation/error jobs still receive local `NativeSlice<T>` views and do not validate per point.
## Decision 065 - Babel subtitle runtime stops retaining legacy Vault descriptors
Problem: `BabelSubtitleSyncRuntime.cs` persisted two static `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and resolved subtitle cue/telemetry buffers through `handle.Resolve`. static runtime survives scene churn and can keep pointer-bearing metadata alive across Vault relocation or DataVault replacement.
Solution: Replace both descriptors with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve cue and telemetry buffers through cached `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, reacquire with `GetGenerationHandle<T>` during cold initialization, and release BufferIDs `15070550` and `15070551` on subsystem reset or DataVault hot-swap after fencing any active cue evaluation job.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handle because runtime already used method-local `NativeArray<T>` values was rejected; persistent descriptor itself still carried pointer metadata. Releasing from ordinary read helpers was rejected because transient compaction fence must not mutate ownership from read accessor.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous subtitle dirty budget collapse through `ResolveCanvasDirtyBudget`. Middle/high/ultra keep same visual-only cue flow and 300-frame telemetry without changing authority, DTO layout, or save identity.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations at cue/telemetry phase entry. Burst cue evaluation job still receives local pointer after fresh resolve and performs no per-cue descriptor lookup.
## Decision 066 - CharBufferPool Babel arena removes latest-vault and legacy descriptor routes
Problem: `CharBufferPool.cs` persisted static `VaultBufferHandle<char>` for Babel arena and resolved it through `handle.Resolve`. It also used `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated()` as fallback, which is bootstrap/editor/diagnostic/crash-only route and should not be UI formatting dependency.
Solution: Replace Babel arena handle with `VaultGenerationHandle<char>`, resolve method-local `NativeArray<char>` views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, acquire with `GetGenerationHandle<char>`, release descriptor on subsystem reset, and use only `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` for cold Vault injection. When no Vault exists, existing managed TMP bridge arrays remain fallback.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing on every resolve failure was rejected because compaction fences and temporary Vault unavailability must not mutate ownership from read path. Keeping `TryGetLatestCreated()` was rejected because it hides implicit global heap/diagnostic dependency in UI helper.
Scalability potential: Low devices can skip native arena and use fixed TMP bridge arrays when Vault is unavailable. Middle/high/ultra retain Vault-backed Babel arena without changing text capacity, save identity, or localization authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation when Babel span or native-to-TMP copy uses native arena. fallback path avoids Vault lookup churn and uses preallocated bridge arrays already owned by pool.
## Decision 067 - PDA shell borrows glitch glyph table instead of owning it
Problem: `PDAShellChrome.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<byte>` and used `ResolvePointer` against `DiegeticGlitchSurgeonRuntime.GlitchTableBufferIdRaw`. file also allocated shared table through `GetBufferHandle` and could fall back to `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated()`, making PDA chrome component implicit owner of shared glitch glyph fact.
Solution: Replace field with `VaultGenerationHandle<byte>`, borrow existing descriptor with `IDataVault.TryGetGenerationHandle`, resolve method-local `NativeArray<byte>` views through `TryResolveHandle`, and derive raw byte pointer only for immediate `GlitchEncoder` call. On invalid/missing table, fall back to table-free glitch encoder and clear borrowed descriptor.
Rejected Alternatives: `GetGenerationHandle<byte>` was rejected because it can create shared glyph table from non-owner and then force release ambiguity. Releasing on disable was rejected because PDA shell is now borrower, not owner. Keeping `TryGetLatestCreated()` was rejected because it is crash/diagnostic bootstrap-only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep table-free glitch encoder path when shared table is absent. Middle/high/ultra use richer glyph substitution table when owner has published it, without changing text layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation only when stress-reactive strings need table. no-table fallback avoids Vault allocation and keeps existing fixed scratch buffer path.
## Decision 068 - UberNoir telemetry ring uses generation descriptors only
Problem: `HectonUberNoirRuntimeBridge.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<UberNoirShaderTelemetryEntry>` for shader feature blackbox and called `.Resolve(vault)` in push/dump paths. bridge did not persist `NativeArray<T>`, but legacy handle itself still carried pointer metadata across Vault relocation.
Solution: Replace field with `VaultGenerationHandle<UberNoirShaderTelemetryEntry>`, resolve method-local views with `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, reacquire existing `ShaderFeatureTelemetryRing` through `TryGetGenerationHandle`, allocate only when missing and allocation is unlocked, and release owner-local descriptor on disable/destroy/DataVault replacement. Compaction-fence paths clear only local metadata and fail closed.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handle because ring is graphics-only was rejected; blackbox telemetry is persistent Vault fact and must be relocatable. Releasing from transient resolve failure was rejected because maintenance fences must not decrement ownership. Adding private telemetry array fallback was rejected because it would create second proof artifact.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous UberNoir feature collapse through `GlobalQualityWeight`, stress shedding, and shader feature masks. Middle/high/ultra keep same visual-overkill feature gating while telemetry ring remains generation-safe.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one bounded generation validation per telemetry push/dump phase. ring write/copy loop still uses local `NativeArray<T>` descriptor and does not revalidate per field.
## Decision 069 - Docking spline service stops exporting cached Vault pointers
Problem: `DockingAutopilotService.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<ActiveSplineData>`, used `ResolvePointer`, and read `_activeSplineHandle.ptr` directly in service methods. These methods are called by vehicle automation code across frames, so Vault relocation could leave docking slot reads/writes pointed at dead memory.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<ActiveSplineData>` plus cached row count, resolve method-local `NativeArray<ActiveSplineData>` views at each service operation boundary, and remove manager helper that returned `ActiveSplineData*`. Existing buffer recovery uses `TryGetGenerationHandle`; owner-local creation uses `GetGenerationHandle` only when allocation is unlocked. Disable/shutdown/DataVault replacement release descriptor through owning Vault.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointers for slot scans because buffer is small was rejected; pointer lifetime safety is independent of capacity. Adding private active-spline mirror was rejected because docking truth would split into two owners. Reacquiring via `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` inside each service method was rejected because registry access is cold DI path only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same bounded 64-slot default and cubic Dear Lie docking curve. Middle/high/ultra can raise serialized capacity up to 256 without changing DTO layout, authority route, or slot semantics.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per acquire/write/read/evaluate/release call. O(n) slot scans still operate on local `NativeArray<T>` descriptor and do not validate handle per slot.
## Decision 070 - Material decay blackbox ring stops using legacy handle resolution
Problem: `MaterialDecayRuntime.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<MaterialDecayState>` and used `.Resolve(_dataVault)` for VFX blackbox ring. runtime is visual, but ring is still 300-frame proof artifact and stale pointer metadata can fault after Vault compaction.
Solution: Replace persisted descriptor with `VaultGenerationHandle<MaterialDecayState>`, resolve method-local blackbox views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, recover existing buffers with `TryGetGenerationHandle`, allocate owner-local storage only when Vault is unlocked, and release descriptor on disable/destroy/DataVault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handle because telemetry is VFX-only was rejected; proof artifacts must be relocatable exactly like gameplay buffers. Releasing on compaction-fence failure was rejected because maintenance phases must not mutate ownership. Adding managed/native fallback ring was rejected because it would create second blackbox authority.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing shader-scalar rust/wetness/blood fake and low-tier flag. Middle/high/ultra keep richer material presentation through same global shader uniforms without changing DTO layout or signal ownership.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one bounded generation validation per blackbox push/dump phase. material shader path and rust atlas generation are unchanged.
Problem: `OrbitalRelativityDirector.cs` retained both `VaultBufferHandle<OrbitalTelemetryEntry>` and persistent `NativeArray<OrbitalTelemetryEntry>` telemetry ring. prologue director can span scene transitions and DataVault replacement, so compaction or hot-swap could leave stored ring view pointing at relocated memory.
Solution: Delete persistent `NativeArray` field, store only `VaultGenerationHandle<OrbitalTelemetryEntry>`, resolve method-local ring through cached `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` immediately before record/dump, and release descriptor on dispose, runtime-authority release, or DataVault replacement. Resolve failures during compaction only clear local descriptor.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping ring view because telemetry is low frequency was rejected; stale alias faults regardless of write cadence. Adding local fallback ring was rejected because it creates second blackbox truth outside Vault.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per telemetry record/dump phase. 300-entry dump loop uses local descriptor and does not revalidate per entry.
Problem: `FoveatedRenderCommander.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<FoveatedRenderTelemetryEntry>` and resolved raw `FoveatedRenderTelemetryEntry*` through `ResolvePointer`. commander is singleton-style VR graphics policy owner, so stale telemetry pointers can survive across XR display sampling, UI suppression passes, DataVault replacement, or Vault compaction fences.
Solution: Replace field with `VaultGenerationHandle<FoveatedRenderTelemetryEntry>`, resolve method-local `NativeArray<FoveatedRenderTelemetryEntry>` views through cached `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, stamp entries with `handle.Generation`, and release descriptor on disable, dispose, or DataVault replacement. class no longer needs unsafe context.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `ResolvePointer` because ring is graphics telemetry was rejected; blackbox proof artifacts must be relocatable. Calling `TryGetBufferGeneration` was rejected because it adds second lookup for value already validated in generation descriptor.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per telemetry write/dump phase. XR display enumeration and policy application costs are unchanged; dump loop uses local NativeArray descriptor.
Problem: `HullDentShaderController.cs` and `RepairTool.cs` both used legacy `VaultBufferHandle<float4>` routes for `BufferID.HullDents`. Both could allocate or resolve through pointer-bearing handles, and naive generation migration would let borrower release another owner's shared visual dent lane.
Solution: Make `HullDentShaderController` allocator/owner for `BufferID.HullDents=(BufferID)76`, because it owns shader upload and visual dent presentation. `RepairTool` now borrows descriptor with `TryGetGenerationHandle` and mutates only after phase-local `TryResolveHandle`. Owner bits gate `ReleaseBuffer`, so descriptors recovered through `TryGetGenerationHandle` are clear-only. `RepairToolBlackBox=(BufferID)340` separately uses owned generation descriptor and local NativeArray record/dump views.
Rejected Alternatives: Allowing `RepairTool` to call `GetGenerationHandle` for `HullDents` was rejected because it creates refcount ambiguity for shared visual fact. Keeping raw blackbox pointers was rejected because blackbox proof artifacts are not exempt from relocation safety. Moving capacity/packing into new shared contract was deferred to avoid cross-domain contract edit; both sides already use capacity 16.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per hull dent sync/flush/repair phase and one validation per repair blackbox write/dump. Shader upload remains fixed 16-vector global array; no CPU mesh deformation is introduced.
Problem: `CameraJuiceSystem.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<CameraJuiceTelemetryEntry>` and resolved 300-frame telemetry ring through `handle.Resolve(_dataVault)`. runtime is camera presentation, but it is singleton-style and participates in hot-swap/service rebinding, so stale descriptor can survive compaction or DataVault replacement.
Solution: Replace field with `VaultGenerationHandle<CameraJuiceTelemetryEntry>`, resolve method-local `NativeArray<CameraJuiceTelemetryEntry>` views through cached `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, and gate `ReleaseBuffer` with `_ownsCameraJuiceTelemetryBuffer`. Recovered descriptors from `TryGetGenerationHandle` are borrowed and clear-only; descriptors acquired with `GetGenerationHandle` are released on disable, destroy, or DataVault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `VaultBufferHandle<T>.Resolve` because telemetry is visual-only was rejected; blackbox proof artifacts must remain relocatable. Unconditional release of recovered descriptor was rejected because it can decrement another owner's Vault reference. Changing camera-shake math or DTO layout was rejected because this pass is pointer safety, not presentation redesign.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per telemetry record/dump phase. 300-entry dump loop uses local `NativeArray<T>` descriptor and does not validate per entry.
Problem: `HectonPlayerMovement.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<CinematicFocusTelemetryEntry>` and used `handle.Resolve(_dataVault)` for cinematic focus blackbox. Player movement is long-lived, registry-rebound, origin-shift aware, and fault-dump capable; retaining pointer-bearing descriptor keeps exact stale-alias failure class open in player-critical runtime.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<CinematicFocusTelemetryEntry>`, resolve method-local `NativeArray<CinematicFocusTelemetryEntry>` views through cached `_dataVault.TryResolveHandle`, and gate release with `_ownsCinematicFocusBlackBox`. `TryGetGenerationHandle` recovery is borrowed and clear-only; `GetGenerationHandle` acquisition is released on teardown or DataVault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting whole player kinematics native-state wrapper was rejected as larger owner lane with separate buffers. Keeping legacy blackbox handle because it had no persistent `NativeArray<T>` field was rejected because descriptor itself still carried stale pointer metadata. Changing cinematic focus DTO or dump format was rejected because ABI is already explicit 96 bytes.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per focus sample/dump phase. 300-entry dump loop stays sequential over local `NativeArray<T>` view and does not validate per row.
Problem: `SuitHUDV4CanvasOverlay.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<byte>`, allocated `DiegeticGlitchSurgeonRuntime.GlitchTableBufferIdRaw=70901` through `GetBufferHandle`, fell back to `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated()`, and resolved raw glyph-table pointer. That made HUD overlay implicit allocator/writer for shared UI glyph fact owned by `DiegeticGlitchSurgeonRuntime`.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<byte>`, borrow with `IDataVault.TryGetGenerationHandle`, validate with `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, and derive `byte*` only from freshly resolved method-local `NativeArray<byte>` for immediate `GlitchEncoder` use. Lifecycle teardown and DataVault replacement clear only borrowed descriptor. Invalid, missing, or stale tables fail closed into existing table-free decay encoder.
Rejected Alternatives: Allocating or initializing shared glyph table from HUD was rejected because it splits ownership and release authority. `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated()` was rejected as bootstrap/editor/crash-only fallback. Caching derived `byte*` was rejected because Vault relocation can invalidate native addresses between phases.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation only when corrupted HUD text needs shared table. No Vault allocation, no managed allocation, no persisted native alias, and no borrower-side table copy remain.
