Problem: `VehicleDockingModule.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<DockTelemetryEntry>` and `VaultBufferHandle<int>`, resolved both with `ResolvePointer`, and returned `DockTelemetryEntry*` / `int*` to record and dump helpers. module is pooled and multi-instance, so cached pointer-bearing descriptors can survive DataVault replacement, compaction fences, and dock lifecycle churn.
Solution: Replace both persisted descriptors with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, resolve method-local `NativeArray<DockTelemetryEntry>` and `NativeArray<int>` views through cached `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, and make telemetry record/dump write through those local views only. `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` is now read by cold cache helper instead of hot resolve path.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing `VehicleDockingTelemetryRing` or cursor from `OnDisable` was rejected because this is shared `SystemID.VehiclesPhysics` blackbox lane and `GetGenerationHandle` does not provide per-module refcount increment when BufferID already exists. Borrow-only clear preserves old process-lifetime ownership while eliminating stale pointers. private module telemetry ring was rejected because it would create second blackbox proof artifact.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations per telemetry write/dump phase. dump loop uses one local ring descriptor and one local cursor descriptor; no raw pointer is retained between phases.
Problem: `LootMagnetSystem.cs` did not persist legacy handles, but its generic `TryResolveVaultView<T>` still created `VaultBufferHandle<T>` values, called `TryGetBufferHandle`, and resolved through `.Resolve(vault)`. Cleanup helpers also fell back to `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` when cached `_vault` was null.
Solution: Replace helper with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, `GetGenerationHandle<T>` for owner allocation phases, `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>` for read-existing phases, and `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` for method-local `NativeArray<T>` views. Cleanup and unlock paths now use cached `_vault` only; dependency refresh remains cold registry route.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving local legacy descriptors because they are not fields was rejected; migration goal is to eliminate pointer-bearing API use, not just persistent storage. Adding persistent per-lane handles was rejected because this scheduler already has clean method-local view acquisition and does not need more long-lived state.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays bounded generation validation when lane views are acquired. per-entity pull, commit, and cleanup loops still operate over local `NativeArray<T>` views and do not revalidate handles per item.
Problem: `FaunaBrain.cs` persisted two `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors for one-row corpse-sink kinematic input/output buffers and resolved them through `.Resolve(vault)`. helper also polled `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` from schedule/complete boundary, which is active runtime work, not cold injection.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<CorpseSinkKinematicInput>` and `VaultGenerationHandle<CorpseSinkKinematicOutput>`, cache `_corpseSinkVault` during lifecycle/spawn, and resolve method-local input/output views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Teardown completes any outstanding job and clears descriptors only.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing one-row fauna kinematic buffers from pooled brain was rejected because BufferIDs are shared and current Vault API does not expose per-fauna refcount ownership for existing buffers. Creating private NativeArrays was rejected because corpse-sink job data is rollback/blackbox-adjacent and must remain Vault-backed.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations at corpse-sink schedule/complete boundaries. Burst job receives method-local one-element NativeArray views and does not retain Vault alias after scheduling.
Problem: `HectonVisorFluidDistortionFeature.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<VisorRefractionTelemetryEntry>`, used `ResolvePointer`, compared `GenerationID` against `TryGetBufferGeneration`, and polled `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` from render-pass blackbox path. SRP features are long-lived renderer assets, so cached pointer metadata can survive DataVault replacement or compaction and fault during telemetry write or dump.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<VisorRefractionTelemetryEntry>`, cold-bind `_dataVault` from lifecycle/hot-swap routes, resolve method-local `NativeArray<VisorRefractionTelemetryEntry>` views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`, and gate release with `_blackBoxHandleOwned` plus current generation validation. ring writer and dump loop no longer require unsafe context.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointer because buffer is render telemetry was rejected; blackbox proof artifacts must be relocatable. Polling `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` from `TryEnsureBlackBoxLease` was rejected because registry is cold DI only. Releasing every recovered descriptor was rejected because renderer assets can bind to buffer allocated by another owner.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation at blackbox frame-write/dump entry. 300-row dump uses local `NativeArray<T>` descriptor and does not revalidate per row; visual shader path is unchanged.
Problem: `ScreenSpaceLightShaftRuntime.cs` persisted three `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and resolved them through `.Resolve(vault)` after taking write locks. lock order protected concurrent writers, but descriptor still carried stale pointer metadata across DataVault replacement or compaction.
Solution: Replace top contribution, history contribution, and telemetry descriptors with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, cold-bind `_dataVault` through lifecycle/hot-swap routes, and resolve method-local `NativeArray<T>` views with `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` only after all three buffers are locked. Existing lanes are borrowed; newly acquired descriptors are release-gated by current generation.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `.Resolve(vault)` because locks were already present was rejected; locks do not repair stale pointer descriptor. Polling `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` from `EnsureBuffers` was rejected because late-frame VFX work is hot path. Removing Vault locks was rejected because this pass changes descriptor safety, not writer synchronization.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays three generation validations after existing lock triplet. max source tracker remains fixed at three 64-byte entries, so contribution sort/history costs stay bounded and cache-local.
Problem: `ScannableTarget.cs` already used `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, but it cached static `NativeArray<AbsoluteUniversePosition>` and `NativeArray<uint>` views, then separately polled `TryGetBufferGeneration` to decide whether cached views were current. If Vault relocates, cached view can still point at dead native memory before separate generation check protects all call sites.
Solution: Delete static `NativeArray<T>` view cache and separate generation cache. Every lore entity read/write phase resolves method-local AUP/hash views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` using stored generation descriptors.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached views for 1024-slot scanner speed was rejected because descriptor validation is cheaper than crash and sync loop remains bounded. Keeping `TryGetBufferGeneration` was rejected because it creates second route for same fact.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations when lore buffers are read or written. owner sync loop still walks fixed array and does not validate per slot.
Problem: `PlayerKinematicsRuntime.VaultBufferBinding<T>` stored `VaultBufferHandle<T>` and used `GetBufferHandle<T>` / `Handle.Resolve(dataVault)`. helper backs fifteen player kinematics SOA lanes, so pointer-bearing descriptor risk was multiplied across body state, hand probes, telemetry, and SDF squeeze results.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, reuse existing handles through `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>` when valid, allocate with `GetGenerationHandle<T>` only when needed, and resolve every view through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. helper still returns method-local `NativeArray<T>` views to existing jobs and call sites.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting all player kinematics call sites to explicit view structs was rejected for this pass because generic helper already centralizes dangerous descriptor. Adding unconditional release was rejected because previous helper only cleared views and ownership/refcount changes across fifteen lanes need separate teardown audit.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation validation when binding view is read, replacing prior legacy resolve cost. There is no additional per-element validation inside player body or telemetry loops.
Problem: `HazardZoneManager.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<HazardExposureJobResult>` and resolved it through `.Resolve(vault)` after polling `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` inside result preparation route. manager is long-lived gameplay service and its one-row result buffer can cross DataVault replacement or compaction boundaries while hazard job schedule/consume loop keeps running.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<HazardExposureJobResult>`, cold-bind `_dataVault` during lifecycle setup, register `GlobalRegistry` hot-swap listener, and resolve method-local `NativeArray<HazardExposureJobResult>` views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Allocation-capable `GetGenerationHandle` is limited to cold setup or replacement recovery; hot schedule/consume calls use cached `_dataVault` and existing generation descriptors.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `.Resolve(vault)` because result has one row was rejected; stale pointer descriptors are element-count agnostic. Unconditional `ReleaseBuffer` on teardown was rejected because current hazard job path does not hold Vault write lock and disabled manager can still have active scheduled writer. Moving all hazard registry NativeArrays into Vault was rejected for this bounded pass because they are Sentinel-registered owner-local scratch and require separate route card.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation at schedule/consume boundaries and removes one service-locator lookup from each result preparation. Burst job still writes single 128-byte result row and does not validate per hazard volume.
Problem: `PdaH8lrLoreStore.cs` used `VaultGenerationHandle<byte>` for H8LR mirror, but after cold file copy it stored `_basePointer` from `NativeArrayUnsafeUtility.GetUnsafeReadOnlyPtr(vaultMirror)` and later guarded it with `TryGetBufferGeneration`. matching generation check cannot repair native address that was cached before Vault relocation or DataVault replacement.
Solution: Keep `_basePointer` persistent only for memory-mapped-file path. For Vault-backed lore, validation still uses byte pointer during cold open, then clears `_basePointer`; every lookup resolves `_vaultMirrorHandle` through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` and derives method-local byte pointer from returned `NativeArray<byte>`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `_basePointer` because lore records are read-only was rejected; read-only stale pointers still fault. Replacing MMF with Vault-only storage was rejected because standalone/editor MMF is separate cold file path and not stale Vault alias. Copying each lore record into managed string was rejected because PDA text streaming must remain allocation-free.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per H8LR lookup before B-tree scan. No per-record validation is added inside B-tree walk, and no managed allocation is introduced.
Problem: `ArchitectEyeVisualizer.cs` built hot-entity labels and trails from `TryGetBuffer<VaultHotEntityData>` while separately polling `TryGetBufferGeneration` for display label. visual path split one Vault fact into two lookup routes.
Solution: Add `TryResolveHotEntityData`, which borrows `VaultHotEntityData` generation descriptor with `TryGetGenerationHandle`, resolves local view with `TryResolveHandle`, and returns `handle.Generation` for label.
Rejected Alternatives: Patching only generation label was rejected because adjacent hot-entity reads would still use legacy `TryGetBuffer<T>` route. Persisting diagnostic view was rejected because Architect Eye is visual consumer, not Vault owner.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per visual build phase. Entity label, sector-map, trail, and fallback probe loops use local view and do not revalidate per row.
Problem: `PDAEncyclopediaStreamer.cs` had already moved its lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, but it cached `PdaVaultViews` struct containing persistent `NativeArray<T>` views for ten buffers and guarded those views with `TryGetBufferGeneration`. If Vault relocates, cached `NativeArray<T>` may carry old native address even if later metadata checks detect churn.
Solution: Delete `PdaVaultViews`, `_vaultViewsCached`, generation-poll helper, and synthetic `ConvertExistingDataToNativeArray` wrapper. `ResolveVaultBuffer` now returns actual `NativeArray<T>` from `_vault.TryResolveHandle`; `GetVaultElementRef` derives transient pointer from that phase-local view only.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached views because PDA UI is low frequency was rejected; stale native aliases are cadence-independent. Rebuilding PDA stream path around managed strings was rejected because it violates zero-GC text streaming contract. Adding second local mirror was rejected because localization/lore truth must stay in Vault/Babel/H8LR routes.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation descriptor validation at each PDA lane access boundary. UTF-8 decode, metadata probe, and telemetry copy loops operate on resolved local view and do not validate per byte or per character.
Problem: `ShinobuRespawnReconciliationRuntime.cs` used `TryGetBufferGeneration` inside `IsVaultGenerationCurrent`, creating separate metadata route for handles that are otherwise used through `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` and `TryResolveHandle`.
Solution: Replace metadata generation poll with `TryResolveVaultBuffer(vault, in handle, out NativeArray<T> buffer)` and require `buffer.IsCreated`. Owner checks and required-length checks remain in existing wrapper methods.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping metadata poll because it is cheap was rejected; cheap duplicate facts still violate one-route rule. Removing generation-current helper entirely was rejected because respawn reconciliation has both owned and borrowed physiology/player kinematic descriptors and still needs explicit cold/hot fence.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation descriptor validation per current-handle gate. No per-row validation is added to med-bay, telemetry, CSV, physiology, or kinematic loops.
Problem: `LSystemGenomeLabWindow.cs` used `TryGetBufferHandle(BufferID.FloraGenomeDtos, out VaultBufferHandle<FloraGenomeDTO>)` and `handle.Resolve(vault)` in editor facade. Editor windows can remain open across Vault reloads, so even editor-only pointer-bearing descriptors keep stale-alias pattern alive.
Solution: Borrow `BufferID.FloraGenomeDtos` with `TryGetGenerationHandle` and resolve method-local genome view with `TryResolveHandle` inside `OnGUI`. Missing or empty buffers still use existing mock preview.
Rejected Alternatives: Ignoring editor code was rejected because Task 17 requires Vault X-Ray/editor facades to model safe handle access. Allocating or populating flora genomes from this window was rejected because flora genome ownership belongs to flora genome runtime/baker, not preview UI.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime impact is zero. Editor cost is one descriptor validation per `OnGUI` preview pass.
Problem: `EntityDeltaGizmoProbe.cs`, `EntityDeltaCompressionArchitecture.cs`, and `VoxelDeltaCompressionArchitecture.cs` still used `TryGetBufferHandle` or `GetBufferHandle<T>` plus `.Resolve(vault)`. Save delta buffers are binary payload routes; stale descriptors here risk corrupting or misreporting WAL/delta state.
Solution: Replace gizmo read with `TryGetGenerationHandle` plus `TryResolveHandle`; replace both compression architecture helpers with `GetGenerationHandle<T>` plus `TryResolveHandle`.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving these as cold/editor helpers was rejected because binary save routes are precisely where stale views are least acceptable. Reworking compression or checksum logic was rejected because defect is descriptor lifetime, not codec math.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation per helper acquisition or gizmo draw. RLE, checksum, WAL, and gizmo sector loops do not validate per byte or per sector.
Problem: `VisualPressureAgingRuntime.cs` stored generation descriptors but still called `TryGetBufferGeneration` in owned buffer validation, initialization recovery, external input validation, and stale-external detection. That made descriptor validity depend on separate metadata fact before same handle was resolved.
Solution: Use `TryResolveHandle` through existing descriptor helpers as single proof of generation freshness. Keep `IsHandleForBuffer`, `IsExternalHandleValid`, owner checks, and required-length checks unchanged.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping generation metadata polling because it was explicit was rejected; explicit duplicate facts are still route drift. Rebuilding visual aging Vault layout was rejected because payload identity and shader ABI are already explicit and outside this pointer-lifetime pass.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes metadata poll at validation gates. Aging/degradation jobs, telemetry pushes, and graphics-buffer uploads continue over local views without per-element descriptor checks.
Problem: `HectonFluidEngine.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<float4>` descriptors for `WakeGlobalBuffer` and `WakeVectorBuffer`, allocated through `GetBufferHandle`, and resolved with `.Resolve(vault)` immediately before GPU upload. Dynamic wake presentation can run across Vault compaction or DataVault replacement, so pointer-bearing descriptors are unsafe even when data is visual.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<float4>` descriptors, borrow existing wake buffers during allocation-locked phases, allocate with `GetGenerationHandle` only when unlocked, and resolve method-local `NativeArray<float4>` views with `TryResolveHandle` before upload.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing dynamic wake route was rejected because shader-side wake fake is cheap visual substitute for CPU fluid simulation. Releasing wake buffers on fluid teardown was not added because prior route only cleared descriptors here and wake ownership is already documented as multi-owner conflict with VFX lanes.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two descriptor validations per dynamic wake upload phase. upload loop still copies local `NativeArray<float4>` views to GPU buffer and does not validate per slot.
Problem: `SeedShipAnomalyShaderBridge.cs` cached `VaultBufferHandle<float4>` plus `vault.VaultGenerationID` for `BufferID.ShaderGlobalState`. metadata generation cache could say "current" while pointer-bearing descriptor still represented stale address state.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<float4>`, resolve slot views with `TryResolveHandle`, and use `TryGetGenerationHandle`/`GetGenerationHandle` only to acquire descriptor. Direct shader globals remain as fallback when Vault slot lane is unavailable.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `VaultGenerationID` for fast cache was rejected because generation descriptor already carries proof and must be validated by resolve. Removing direct shader globals was rejected because anomaly presentation should fail closed visually even when Vault slot allocation is unavailable.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation per publish path. bridge writes one `float4` slot and does not validate per shader parameter.
Problem: `SubmarineStructuralGrid.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<float4>` for active breaches and `VaultBufferHandle<DamageControlTelemetryEntry>` for damage-control blackbox telemetry. Vehicle structural state can run for long sessions, so stale descriptors here would hit both visual breach upload and proof-artifact telemetry.
Solution: Store generation descriptors, resolve method-local views through `TryResolveHandle`, and borrow existing descriptors during allocation-locked phases. Allocation remains limited to unlocked Vault phases.
Rejected Alternatives: Migrating entire structural grid private native state was rejected for this bounded pass because it includes many owner-local job arrays and requires separate Vault route card. Keeping two handle fields because data is visual/blackbox was rejected because blackbox proof artifacts and long-lived breach visuals must be relocatable.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at breach and telemetry resolve boundaries. Breach repair jobs and telemetry loops use local views and do not validate per row.
Problem: `WorldGenerativeGeologyTerrainSeamApplier.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<float>` per terrain baseline, `NativeArray<float>` baseline alias in `TerrainApplyState`, and `VaultBufferHandle<TerrainSeamTelemetryEntry>` for seam blackbox. Terrain apply state can survive multiple reconcile/preview passes, so both handle and stored native view could point at relocated Vault memory.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<float>` and `VaultGenerationHandle<TerrainSeamTelemetryEntry>` descriptors only. Resolve method-local `NativeArray<T>` views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` before baseline copy/populate/projection and blackbox record/dump. During allocation-locked phases, borrow existing descriptors with `TryGetGenerationHandle`; allocate/grow only while Vault is unlocked.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping baseline `NativeArray<float>` cache because terrain patching is editor/slow-path was rejected; stale native aliases are cadence-independent. Reworking MapMagic, hybrid projection, voxel blend mask upload, or terrain writeback was rejected because defect is descriptor lifetime, not terrain math. Releasing baseline buffers from `TerrainApplyState.ReleaseBaseline()` was rejected for this bounded pass because existing state did not own reference-count teardown and terrain baseline BufferIDs are per-terrain compatibility lanes.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation descriptor validation when baseline or blackbox view is opened. Heightmap sample loops, hybrid Burst jobs, and blackbox dump loops operate on local resolved view and do not validate per sample or per entry.
Problem: `SubmarineFluidDynamics.cs` used generic `VaultNativeBuffer<T>` wrapper holding `VaultBufferHandle<T>`, dereferenced `_handle.ptr` in its indexer, refreshed through `TryGetBufferHandle`, and polled `TryGetBufferGeneration`. That one wrapper backed all compartment, bulkhead, hydro, blackbox, and exterior thermal lanes, so single stale pointer could contaminate whole submarine fluid route.
Solution: Replace wrapper storage with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` plus cached length scalar. `Ensure` acquires/grows via `GetGenerationHandle<T>` only while Vault is unlocked and borrows via `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>` under allocation lock. `Refresh`, indexer access, and implicit `NativeArray<T>` conversion open method-local views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`.
Rejected Alternatives: Patching each of 28 lane fields separately was rejected because stale alias pattern was centralized in wrapper. Keeping cached `NativeArray<T>` view inside wrapper was rejected because `NativeArray<T>` carries native address and can go stale after relocation. Releasing all fluid buffers on disable was rejected for this pass because existing route only clears wrapper state after dependency fences and ownership/refcount policy for shared vehicle lanes needs separate teardown audit.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation when wrapper opens view. Scheduled Burst jobs still receive local `NativeArray<T>` values and do not validate descriptors inside their loops. stale raw pointer path is removed for all submarine fluid lanes.
Problem: `ShinobuFloraFaunaSymbiosisSolver.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors for all major symbiosis lanes, resolved them with `.Resolve(vault)`, and exposed unused `GetFloraRef` bridge through `GetElementAsRef`. These buffers feed long-lived AI ecosystem jobs and can cross Vault relocation, so pointer-bearing descriptors are unacceptable.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors for all symbiosis lanes. Add local helpers for claim, borrow, and resolve so cold setup uses `GetGenerationHandle<T>` only when unlocked, allocation-locked phases borrow existing descriptors, and runtime reads/writes derive method-local `NativeArray<T>` views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`.
Rejected Alternatives: file-wide managed abstraction was rejected because hot path needs flat descriptors and local `NativeArray<T>` views. Keeping byref `GetFloraRef` bridge was rejected because ref must originate from current phase-local view. Editing simulation jobs was rejected because their inputs already accept `NativeArray<T>` and defect was stale descriptor lifetime, not math.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation validation at view-open boundaries. Flora/fish/link Burst loops still receive local arrays and do not validate per entity or per link.
## Decision 098 - Thermodynamics file worker is blocked until Core exposes relocation-pinned lease
Problem: `ThermodynamicsHazardGridRuntime.FileWorker.cs` keeps `_binaryConstantsWorkerPtr` and `_csvWorkerPtr` from Vault byte lanes for background worker thread. worker can outlive Vault relocation, and current evidence does not show defrag honoring active writer metadata strongly enough to make direct worker writes safe.
Solution: Do not apply cosmetic local `TryResolveHandle` patch. safe migration is to parse binary constants and CSV overrides into worker-local staged scalar payloads, publish staged readiness with `Volatile.Write`, and apply to `_constants` on owner/main phase after resolving `VaultGenerationHandle<ThermodynamicsHazardConstants>`.
Rejected Alternatives: Letting worker resolve `NativeArray<byte>` locally was rejected because resolution returns phase-local view, not relocation-pinned lease. Holding normal write lock was rejected because inspected relocation path does not prove it fences external worker writers. Leaving issue undocumented was rejected because this is real UAF class.
Scalability potential: Low devices benefit from avoiding worker/Vault contention and can keep cheap staged constants. Middle/high/ultra keep richer thermal hazard tuning once applied from owner phase; gameplay truth and DTO layout stay unchanged.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids unsafe background writes into relocatable Vault memory. future safe patch shifts file IO parsing to worker-local memory and one owner-phase descriptor validation before writing constants.
Problem: `ToxicOutgassingChemistryRuntime.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors for every density, chemistry, signal, telemetry, CSV, binary, and header lane, resolved them with `.Resolve(vault)`, exposed constants through `ConstantsRef`, and exposed raw pointer through `TryGetConstantsPointer`. These lanes are long-lived, scheduled, and blackbox-visible; stale aliases here can corrupt gas density, chemical exposure signals, and 300-frame dump.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors only. Open method-local `NativeArray<T>` views with `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` before owner mutation, job setup, telemetry commit, shader publish, CSV parse, and binary probe. Replace constants ref/pointer facade with value read/write calls and update editor tuner to edit local copy before writing it back.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping editor-only pointer was rejected because editor windows can outlive Vault relocation and still model unsafe API usage. Replacing every call with per-cell generation check was rejected because descriptor validation belongs at phase boundaries, not inside Burst loops. Moving toxicity buffers into private native arrays was rejected because atmosphere chemistry state and blackbox data are Vault-owned proof/state lanes.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation at each view-open boundary. 32^3 diffusion, flow, exposure, biolum, and telemetry Burst jobs still run over local `NativeArray<T>` views with `[NoAlias]` fields and no per-cell descriptor validation. Removing public pointer escape eliminates one relocation UAF class without adding managed allocations.
Problem: `AmbientBiotaDirector.cs` persisted six `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and three `NativeArray<T>.ReadOnly` aliases created through `IDataVault.CreateAlias`. Read-only aliases still carry native addresses, and ambient service exposes them to chunk residency consumers, so relocation could leave consumers reading stale biota AUP/state memory.
Solution: Store generation descriptors for biota AUP, velocity, state, macro-hydration counter, telemetry ring, and telemetry cursor lanes. Resolve local views with `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` at phase/service boundaries. Public read-only service properties now return transient `.AsReadOnly()` wrappers over freshly resolved local views rather than cached aliases.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached read-only aliases was rejected because read-only does not mean relocation-safe. Reworking `IAmbientBiotaService` contract was rejected because it is cross-domain contract; same return types can be backed by current generation-resolved views. Replacing indirect draw or macro hydration logic was rejected because defect is descriptor lifetime, not presentation math.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation when opening biota/counter/telemetry views. Drift, spawn, hydration, dehydration, and residency loops still iterate local arrays without per-row descriptor validation. Removing `CreateAlias` fields eliminates three persistent native-address aliases.
Problem: `CartographyGridJobs.cs` defined `CartographyVaultHandles` with `VaultBufferHandle<T>` fields, allocated them through `GetBufferHandle`, borrowed through `TryGetBufferHandle`, and opened all cartography views through `.Resolve(vault)`. `PlayerExplorationTracker` persists this bundle, so stale descriptors could hit discovery words, telemetry, tuning, scanner profiles, upload payloads, and rollback snapshots.
Solution: Replace every field in `CartographyVaultHandles` with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`. Unlocked acquisition now uses `GetGenerationHandle<T>`, allocation-locked acquisition uses `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>`, and `TryResolveViews` opens all buffers through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting `PlayerExplorationTracker` was rejected because consumer already depends on bundle API and stale pointer route is centralized inside `CartographyVault`. Adding per-word descriptor checks was rejected because discovery, RLE, and upload jobs must remain dense data-local loops.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation once per cartography view binding. Discovery, sonar, POI injection, RLE, upload, telemetry, and rollback Burst jobs continue to operate on local arrays without descriptor checks inside word/voxel loops.
Problem: `ShinobuEcosystemBalancer.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors for ambient entity/AUP rows, boid states, frame snapshots, sector/tuning/counter/telemetry/debug lanes, render matrices/custom data/indirect args, spatial hash buffers, CSV scratch, legacy scratch, and species profiles. It resolved them through `.Resolve(vault)` and kept unused `GetAmbientEntityRef` bridge over `GetElementAsRef`, leaving primary swarm simulation exposed to stale native addresses after Vault relocation.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors only. Add `ClaimVaultHandle` and `TryOpenVaultView` so allocation uses `GetGenerationHandle<T>` only when Vault is unlocked, locked phases borrow existing descriptors through `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>`, and every owner phase derives method-local `NativeArray<T>` views with `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting flocking, spatial hash, macro biomass, HZB/GPU upload, or predator logic was rejected because defect is pointer lifetime, not ecosystem math. Keeping static byref helper was rejected because any ref must originate from current local view, not persisted pointer handle. Adding per-boid descriptor checks was rejected because boid loops must remain vectorizable dense array work.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep continuous quality-weight budget collapse, update stride, reduced neighbor samples, and GPU/indirect fail-closed behavior. Middle/high/ultra retain richer flocking samples, debug cells, indirect procedural draw payloads, CSV-authored species profiles, and blackbox telemetry through same BufferIDs without changing gameplay authority, DTO layout, shader ABI, or save identity.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation only at schedule, CSV, initial-population, GPU-upload, and telemetry boundaries. local-shift, spatial hash, flocking, render payload, macro biomass, indirect args, and telemetry count jobs still consume local arrays without per-row descriptor validation or managed allocation.
Problem: `EcosystemPopulationBalancer.cs` persisted eight `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and resolved them through `.Resolve(vault)`. Six lanes are owned population buffers, while `EntityAUPs` and `EntityFlags` are external truth lanes; treating both as pointer handles risks stale aliases and treating both as owned would violate authority boundaries.
Solution: Convert all eight descriptors to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`. Owned buffers `EcosystemPopulationCoefficients`, `EcosystemPopulationSectorState`, `EcosystemPopulationCullEvents`, `EcosystemPopulationTelemetryRing`, `EcosystemPopulationFreeRing`, and `EcosystemPopulationCounters` use `GetGenerationHandle<T>` only when allocation is legal and are exact-released on teardown/DataVault rebind. External `EntityAUPs` and `EntityFlags` are borrowed through `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>` and resolved only into method-local views.
Rejected Alternatives: Owner-wide `ReleaseOwnerBuffers(SystemID.AIEcology)` was rejected because `SystemID.AIEcology` is shared by other ecology runtimes. Rewriting population math or death SignalBus payloads was rejected because unsafe route was Vault descriptor lifetime, not bounded Lotka-Volterra job.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cold-tick population governor, free-ring reuse, and tier flee-down requests. Middle/high/ultra keep richer sector/cull telemetry and SignalBus death proof through same DTO layouts; `GlobalQualityWeight`, save identity, and entity truth ownership are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation validation at cold setup, sector-state rebuild, job schedule, telemetry write, and signal publish boundaries. Burst job still receives local `NativeArray<T>` values and does not validate descriptors per entity or per sector.
Problem: `ShinobuApexBrainVault.cs` persisted public bundle of fifteen `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors, opened all cognition lanes through `.Resolve(vault)`, and exposed `GetStateAsRef` over `GetElementAsRef`. bundle is reused by editor tooling and scheduled cognition jobs, so stale descriptors could corrupt apex state, signals, tuning, CSV scratch, or blackbox telemetry after Vault relocation.
Solution: Convert `ApexBrainVaultHandles` to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, acquire unlocked lanes through `GetGenerationHandle<T>`, borrow locked lanes through `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>`, and bind `ApexBrainVaultBuffers` through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Replace byref accessor with value-copy `TryReadState` and `TryWriteState`. Add `ReleaseOwnedHandles` for exact apex BufferIDs.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping public byref helper was rejected because refs can escape phase-local view. Rewriting cognition scoring, signal queues, CSV parser, or dump format was rejected because those paths already consume local arrays; defect was handle lifetime. Owner-wide release was rejected because `SystemID.AICognition` is shared by adjacent cognition vaults.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation once per bundle view binding. apex cognition Burst job still receives local arrays with `[NoAlias]` fields and does not validate descriptors per leviathan, acoustic tap, or influence node.
Problem: `TradeMarauderRuntime.cs` persisted twenty-three `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors for marauder state, inventories, economy weights, sector data, * scratch, telemetry, tuning, faction standing, mock inventory, signal scratch, loot, sector hash, CSV scratch, counters, route plans, and visual proxy lanes. It resolved those descriptors with `.Resolve(_vault)` from FrostTick, editor, CSV, reputation, and post-job publish paths, leaving economy proof/state lanes exposed to stale native addresses after Vault relocation.
Solution: Replace every trade marauder lane field with `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`. Cold setup now validates existing descriptors with `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>`/`TryResolveHandle`, allocates with `GetGenerationHandle<T>` only while Vault is unlocked, and opens method-local `NativeArray<T>` views through `TryOpenVaultView`. Non-deferred teardown and DataVault rebind release exact owner descriptors through `ReleaseBuffer(in handle)`.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting * pathfinding, offscreen theft, trade negotiation, acoustic ping publication, or visual proxy hydration was rejected because those jobs already consume local arrays and defect was handle lifetime. Forcing `JobHandle.Complete()` during `OnDisable` was rejected because dispatcher owns completion windows and hidden teardown stalls violate phase discipline. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact BufferID release is safer than broad owner release under parallel-agent edits.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per opened lane at setup/FrostTick/editor/CSV/publish boundaries. * node loops, inventory loops, theft negotiation, visual hydration, acoustic signature, and telemetry jobs still operate on local `NativeArray<T>` values with no per-node descriptor validation or managed allocation.
Problem: `AlphaLeviathanCognitionVault.cs` persisted public `AlphaLeviathanVaultHandles` bundle made of `VaultBufferHandle<T>` rows and resolved them through `.Resolve(vault)`. bridge also exposed raw `TryAcquireBuffers` path over `GetBuffer<T>`/`TryGetBuffer<T>`, allowing callers to cache native views without current generation proof.
Solution: Convert five Alpha cognition lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` and bind views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle` at method boundaries only. `TryAcquireBuffers` now acquires descriptors first and then resolves transient views, so even compatibility callers pass through generation route. `ReleaseOwnedHandles` releases only exact five owner descriptors.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting tangent-orbit stalking, SDF contour collapse, phase byte compatibility, or blackbox binary dump was rejected because those systems already operate on local arrays and defect was descriptor lifetime. Keeping direct `GetBuffer<T>` compatibility was rejected because it preserved raw-view cache path. Owner-wide release was rejected because `SystemID.AICognition` is shared by apex cognition and other predator cognition lanes.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays five descriptor validations at acquire/resolve boundaries. Burst stalk job still receives local `NativeArray<T>` values and no per-slot descriptor check; `AlphaLeviathanCognitionState=192`, `AlphaLeviathanSensoryStimulus=176`, `AlphaLeviathanSteeringOutput=128`, and telemetry `=64` remain aligned and unchanged.
Problem: `DataArchaeologyRuntime.cs` persisted `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors for discovery word, notification, and telemetry lanes, resolved them through `.Resolve(vault)`, and repeatedly polled `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` from private resolver paths. same file also used `GlobalRegistry.ScalabilityTier`/`HectonQualityTier` to skip scanner shader points outright on low tiers.
Solution: Convert three lanes to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, cache `IDataVault` only from cold lifecycle/hotswap code, and open method-local views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Allocation/grow routes are explicitly named `TryOpenOrAcquire*` so read-style accessors do not hide mutation. Safe teardown/rebind releases exact three owner descriptors. Scanner presentation now uses `HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight` with smoothstep progress scale.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `TryResolve*` methods that allocate was rejected because read accessors must be pure by doctrine. Owner-wide release was rejected because `SystemID.GameplayTools` is shared. Low-tier scanner early return was rejected because binary quality gates create visible feature popping and violate continuous scalability.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep scanner feedback as dim/cheap shader scalar rather than hard-off feature. Middle devices get partial progress visibility. High/ultra retain full scanner shader progress and existing notification/telemetry fidelity through unchanged BufferIDs and DTO layouts.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at setup, lore sync, notification enqueue/dequeue, telemetry commit, and blackbox dump boundaries. Discovery bit loops and telemetry row writes still use local `NativeArray<T>` views with no per-row descriptor validation; removing binary tier gate avoids branchy presentation policy tied to stale enum state.
Problem: `BaseAtmosphereEngine.cs` persisted four `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors and also cached four Vault-backed `NativeArray<T>` views as fields. Front/back compartment arrays are swapped after cold tick job, so stale native views here could survive Vault relocation or DataVault replacement. original teardown only cleared aliases and descriptors.
Solution: Store only `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors for front/back compartment lanes, CO2 byte lane, and blackbox telemetry. Resolve method-local native views at setup, seed, schedule, mutation, and blackbox boundaries. Swap front/back descriptors after job completes. Public read routes use `IDataVault.TryReadHandle`; mutation/schedule routes use `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Exact owner release is immediate when no job is active and deferred through captured generation descriptors when cold tick job fence is still pending.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached `NativeArray<T>` fields was rejected because they are raw address aliases even without explicit pointers. Forcing `JobHandle.Complete()` on teardown was rejected because dispatcher-owned completion windows must remain non-blocking. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact BufferID release is sufficient and safer under shared `SystemID.HabitatAtmosphere`.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at setup, schedule, seed, compartment mutation, and blackbox write boundaries. cold tick job still receives local contiguous arrays and no per-compartment descriptor validation; deferred release avoids teardown main-thread stall.
Problem: `HectonSurfaceWeatherDirector.cs` kept `VaultBufferHandle<SurfaceWeatherJobOutput>`, resolved it with `.Resolve(vault)` for seed/schedule/complete, and pulled `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` from output resolver. Disposal also used `forceComplete: true`, creating hidden teardown stall.
Solution: Store `VaultGenerationHandle<SurfaceWeatherJobOutput>` only. Cache `IDataVault` during lifecycle setup, acquire output lane through `GetGenerationHandle<T>`, and open method-local output views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Disposal now attempts non-forced completion and releases exact descriptor only when fence permits it.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping hot `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` lookup in `TryResolveWeatherJobOutput` was rejected because registry is cold DI. Keeping `forceComplete: true` was rejected because weather output disposal must not seize dispatcher completion window. Rewriting weather math job or AUP-safe origin changes was rejected because unsafe route was output lane descriptor.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation at weather output seed/schedule/complete boundaries. Burst job still writes one-element `NativeSlice<SurfaceWeatherJobOutput>` with no per-parameter descriptor validation, and teardown no longer forces main-thread wait.
Problem: `CablePhysicsDebugGizmo132.cs` used `TryGetBufferHandle` and `.Resolve(vault)` to draw solver-owned cable nodes and constraints. Even though this is diagnostic code, it kept obsolete pointer-bearing descriptor route alive.
Solution: Borrow `VaultGenerationHandle<CableNodeDTO>` and `VaultGenerationHandle<TetherConstraintDTO>` through `TryGetGenerationHandle<T>`, then open read-only diagnostic views through `IDataVault.TryReadHandle`.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing cable buffers from gizmo was rejected because cable solver owns those lanes. Adding per-node descriptor checks was rejected because draw loop should consume local read views.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two descriptor reads per gizmo draw. node/constraint loops do not validate descriptors per element and no managed allocation was added.
Problem: `CablePhysicsSolver132.cs` still used `GetBufferHandle(...).Resolve(...)` for mock bootstrap lanes, mock view binding, telemetry sampling, and blackbox dump reads. `Shinobu132CablePhysicsTunerWindow.cs` also wrote tuning/material lanes through same legacy pointer descriptor API.
Solution: Add generation-safe solver helpers that acquire `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors, open method-local `NativeArray<T>` views through `TryResolveHandle`, and use `TryReadHandle` for telemetry/dump reads. editor tuner now calls those helpers for tuning and material CSV writes.
Rejected Alternatives: Cleaning only editor window was rejected because unsafe pointer route would remain in runtime helper surface. Releasing buffers from editor code was rejected because solver owns cable lanes. Reworking TetherManager bootstrap scheduling was rejected in this pass because defect was descriptor lifetime, not dispatcher cadence.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep continuous quality-weight mock tether collapse, lower iteration counts, and reduced spline vertices. Middle devices keep normal editor tuning and telemetry. ## Decision 127 - Verlet tow and builder holography editor writes require explicit fences
Problem: `VerletTowTunerWindow.cs` still used `TryResolveHandle` to mutate cable tuning/material lanes, and `BuilderHolographyTools.cs` used latest-created Vault fallback, runtime all-view resolver for UI reads, and raw native pointer/ref in profile CSV parser.

Move Builder Holography UI reads to lane-specific `TryReadHandle` calls, route slider writes through short writer fence, and parse CSV into local DTO copy before writing row `0`.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating editor windows as safe exceptions was rejected because they are long-lived and survive Vault relocation. Keeping `TryResolveVaultViews` for tuner was rejected because it returns broad mutable runtime views when UI needs only tuning and telemetry lanes. Keeping raw parser ref was rejected because direct pointer extraction is precisely stale-alias pattern SHINOBU_202 is removing.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because both files are editor-only. Editor tuning reads validate descriptors once per refresh, edits pay one writer-fence transition, and CSV parsing stays descriptor-free after local view opens.
Problem: `VaultXRayWindow.cs` used `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated` for snapshot refresh, force defrag, and CSV override reload. That was allowed only for narrow bootstrap/editor diagnostic exceptions, but this window can use registered dependency without losing any X-Ray surface.
Solution: Replace static latest-created lookups with `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` and call existing `IDataVault` telemetry, memory map, generation id, defrag request, and CSV override APIs through that interface.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping latest-created because window is editor-only was rejected because it normalizes fallback route when registry-published owner is available. Casting to concrete `GlobalDataVault` was rejected because `IDataVault` already exposes required diagnostic methods.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because file is editor-only. Editor refresh cost is unchanged: one registry read followed by existing bounded 64-sample waterfall and 256-block memory-map pass.
Problem: `ShinobuOceanSurfaceAtmosphereRuntime.cs` persisted thirteen legacy `VaultBufferHandle<T>` fields, used direct `TryGetBuffer<T>` for tuner/debug snapshots, kept latest-created diagnostic fallback, and applied tuner values directly into runtime-owned lanes without writer fences.
Solution: Replace all persisted ocean Vault handles with 16-byte `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors. Resolve every lane through `_vault.TryResolveHandle` at method scope, read editor/debug snapshots through `TryReadHandle`, remove latest-created fallback, and wrap static tuner writes in `SystemID.CoreDiagnostics` writer fences released in `finally`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because `.Resolve(vault)` refreshes pointers was rejected because handle itself still carries cached pointer metadata. Keeping direct `TryGetBuffer<T>` for editor snapshots was rejected because snapshot APIs are long-lived UI consumers and should not normalize direct buffer access. Adding new runtime allocations or buffer IDs was rejected because existing lanes already own wave/atmosphere truth.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is single generation validation per lane open, not per wave lane. Editor slider writes pay bounded writer-fence transitions; frame-loop wave math, telemetry serialization, readback ring traversal, and GPU upload loops remain descriptor-free after local views open.
Problem: `SubmarineOsThermalGridRuntime.cs` persisted twenty legacy `VaultBufferHandle<T>` descriptors, used `GetBufferHandle<T>` and `handle.Resolve(vault)`, kept editor latest-created fallback, and exported `SubmarineThermalGridTuningDTO*` to two editor windows. That allowed long-lived editor pointer to outlive Vault relocation and kept stale pointer metadata in runtime Power solver.
Solution: Replace persisted thermal-grid handles with 16-byte `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` descriptors. Resolve method-local `NativeArray<T>` views through `IDataVault.TryResolveHandle`. Remove latest-created fallback from runtime route. Replace raw tuning pointer API with `TryReadTuning` and `TryApplyTuning`; editor windows now edit DTO copies and commit through `SystemID.CoreDiagnostics` writer fences. CSV reload opens CSV/spec/tuning/counter lanes through writer-fence views and releases them in `finally`.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving pointer API as editor-only was rejected because editor windows survive play-mode reloads and Vault relocation. Converting solver jobs away from raw pointers in this pass was rejected because jobs already receive pointers only after method-local descriptor resolution and that broader Burst-signature rewrite would expand blast radius. Using `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated` as editor fallback inside runtime was rejected because runtime already has registry/injected Vault route and standalone editor Vault fallback for isolated windows.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is one generation validation per lane open before schedule/readback/commit. Hot Jacobi jobs, topology copy, telemetry write, and shader scalar loops remain descriptor-free after local view binding. Editor slider writes pay one tuning writer-fence transition; CSV reload pays four writer-fence transitions before allocation-free byte parsing.
Problem: `RadioisotopeThermalGenerator.cs` persisted seven static `VaultBufferHandle<T>` lanes and opened them through `GetBufferHandle<T>` plus `handle.Resolve(vault)`. helper also polled `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` on every open and relied on handle length/created properties that do not exist on strict 16-byte descriptor.

Middle/high/ultra retain full 300-entry telemetry, save integration, thermodynamics/radiation signals, and visual/audio warning surfaces without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, or Power authority.
