Problem: guarded Core build after Fluid ring patch exposed broad compile wall in unrelated domains. Most errors were private helper visibility mismatches on nested Vault wrappers (`Open`, `AsNativeArray`, `GetSubArray`, `Resolve`, `OpenView`) already consumed by sibling partials or same-type methods. remaining errors were read-only contract drift in save/audio paths, legacy SignalBus bridge visibility mismatch, and Core facade hard-referencing optional DOTS scatter assembly.
Solution: Make only already-consumed wrapper view helpers public within their nested value types; no new allocation, handle shape, BufferID, or ownership route was added. Convert sector override writer to pass `sectorRecords.AsReadOnly()` into existing read-only helpers. Keep acoustic SDF aliases read-only and restore read-only raymarch payload assignment. Open `SignalBus<T>.OpenQueueForLegacyGlobalSignals()` as `internal` for legacy bridge. Remove direct `Hecton8.World.Dots.ScatterEntitiesSimulationBackend` type check from Core scatter facade; ClassicJobs remains schedulable, unknown optional backends are forced complete and rejected through existing warning route.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing optional DOTS project references was rejected because Core should not gain sibling-domain compile dependency. Rewriting wrapper consumers was rejected because these are compile-surface mismatches, not H-Phi ownership migrations. Widening `OpenQueueForLegacyGlobalSignals` to public was rejected; `internal` is enough. Returning mutable SDF payloads from `HectonVoxelVolume` was tested and rejected; final route keeps read-only SDF contracts.
Scalability potential: Runtime quality behavior is unchanged. Low devices keep same classic scatter fallback, audio raymarch budget, and Vault-owned scratch capacities; middle/high/ultra keep same visual-overkill paths where their owning assemblies are present. `GlobalQualityWeight`, DTO layouts, save identity, shader ABI, and authority routes are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: No player hot-path work was added. Compile-surface fixes are access changes or read-only argument conversions. Unknown optional scatter backends are not scheduled through Core until their contract assembly is present, avoiding direct dependency and protecting compile wall.
Problem: `SpatialAudioManager` retained `_acousticVoxelSdfTexture3D` as borrowed `NativeArray<byte>.ReadOnly` field, but field was never read. actual acoustic SDF payload path already resolves local read-only view from WorldStreaming-owned `VoxelSdfTexture3D` row. Keeping field created dead persistent Vault alias with no behavior value.
Solution: Delete `_acousticVoxelSdfTexture3D` field and all assignments/resets. Keep `_acousticVoxelSdfTexture3DHandle` because `TryOpenBorrowedAudioVaultBuffer` still uses descriptor to re-open WorldStreaming row when needed. active payload method returns its local `resolvedSdf` directly.
Rejected Alternatives: Deleting handle was rejected because it would force repeated cold handle acquisition and lose descriptor refresh route. Rewriting full SpatialAudio Vault pool set was rejected because virtual voice pools, DSP outputs, and material rows have broader scheduling semantics and need their own migration.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same acoustic SDF probe budget and virtual voice pressure. Middle/high/ultra keep same richer sonar/occlusion behavior. `GlobalQualityWeight`, BufferIDs, SDF payload shape, audio material IDs, and authority route are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes one persistent borrowed native view field. Runtime cost is unchanged; no managed allocation, native allocation, job, hidden `.Complete()`, shader variant, DTO stride change, direct sibling dependency, or hot GlobalRegistry polling was introduced.
Problem: `VaultSurgeryEditTests.cs` and `HeadlessKccSmokeTests.cs` still compiled against deleted pointer-era Vault APIs (`GetBufferHandle`, `TryGetBufferHandle`, `VaultBufferSlice<T>`, `GetElementAsRef(vault, ...)`, `GetElementAsReadOnlyRef(vault, ...)`, and `.Resolve(vault)`). Runtime code had moved to 16-byte generation descriptors, so leaving stale tests would block editor compile and teach wrong API.
Solution: Convert tests to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, `TryResolveHandle`, `TryReadHandle`, `TryAcquireSliceHandle`, and `TryResolveSlice`. Update ABI assertions to 16-byte `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` / `VaultBufferHandle<T>` and 32-byte `VaultSliceHandle<T>`. Update internal layout assertions to current 64-byte `VaultBufferMeta` and `ReservedCursorBytes` telemetry field.
Rejected Alternatives: Restoring pointer-bearing handle or raw slice API was rejected because it would recreate stale pointer retention. Deleting tests was rejected because ABI needs proof artifacts. Converting tests to private reflection access was rejected because it would normalize bypassing DataVault public ownership routes.
Scalability potential: Runtime low/middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged. value is compile-time proof that descriptor ABI remains pointer-free and ARM64-aligned.
Hardware Impact: 0 player runtime cost. Editor tests now validate current descriptor sizes without creating raw pointer routes or managed hot-path allocation.
## Decision 261 - Scatter stale-contract shim is compile-wall containment patch
Problem: Guarded Core build continued to see stale mutable `IScatterSimulationBackend.TrySchedule(ScatterSimulationConfig, NativeArray<float>, NativeArray<ScatterSimulationCellState>)` even though current source declares read-only inputs. This is outside SHINOBU_202, but it blocked verification of SHINOBU files.
Solution: Add mutable overloads to known classic and DOTS backend classes that delegate to current read-only implementation with `AsReadOnly()`. Change facade scheduler to dispatch known backend implementations directly, so it does not depend on stale interface metadata during this compile-wall state.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting World.Contracts, copying DLLs into `Library/ScriptAssemblies`, deleting build caches, or launching full rebuild were rejected. Broadly editing Scatter ownership or reverting to mutable source contract was rejected because it would weaken read-only snapshot route.
Scalability potential: Runtime quality behavior is unchanged. shim affects only backend scheduling compatibility; continuous scatter budgets and visual-overkill policy stay with existing systems.
Hardware Impact: One backend dispatch branch per scatter schedule. No per-cell loop cost, no GC allocation, no job completion, no DTO stride change, no shader variant, and no sibling assembly reference introduced.
## Decision 262 - Core compile wall stopped after three guarded attempts
Problem: After Scatter shim, Core build exposed 65 errors across many dirty, unrelated domains: private wrapper methods called across partial files, read-only NativeArray signature drift, SignalBus queue accessibility, and read-only byte buffer assignments. Mass-fixing those from SHINOBU_202 would violate domain boundaries and create refactor loop.
Solution: Stop build attempts after third guarded Core compile and record wall. SHINOBU-local diff checks and stale API scans pass; remaining compile ownership belongs to affected domain agents/integrator.
Rejected Alternatives: Making dozens of private wrapper methods public across Gameplay, Fauna, Ecosystem, Physics, Audio, Save, and SignalBus was rejected as architectural sabotage. Reverting unrelated dirty files was rejected because they are not owned by this task.
Scalability potential: No runtime behavior changed. This preserves compile-wall discipline and prevents one verification loop from becoming cross-domain rewrite.
Hardware Impact: Developer hardware cost was three narrow `Hecton8.Core.csproj` builds under CPU/compiler gate. No further build spam was launched after 3-strikes threshold.
## Decision 263 - Compile-wall wrapper accessors stay inside owner wrappers
Problem: Core compile exposed private helper methods on Vault-backed wrapper structs that were invoked from surrounding owner/partial code. wrappers already resolved generation handles into phase-local `NativeArray<T>` views; failure was C# accessibility, not missing data route.
Solution: Change only existing helper methods to public inside their already-private owner wrappers: `GetSubArray`, `Open`, `AsNativeArray`, `Resolve`, and `OpenView`. This preserves current descriptor route and avoids new allocations, new pointers, or new registry polling.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting Gameplay, Fauna, Ecosystem, Physics, Submarine, and VR somatic storage models in one pass was rejected as refactor loop. Restoring pointer-era handles was rejected because it would undo SHINOBU's stale-pointer work.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra runtime behavior is unchanged. This is compile access hygiene only.
Hardware Impact: 0 player runtime cost. No job, `.Complete()`, DTO stride change, shader variant, GC allocation, or sibling assembly reference was introduced.
Problem: Save, SpatialAudio, GlobalSignals, Scatter, and PlayerCritical audio had signature drift after descriptor/read-only migrations. risky fix would be to return mutable SDF or persistent-world aliases to consumers just to satisfy stale compile metadata.
Solution: Save converts validated sector override array to `.AsReadOnly()` once before table build/write. SpatialAudio stores borrowed voxel SDF as `NativeArray<byte>.ReadOnly`. GlobalSignals exposes legacy queue opener as `internal`, not public. Scatter dispatches only known read-only backend implementations and refuses unknown stale interface scheduling. PlayerCritical defines private included Burst SDF raymarch job with read-only `NativeArray<byte>.ReadOnly` inputs to avoid depending on stale `Hecton8.Audio.Echolocation.dll` field metadata.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing generated csproj, copying DLLs, deleting Library, exposing public signal queues, or adding mutable World SDF APIs was rejected. Those would weaken compile wall or data sovereignty.
Scalability potential: sonar raymarch remains same cinematic SDF fake: low quality can reduce `ResolveSonarSdfProbeCount()` and step budget; high/ultra can spend more probes on richer echo returns. Gameplay truth, DTO layout, save identity, and authority route are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids mutable alias expansion and keeps same read-only SDF sample path. Scatter unknown backend fallback now fails cold instead of attempting stale interface dispatch. No GC allocation or hidden main-thread completion was added.
## Decision 265 - Verification stops at one clean Core build
Problem: After Loop 251 patches, another build was needed to prove compile wall was actually reduced rather than hidden. Repeated builds would violate command discipline once target was proven.
Solution: Wait for CPU/compiler gate to clear, then run one narrow `Hecton8.Core.csproj` build. It succeeded with 0 errors and 29 warnings. No further build/rebuild/test run was launched.
Rejected Alternatives: Launching full solution rebuild, Unity batchmode, or test suites was rejected because mandate forbids unnecessary rebuild spam and current task only needed Core compile proof.
Scalability potential: None changed. Verification only.
Hardware Impact: Developer hardware cost was one gated 39.77s Core compile. Runtime cost is unchanged.
Problem: Post-build scan still found `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` in several runtime owners. Some mandates say no hot polling, but inspected snippets were boot, bind, lazy resolve, or periodic cache-refresh routes rather than per-element Burst/job hot loops.
Solution: Leave these routes unchanged in this loop and record them as owner-policy migration candidates. Any conversion needs owner-specific publication phase and cached interface proof, not blanket `TryGetLatestCreated()` replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Mechanical replacement with `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated()` was rejected because that API is explicitly diagnostic/bootstrap/crash-only outside route card. Removing lazy fallback from owners was rejected because it could break boot order.
Scalability potential: No behavior changed. Future owner route cards can reduce registry touch frequency without changing `GlobalQualityWeight`, DTO layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime change in this loop. Avoided unsafe architectural edit that could create null boot races.
Problem: After clean Core build, context compaction required re-verifying objective file state. Static scans still show many private `NativeArray<T>` and `NativeList<T>` fields in `HectonFluidEngine` and `SpatialAudioManager`, but remaining fields are not all equivalent to deleted stale Vault impact ring. Some are owner-local SoA scratch buffers, some are Vault aliases coupled to virtual voice/radar/portal scheduling, and Core DataVault's native tables are its owned storage.
Solution: Run targeted source hygiene and stale-pointer scans, then record distinction. deleted pointer-era DataVault surface remains absent: no `VaultBufferSlice<T>`, no public `TryAcquireSlice(...)`, no emergency overflow/dummy pointer route, no `.ptr` handle route, and no retained Fluid impact ring view/helper. Remaining Fluid/SpatialAudio native fields are fenced as owner migrations requiring route cards and profiler/scheduling proof.
Rejected Alternatives: Running another build was rejected because no compile-relevant source edit followed prior gated success. Running `.py` audit scripts was rejected by operator constraint and because they are known to deadlock machine. Mechanically deleting or resolving every remaining native field was rejected as cross-domain refactor loop.
Scalability potential: Runtime quality behavior is unchanged. Future owner migrations can convert persistent aliases to descriptor-resolved phase views without changing `GlobalQualityWeight`, DTO layout, save identity, authority route, or shader ABI.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Verification cost was static `rg`, `git diff --check`, and file inspection only; no new allocation, job, hidden `.Complete()`, shader variant, sibling assembly reference, or main-thread work was introduced.
Problem: `MacroDatabasePayloadHandle` carried public `IntPtr Pointer`, and Save/Ecosystem consumers dereferenced it directly. That made owner-private DataVault cache allocation look like stable cross-domain handle, creating stale pointer/UAF route whenever cache evicted, rewrote dirty payloads, or shut down.
Solution: Keep public handle as 40-byte explicit metadata DTO but replace offset 8 with `PayloadToken`. Store real pointer only in DataVault's private `MacroDatabasePayloadCacheEntry`. Add bounded copy APIs: `IMacroDatabaseNativeCacheOwner.TryCopyMacroDatabasePayload(...)` and `IMacroDatabaseService.TryCopyPayload(...)`. Consumers now copy into pre-owned native scratch before parsing.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping pointer and documenting caution was rejected because type name made it portable handle. Moving every payload into new per-sector Vault buffer was rejected because dynamic BufferID creation would be new global route without GREEN route card. Managed `byte[]` copies were rejected because WFC restore, macro swarm hydration, and dirty append are zero-GC binary paths.
Hardware Impact: MX350/i3 avoids cross-domain stale pointer dereference at cost of bounded `UnsafeUtility.MemCpy` into existing native scratch during hydration/append. public DTO remains 40 bytes: SectorHash@0 u64, PayloadToken@8 u64, FileOffset@16 i64, ByteLength@24 i32, Version@28 u32, Flags@32 u8, Reserved0@33 u8, Reserved1@34 u16, _pad0@36 u32.
Problem: `H8MacroDatabaseService` stored dirty payload handles in Vault slots and later appended by dereferencing `dirty.Pointer`. Even though this lived in Core/Save, slot is Vault DTO and must not contain address that survives cache mutation.
Solution: Add `BufferID.SaveMacroDatabasePayloadCopyScratch = 70377` and generation handle `_payloadCopyScratchHandle`. Dirty append, compaction flush, and clean-cache rewrite call DataVault copy into this scratch lane, then append/store from scratch pointer within same locked phase.
Rejected Alternatives: Stackalloc for 256KB payloads was rejected as unsafe for large macro records. private `NativeArray<byte>` field was rejected because SHINOBU is removing private persistent arrays from shared binary routes. Reusing WFC or Ecosystem scratch was rejected because SavePersistence owns Macro DB append staging.
Hardware Impact: One 256KB maximum Vault scratch lane, allocated through DataVault, replaces public long-lived payload addresses. No new GC allocation, no job completion, no shader variant, no DTO size change, and no sibling runtime dependency.
## Decision 270 - Compile-wall containment stops at source-owned seams
Problem: guarded Core verification build after macro payload pointer quarantine failed outside SHINOBU-owned Vault/Macro files. first surface was stale/missing Gameplay symbols: `VRSomaticProvider.Comfort.cs` referenced horizon DTOs and kernels from `VRSomaticProvider.HorizonLock.cs`, while generated Core project did not compile that new partial. `PlayerKinematicsRuntime_HandIK.cs` also depended on stale `Hecton8.Core.Contracts.dll` that did not expose `PlayerHandIkConfigFlags`, and C# definite-assignment analysis could not prove bridge native views were assigned after short-circuit resolution.
Solution: Make only source-owned, narrow containment edits. Move VR somatic DTO layouts into `VRSomaticProvider.cs`, which already owns provider and is present in generated Core project; remove duplicate DTO definitions from horizon partial. Use local HandIK config flag constants with same bit values as source contract and initialize bridge native views to default before conditional resolve. SHINOBU macro pointer scan remains clean after these changes.
Rejected Alternatives: Hand-editing generated `Hecton8.Core.csproj` was rejected because prior project logs explicitly identify generated project omission as Unity regeneration debt. Copying or rebuilding `Library/ScriptAssemblies/Hecton8.Core.Contracts.dll`, deleting Library, launching Unity regeneration, or broad-fixing Combat/KCC errors was rejected as compile-wall escalation outside SHINOBU_202. Moving entire horizon partial into main provider was rejected because it would be large Gameplay rewrite to work around generated-project state.
Scalability potential: Runtime low/middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged. DTO layout, save identity, Vault BufferIDs, horizon quality curves, and authority routes are not changed by this containment. core SHINOBU result remains pointer-free macro payload route.
Hardware Impact: 0 player runtime cost. only build cost was one gated narrow Core build after CPU dropped below 50%; it failed on generated-project/foreign-domain compile wall, not on Macro/Vault files. No new job, `.Complete()`, allocation, shader variant, direct sibling dependency, or hot registry polling was introduced.
Problem: `GlobalNativeBufferHandle` was public cross-assembly contract named as DataVault slice handle but carried `IntPtr Pointer` at offset 0. That normalizes passing process-local address through compile-wall contracts and conflicts with pointer-free descriptor law already applied to `VaultGenerationHandle<T>` and `MacroDatabasePayloadHandle`.
Solution: Preserve 32-byte ABI and offset map while replacing offset 0 with opaque `ulong DescriptorToken`. Update `VaultOffsets.g.cs` and Assembly X-Ray generator string from `GlobalNativeBufferHandle_Pointer` to `GlobalNativeBufferHandle_DescriptorToken`. typed `PhysicsFacade` function pointer path remains unchanged because unmanaged function pointers are explicit cold bridge route and not DataVault storage ownership.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping address field and relying on comments was rejected because contracts outlive allocator phase that produced address. Rewriting all static-data `byte*` parser jobs was rejected because those pointers are job-local, `[NoAlias]`, and not public retained DataVault handles. Removing `GlobalFunctionPointerHandle` or `PhysicsFacade.FunctionPointer<T>` was rejected because it would break approved devirtualized bridge path.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged. This is authority hardening: quality weight can scale cadence/capacity elsewhere, but it must not turn descriptor into retained process address.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. public handle is still one 32-byte value: DescriptorToken@0 u64, Length@8 i32, StrideBytes@12 i32, OwnerHash@16 u32, Generation@20 u32, AccessFlags@24 u32, Reserved@28 u32. It removes one stale-address route without adding job, allocation, hidden completion, shader variant, or sibling assembly dependency.
Problem: `TryOpenMacroDatabasePayload` and `TryCopyMacroDatabasePayload` intentionally call `TouchMacroDatabasePayload(...)` to update cache residency. Without explicit contract note, future cleanup pass could misclassify them as pure read accessors and either rename them back to `TryGet*` or remove LRU touch.
Solution: Add contract comments stating that open/copy refresh cache residency and that service-level copy returns bytes into caller-owned native memory without leaking cache addresses. This keeps pure read naming reserved for APIs that do not mutate global/cache state.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing LRU touch was rejected because it would make eviction less representative under streaming/hydration pressure. Renaming back to `TryGetPayload` was rejected because it violates read-accessor doctrine. Adding second pure lookup API was rejected because consumers currently need residency refresh when they actually consume payload metadata/bytes.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost and 0 compile behavior change. Documentation only; no job, allocation, pointer, shader variant, or sibling dependency added.
Problem: After `GlobalNativeBufferHandle` stopped exposing data address, `GlobalFunctionPointerHandle` still had generic public field named `Pointer`. route is allowed, but field name hides critical distinction between code pointers and retained DataVault/native-buffer addresses.
Solution: Rename field at offset 0 to `FunctionPointer` while keeping explicit 32-byte layout and `IntPtr` type. No source consumer referenced old field name in executable Global/Core source.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing function-pointer support was rejected because unmanaged function pointers are approved devirtualized bridge for cold non-generic registry slots. Replacing it with interface arrays was rejected because it would reintroduce virtual dispatch. Converting it to DataVault descriptor token was rejected because code pointers and native buffer descriptors are different authority routes.
Scalability potential: Runtime behavior is unchanged across quality levels. gain is compile-wall clarity: GlobalQualityWeight may scale work, but it does not change whether handle names executable code or native data.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Layout remains FunctionPointer@0 IntPtr, FunctionHash@8 u32, ContractHash@12 u32, Version@16 u32, Flags@20 u32, Reserved@24 u64.
Problem: `VaultTransformAlias` was public Vault memory contract with `long MatrixPointer` at offset 0. Even if intent was cinematic Dear Lie to avoid per-entity matrix copies, exporting retained process-local matrix address is same stale-pointer class as deleted Vault slice and macro payload pointer routes.
Solution: Keep `VaultTransformAlias` at 32 bytes but replace pointer with `MatrixBufferId`, `MatrixOffsetBytes`, and `MatrixGeneration`. Update offset constants accordingly. record now says which Vault buffer generation and byte offset owns shared matrix, not where that matrix happened to live in this process.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping pointer was rejected because relocation/defrag/origin-shift can invalidate it. Per-static-entity matrix copies were rejected because Dear Lie is valid; alias shape was flaw. Widening to 64 bytes was rejected because no executable consumer needs extra metadata and existing 32-byte stride is cache-friendlier.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost in current source because no executable consumer reads alias. Future consumers perform one descriptor resolve per batch/phase instead of trusting stale raw address. Layout is MatrixBufferId@0 u32, MatrixOffsetBytes@4 u32, MatrixGeneration@8 u32, TransformHash@12 u32, EntityId@16 u32, Flags@20 u8, padding 21..31.
Problem: `VaultSovereigntyMaintenance.RunPreSimulationFrost` scheduled two jobs, registered handle, and immediately called `handle.Complete()` before reading back stats. That is same-frame schedule/readback loop hidden inside read-looking maintenance helper and violates dispatcher-owned completion discipline.
Solution: Run bounded Frost maintenance loops directly inside owner phase. method already executes only on memory defrag cadence and uses `ResolveSweepBudget(...)` with `GlobalQualityWeight` and `StrideAggressiveness`; those controls remain intact. `FlagSweepScheduled` became `FlagSweepExecuted` so telemetry describes what actually happened.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping hidden completion was rejected. Returning new pending `JobHandle` from this pass was rejected because SystemDispatcher would need route-carded deferred telemetry path and failure handling. Creating tiny jobs just to recover Burst while completing immediately was rejected because it preserves bad scheduling pattern.
Scalability potential: Low devices still sweep minimum budget and lower cadence through existing quality curve; high/ultra still sweep more rows when quality permits. Gameplay truth, DTO layout, save identity, and authority route are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes one job registration and one forced main-thread `Complete()` per Frost maintenance tick. Work remains O(AUP row count + quality-scaled sweep budget) and is already recorded in `MaxJobUs` telemetry for budget forensics.
Problem: `VaultRelocationRecord`, `VaultMemoryAddressShiftRecord`, and `MemoryAddressShiftSignal` exposed `OldPointer`/`NewPointer` numeric process addresses. Current executable consumers use buffer id, flags, entity id, and indices to refresh cached views or draw diagnostics; publishing process addresses is unnecessary stale-pointer surface.
Solution: Preserve DTO sizes and offsets while renaming lanes to `OldOffsetBytes` and `NewOffsetBytes`. `GlobalDataVault.RecordRelocation` converts old/new arena pointers into offsets relative to `_arenaBase` before storing records, and `SystemDispatcher` forwards offsets to signal.
Rejected Alternatives: Deleting relocation signals was rejected because SubmarineFluidDynamics and diagnostics consume them as refresh notices. Keeping pointer values was rejected because it normalizes retaining addresses after defrag. Adding both pointer and offset lanes was rejected because it would expand ABI and keep hazard.
Scalability potential: Runtime quality behavior is unchanged. Low devices avoid stale address propagation during memory pressure; high/ultra retain same relocation notice fidelity without DTO identity changes.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. Relocation emits two pointer-minus-base calculations only when defrag moves block. Signal/record sizes remain unchanged: old offset @0 i64, new offset @8 i64, metadata unchanged from byte 16 onward.
Problem: `MemoryDesyncSignal`, `HashDeltaUpdateSignal`, and `MemorySentinelRollbackSignal` carried `TargetMemoryPointer` at offset 32. sentinel owner needs target addresses internally to hash and rollback memory, but SignalBus consumers do not need process-local addresses. Publishing them widens stale-address propagation beyond owner route.
Solution: Preserve all 64-byte signal layouts and offset 32 while replacing public signal lane with `TargetMemoryFingerprint`. Rename `MemorySentinelTargetDTO.FunctionPointerHash` to `TargetMemoryFingerprint` at offset 48 because it was already hash of target memory address/length/buffer id, not executable function pointer. Runtime and Burst publishers now copy fingerprint into signal payloads.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing `ValidationStateDTO.TargetMemoryPointer` and `MemorySentinelTargetDTO.TargetMemoryPointer` was rejected in this pass because sentinel validation job must dereference guarded memory after owner locks target buffers. Publishing raw addresses through SignalBus was rejected because hash/buffer/frame/severity data is enough for diagnostics and rollback notice routing. Converting sentinel to resolve every target by BufferID inside job was rejected without route card because some targets are mock/mod quarantine spans and pointer-registry sentinel sources.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cadence-scaled validation budget and reduced lane capacities. Middle/high/ultra retain richer integrity telemetry without public address leakage. `GlobalQualityWeight`, DTO sizes, save identity, authority route, and SignalBus lane counts are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. fingerprint was already computed during target append; signal copy remains 64 bytes. No new allocation, job, hidden `.Complete()`, shader variant, sibling assembly reference, or hot registry polling was introduced.
Problem: `NativeAllocationSnapshotSource` was public 32-byte struct with public `Pointer` field, but only executable consumer is `DodReplayRecorder` through `NativeMemorySentinel.CopySnapshotSources(...)`. That made cold recorder implementation detail look like reusable cross-domain address DTO.
Solution: Make `NativeAllocationSnapshotSource` and `CopySnapshotSources(...)` internal, rename address lane to `SourcePointerValue`, and keep consumption inside Core replay recorder. Also remove unnecessary `public` field access from two private owner structs: `NativeMemorySentinel.NativeAllocationRecord.Pointer` and `GlobalDataVault.MacroDatabasePayloadCacheEntry.Pointer`.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing recorder capture with managed byte arrays was rejected because replay snapshots are native binary dumps. Removing pointer from recorder source was rejected because recorder must copy registered allocation bytes at capture time. Leaving struct public was rejected because no external owner has valid route to retain those addresses.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same snapshot capture cadence and sidecar suppression; high/ultra retain richer native snapshot capture when forced. `GlobalQualityWeight`, save identity, dump header, and authority route are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. This is accessibility hardening; snapshot-time copy remains O(changed allocation bytes), no new allocation/job/hidden completion/shader variant/sibling dependency was introduced.
Problem: After SignalBus payloads stopped publishing raw target addresses, pointer-bearing sentinel validation DTOs were still public types and exposed `TargetMemoryPointer` fields. They are not used outside `MemorySentinelRuntime` and validation job.
Solution: Make `ValidationStateDTO`, `MemorySentinelTargetDTO`, `MemorySentinelResultDTO`, and `MemorySentinelValidationJob` internal. sentinel still stores target addresses while it owns locked validation buffers, but external contracts only see fingerprints and hash/buffer metadata.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing owner-local address table was rejected because hashing and rollback require direct memory access after DataVault locks. Resolving all targets by BufferID inside Burst job was rejected without route card because some targets are mock/mod quarantine spans and native pointer registry sources.
Scalability potential: Validation cadence and lane capacities still scale continuously with quality and configured frequency. No gameplay truth, DTO size, save identity, or SignalBus lane identity changed.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. Accessibility only; Burst job inputs, `[NoAlias]` fields, deterministic mode, and validation work are unchanged.
Problem: `VaultSurgeryEditTests` still asserted deleted pointer-era names for `VaultTransformAlias.MatrixPointer` and `VaultRelocationRecord.OldPointer/NewPointer`. That would either fail compile or preserve false proof artifact after descriptor migration.
Solution: Update assertions to `MatrixBufferId`, `MatrixOffsetBytes`, `MatrixGeneration`, `OldOffsetBytes`, and `NewOffsetBytes` while keeping existing size/alignment tests.
Rejected Alternatives: Deleting assertions was rejected because ARM64 layout proof is required. Restoring old source fields to satisfy tests was rejected because it would reintroduce public process-address routes.
Scalability potential: Runtime behavior is unchanged. gain is proof integrity across low/middle/high/ultra builds.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Editor-only static ABI proof now matches executable source.
Problem: `BlockDescriptor` and `H8AllocationRecord` were public explicit-layout structs with raw address lanes. Even if H8Memory owns those allocations, public accessibility made allocator internals look like cross-domain DTOs.
Solution: Make both structs internal and make their address lanes internal. Keep exact sizes and offsets because H8Memory free/reap and block descriptor validation must still use exact native addresses inside owner. Update editor ABI proof to use reflection so tests can assert internal layout without reopening public surface.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing allocator pointers with descriptor tokens was rejected because allocator must call `UnsafeUtility.Free` on exact addresses and validate owner pointer maps. Leaving structs public was rejected because no external owner has valid route to retain allocator addresses. Adding `InternalsVisibleTo` was rejected as compile-wall expansion.
Scalability potential: Runtime behavior is unchanged across low/middle/high/ultra. This is authority hardening; `GlobalQualityWeight` does not change allocator identity, DTO layout, save identity, or owner route.
Hardware Impact: 0 player-frame cost. Layout remains `BlockDescriptor=40` and `H8AllocationRecord=48`, both 8-byte aligned. No job, allocation, shader variant, sibling dependency, or hot registry polling was introduced.
Problem: `DumpAllocationTableText` and fatal leak binary dumps wrote `record.Pointer.ToInt64()`. That leaks process-local addresses into public diagnostics and preserves same stale-address vocabulary SHINOBU_202 is removing from SignalBus and Vault contracts.
Solution: Replace dumped address lane with `AddressFingerprint`, FNV-1a-style 64-bit fingerprint over pointer, bytes, allocation index, generation, owner, and flags. Bump `FatalLeakDumpVersion` from 3 to 4 so dump readers cannot silently interpret fingerprint as raw pointer. Route teardown waits through `DispatcherJobFence.TryComplete` so H8Memory no longer has direct `.Complete()` calls.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw addresses was rejected because post-mortem correlation needs identity, not reusable process addresses. Dropping lane was rejected because allocation dump rows still need correlation key. Removing teardown waits was rejected because freeing owner memory before scheduled jobs are fenced is unsafe.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay nothing during gameplay; dump generation only happens on fatal leak/diagnostic paths. High/ultra get same blackbox fidelity without exporting retained addresses. No `GlobalQualityWeight`, save identity, DTO truth, or authority route changed.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. Dump-only overhead is six scalar hash mixes per dumped allocation. Direct H8Memory `.Complete()` scan is clean; allowed teardown block is centralized through existing dispatcher fence.
Problem: `HectonArenaAllocator` exposed public `IntPtr` arena base properties, public raw `TryAllocateBytes(...)` methods, and public `NativeArenaSlice<T>.Ptr`/constructor. That lets consumers bypass typed frame-lifetime arena handles and retain process-local addresses.
Solution: Make raw pointer properties, raw byte allocator overloads, slice pointer field, slice constructor, and internal allocation pointer field non-public. Keep public typed arena routes (`NativeArenaArray<T>`, `NativeArenaSlice<T>` ref accessors, owner telemetry) so existing gameplay/editor consumers can work without raw pointer ownership.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping public byte pointers for tests was rejected because tests should not define production API shape. Removing typed arena APIs was rejected because Habitat and editor smoke tests use them as bounded frame-lifetime scratch. Replacing arena scratch with managed arrays was rejected because it violates zero-GC frame discipline.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. Raw allocation code path is unchanged inside Core; public scan for arena `IntPtr`/`byte*`/`void*` exports is clean.
Problem: `GlobalTelemetryBus.Blackbox` exposed public raw byte ring DTO plus public pointer-bearing jobs, but source search found no external consumers. Keeping them public would preserve general raw blackbox memory API outside telemetry owner.
Solution: Make raw ring DTO, NaN sweep job, origin-shift mock fire job, and `TryGetBlackboxRingBuffer(...)` internal. Pointer fields inside internal blackbox source/job structs are internal as well. Public telemetry APIs keep scalar/event publishing and do not expose memory addresses.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping DTO public was rejected because no external route card consumes it. Deleting blackbox telemetry was rejected because fatal forensic capture is still required. Replacing internal pointer job fields with managed arrays was rejected because blackbox path is native and allocation-free.
Scalability potential: Runtime behavior is unchanged across quality levels. Low devices and high/ultra keep same blackbox capacity and dump path; change only blocks external address retention.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Accessibility-only; no new allocation, job, completion, shader variant, sibling dependency, or hot registry polling.
Problem: `H8CacheBTree.TraceBTreeTraversalJob` was public and editor topology window constructed it with public `byte* BasePointer`. pointer is job-local and non-retained, but exposing job as public construction contract keeps raw address route in API surface.
Solution: Make pointer-backed BTree jobs internal and add `H8CacheBTree.ScheduleTraceBTreeTraversal(...)`, public scheduler facade that accepts `NativeArray<byte>`, output arrays, traversal offsets, quality weight, and dependency, then returns scheduled `JobHandle`. editor window still completes explicitly because it is editor diagnostic UI, not runtime phase code.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding blocking `RunTrace...` helper was rejected because it would hide `Complete()`. Leaving public raw job fields was rejected because editor convenience is not reason to publish process-local addresses. Copying BTree bytes into managed arrays was rejected because it violates zero-GC data path expectations.
Scalability potential: Runtime BTree traversal and continuous prefetch quality behavior are unchanged. Low devices keep cheap traversal; high/ultra keep same prefetch cadence behavior through `GlobalQualityWeight`.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. facade only moves pointer extraction into owner scheduler and does not add allocation, completion, shader variant, sibling dependency, or hot registry polling.
Problem: `NativeMemorySentinel.UnregisterPointer(void*)` and `MockUIBuffer.Ptr` were public raw pointer surfaces with no valid cross-domain address ownership story. `MockUIBuffer` had no source consumers.
Solution: Make `NativeMemorySentinel.UnregisterPointer(void*)` internal and make `MockUIBuffer` plus its pointer lane internal. Public sentinel unregister routes remain id/owner/label based.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping general public pointer unregister API was rejected because external callers should not route by process address. Deleting sentinel pointer tracking was rejected because Core still needs owner-local native allocation tracking for diagnostics and replay snapshots. Keeping `MockUIBuffer` public was rejected because it is unused smoke scaffolding.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Accessibility-only; no memory copy, job, completion, or allocator behavior changed.
Problem: `BabelBTreeSearchKernel` and `BabelLoreXorDecryptPointerJob` exposed public raw pointer fields for MMF-backed dictionary bytes and index tables. Search showed pointer decrypt job is scheduled only by `BabelDictionaryStore`; public consumer `LocRegistry` uses non-pointer `BabelLoreXorDecryptJob`.
Solution: Make MMF pointer jobs internal and make their raw pointer lanes internal. Keep public NativeArray decrypt job public to preserve existing localization route.
Rejected Alternatives: Public MMF pointer jobs were rejected because no sibling domain should construct them. Copying MMF bytes for every decrypt was rejected because it doubles bandwidth. Changing `LocRegistry` was rejected because it already uses safer NativeArray job and should not be pulled into this Core pointer pass.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep no-copy MMF path for memory pressure; high/ultra retain same throughput. No `GlobalQualityWeight`, DTO size, save identity, or authority route changed.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. same jobs run with same Burst attributes and `[NoAlias]` raw pointer fields, now hidden inside owner class.
Problem: Several already-contained Core/private types still declared raw pointer members or constructors as public: `UnsafeArenaAllocator.ArenaBlock.Ptr`, `ArenaAllocation(void*)`, `VaultDefragmentationJob.ArenaBase`, `InitializeAlignedBufferJob.BufferPtr`, and AUP rebase job pointer lanes. These were not all externally visible, but they polluted source scans and normalized public pointer language.
Solution: Change those members to internal and make `AUP_StateDTO.ElementAt(void*, int)` internal after exact-call search found no external use. Leave broad pure helper APIs (`H8Crc32.Compute(byte*)`, `MemorySentinelMath` hash helpers, `NativeArenaArray<T>.GetUnsafePtr`, `VoxelUnsafeExtensions`) unchanged pending separate route-carded migration because they have existing consumers or are explicit native-view utilities.
Rejected Alternatives: Blindly flipping every public pointer helper was rejected because it would create compile-wall migration across Core, UI, Networking, Terrain, and tests. Leaving contained private-job fields public was rejected because current task is pointer API surface reduction.
Scalability potential: Runtime behavior is unchanged. Low/middle/high/ultra tiers retain same arena, vault defrag, alignment telemetry, and AUP rebase behavior.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. This is compile-surface and audit-scan reduction only; no allocation, job scheduling, completion, data layout, shader variant, or authority route changed.
Problem: After Loop 266, remaining public pointer surfaces are helper APIs rather than retained DTO fields: `H8Crc32.Compute(byte*)`, `MemorySentinelMath` pointer hash helpers, `NativeArenaArray<T>.GetUnsafePtr/GetUnsafeReadOnlyPtr`, and `VoxelUnsafeExtensions`. Consumer search shows they cross Core, LocRegistry, World terrain paging, Networking rollback contracts, editor telemetry validation, SaveSystem, UI, Physics, Construction, Fauna, and tests.
Solution: Classify them as route-card migration work. Any replacement must add span/NativeArray/descriptor facades first, then migrate consumers domain-by-domain before narrowing raw pointer helper. This preserves compile-wall discipline and avoids breaking hot-path native views.
Rejected Alternatives: Making these helpers internal immediately was rejected because it would break many unrelated domains. Leaving classification implicit was rejected because future audits would rediscover same broad helpers and risk careless sweep.
Scalability potential: Runtime quality behavior is unchanged. Low devices keep no-copy pointer hashing/native views; high/ultra keep same throughput until planned wrapper migration exists.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. This is audit routing only; no source behavior, allocation, job, completion, shader variant, DTO layout, save identity, or authority route changed.
Problem: fresh Core scan found two contained hazards after pointer-helper boundary classification. `ModuloSimulationBucketer` still directly called `_rebalanceHandle.Complete()` in teardown and ready-finalization paths, and public `JobDependencyDTO` exposed offset-0 lane named `JobHandlePtr` even though `SystemDispatcher.CaptureJobHandleBits` stores correlation bits, not reusable process pointer.
Solution: Route bucketer finalization through `DispatcherJobFence.TryComplete(...forceComplete: true)` for teardown and `DispatcherJobFence.TryFinalizeCompleted(...)` for already-completed rebalance jobs. Rename `JobDependencyDTO.JobHandlePtr` to `JobHandleBits` while preserving 32-byte explicit layout and offset 0; update dispatcher writer/reader code and editor layout validator.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving direct `.Complete()` in bucketer was rejected because Core already has central fence helper and SHINOBU_202 is reducing hidden completion surfaces. Removing rebalance synchronization was rejected because Vault-backed job memory cannot be released while handle may still touch it. Keeping `Ptr` in public DTO name was rejected because it contradicts descriptor/fingerprint vocabulary already applied to Vault, Sentinel, H8Memory, and relocation payloads. Changing DTO size or deleting handle-bit telemetry was rejected because diagnostics still need stable correlation without ABI churn.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. `TryFinalizeCompleted` is entered only after `IsCompleted`, so it does not add stall; teardown remains explicit forced fence through central helper. DTO rename is IL/source vocabulary only and keeps `JobDependencyDTO` at 32 bytes.
Problem: After macro payload handle tokenization, public `IMacroDatabaseNativeCacheOwner` and `IMacroDatabaseService` interfaces still accepted `IntPtr source`, `IntPtr destination`, and `IntPtr payload` parameters. implementation copied synchronously, but public route still trained consumers to pass process-local addresses across service boundaries.
Solution: Replace those interface parameters with caller-owned `NativeArray<byte>` buffers and add `MarkDirty<T>(ulong, in T, byte)` for small unmanaged DTO payloads. `GlobalDataVault` copies from/to NativeArray view internally, `H8MacroDatabaseService` wraps MMF payload pointers in transient owner-local `NativeArray<byte>` views before cache store, `H8BridgeFacadeRuntime` uses unmanaged DTO overload, `SaveManager` uses its existing WFC payload buffer directly, and `EcosystemDirector` uses generic typed NativeArray copy route.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `IntPtr` in public service contract was rejected because it contradicts pointer-token/fingerprint migration. Managed byte arrays were rejected because save/world macro payload routes must stay zero-GC. Moving World/Save ownership in this pass was rejected because only call-site signature repair was required to preserve compile wall.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. copy path remains O(payload bytes) and already existed; this edit removes public address retention, not bandwidth. only added work is stack NativeArray view construction around already-valid owner-local memory before synchronous copy.
Problem: `MathGuard` stored static `NativeArray<int>` and `NativeArray<InvalidNumberCounter64>` aliases derived from Vault buffers. They were generation-checked at resolve time, then retained across frames, which is exactly stale-alias pattern SHINOBU_202 is removing.
Solution: Keep only `VaultGenerationHandle<int>`, `VaultGenerationHandle<InvalidNumberCounter64>`, and cached `IDataVault`. `AsParallelWriter` and `DrainInvalidNumberErrors` resolve method-local NativeArray views and then derive transient writer pointer or drain counter reference. `JobFenceManager.Handles` was also narrowed from public to private after exact consumer search found no external access.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping static NativeArray aliases was rejected because Vault relocation/generation churn should invalidate views at boundary. Allocating managed queue was rejected because MathGuard is hot diagnostic ingress. Inventing new JobFenceManager Vault BufferID was rejected because no live consumer exists and route card is required before adding new global lane.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay one O(1) generation resolve per MathGuard writer/drain boundary and avoid stale diagnostic buffers. High/ultra retain same invalid-number blackbox fidelity. No gameplay truth, DTO layout, save identity, or authority route changed.
Hardware Impact: MathGuard adds predictable metadata compare at diagnostic boundary and removes persistent alias risk; no GC, no new job, no hidden completion, no shader variant, and no sibling assembly dependency were introduced. JobFenceManager visibility hardening costs 0 runtime microseconds.
Problem: `H8Crc32.Compute(byte*, int)` was public and used by Core data readers, editor baker, localization, and terrain streaming. CRC validation is valid no-copy operation, but exposing pointer overload as public route made sibling domains pass process-local addresses into Core helper.
Solution: Add public `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` and `NativeArray<byte>` overloads and make raw `byte*` overload internal. Migrate `StaticDataStore`, `BabelDictionaryStore`, `H8DataBaker`, `LocRegistry`, and `TerrainChunkPagerRuntime` to span route. MMF-backed readers still create transient spans over owner-local memory for synchronous hashing.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping public pointer overload was rejected because it is convenience pointer API, not ownership contract. Managed byte arrays or copies were rejected because MMF/static payload validation must stay no-copy. Changing static-data, Babel, localization, or terrain payload formats was rejected because hazard was API shape, not binary layout.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same sequential CRC bandwidth and avoid extra memory copies. Middle/high/ultra retain identical payload validation fidelity; no `GlobalQualityWeight`, save identity, Data Monolith layout, shader ABI, or SignalBus route changed.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. CRC remains O(payload bytes). `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` over existing pointer/array is stack-only and does not allocate; raw pointer loop remains owner-internal.
Problem: `MemorySentinelMath.ComputeXXHash3Folded(void*)`, `ComputeXXHash3Full64(void*)`, and `HasModPrefix(byte*)` were public. Sentinel validation still needs owner-local raw target memory while buffers are locked, but networking/editor callers do not need public Core pointer helper.
Solution: Add public `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` and `NativeArray<byte>` overloads for folded/full hash and mod-prefix checks; make raw pointer overloads internal. Migrate `RollbackNetcodeMath.HashExactBytes` to publish public span route and keep its pointer route internal. Migrate telemetry dump validator to public span hash route.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing pointer hashing from sentinel internals was rejected because validation jobs hash locked native memory. Copying rollback/dump bytes before hashing was rejected because it adds bandwidth and potential GC pressure. Keeping public raw hash helpers was rejected because byte-view facades provide same no-copy behavior with narrower contract.
Hardware Impact: 0 hash-loop cost change. Boundary span construction is stack-only; no allocation, job, hidden completion, shader variant, or sibling assembly reference was introduced.
Problem: `VoxelUnsafeExtensions` publicly exposed raw byte pointer access/write helpers, and exact source search found no executable consumer. Keeping unused public byte pointer write helpers weakens pointer-quarantine audit surface.
Solution: Make class and its methods internal. This preserves Core-local emergency utility while removing it from public contracts.
Rejected Alternatives: Deleting file during this pass was rejected because source deletion is higher-risk cleanup than accessibility hardening. Leaving it public was rejected because no caller proves need.
Scalability potential: Runtime behavior is unchanged across all tiers because no executable source consumer exists.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Visibility-only; no DTO, BufferID, job, allocation, shader, save, or SignalBus behavior changed.
Problem: `VaultGenerationHandle<T>`, obsolete pointer-free `VaultBufferHandle<T>`, and `VaultSliceHandle<T>` used `[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential, Pack = 4, Size = ...)]`. Their current fields are all 4-byte scalars, so present byte size was not broken, but explicit pack setting would silently under-align any future 8-byte descriptor lane on ARM64.
Solution: Remove `Pack = 4` and keep `LayoutKind.Sequential` plus explicit `Size = 16/16/32`. Existing field order remains `uint/uint/uint/uint` for 16-byte handles and `uint/uint/uint/uint/int/int/uint/uint` for 32-byte slice descriptor. `GlobalDataVault.ValidateAbiLayout()` remains cold boot proof for size.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving `Pack = 4` was rejected as future ARM64 footgun. Switching to explicit field offsets was rejected because these descriptors contain only 4-byte scalar lanes, and current sequential layout with explicit size is simpler while preserving ABI. Adding new padding fields was rejected because final sizes already land exactly on 16 and 32 bytes.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. This removes ABI trap without adding allocations, jobs, hidden completions, branch work, or memory bandwidth.
Problem: `UIStateStore` read accessors called `EnsureInitialized()`, which can allocate five persistent `NativeArray` blocks from visual/read paths. This violates rule that `Get*`, `TryGet*`, and read helpers stay pure and do not allocate or mutate owner state.
Solution: Reads now return default, false, or caller fallback while store is cold. Write/boot paths still call `EnsureInitialized()` and own allocation. Rollback read/write restoration returns false when no history backing store exists.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping read-time allocation was rejected because presenter polling UI state could become owner of persistent memory. Moving allocation to every caller was rejected because ownership belongs to UI store owner phase. Managed fallback buffers were rejected because store is native and zero-GC.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid accidental cold allocations from visual polls. Middle/high/ultra retain identical UI fidelity once owner has initialized store. No `GlobalQualityWeight`, save identity, SignalBus layout, shader ABI, or gameplay authority route changed.
Hardware Impact: Removes five possible cold persistent NativeArray allocations from read routes. Hot reads remain O(1); cold reads become immediate false/default.
Problem: `HomeostasisBrain.GlobalHardwareMetrics` returned mutable `NativeArray<float>` and resolved through helper that can allocate/acquire Vault lane when handle is cold.
Solution: Return `NativeArray<float>.ReadOnly` and add `TryReadHardwareMetrics`, which requires existing generation handle and uses `IDataVault.TryReadHandle`. allocation/acquire route remains private to initialization and update logic.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping mutable readback was rejected because external code could write hardware metrics without owner. Calling `TryResolveOrAcquire` from property was rejected because property read must not grow Vault buffers. Returning managed copy was rejected because it adds GC/bandwidth.
Hardware Impact: 0 hot cost increase; read property avoids allocation and only returns read-only native view when existing handle is valid.
Problem: `RollbackNetcodeBufferAccess.FrameSnapshotAt(...)` exposed public raw ref over native snapshot array. Source search showed only `StateSnapshotJob` in same file uses it.
Solution: Make helper class and method internal. Rollback jobs keep same in-place snapshot write, but sibling assemblies no longer receive public raw ref accessor.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving helper public was rejected because rollback snapshot memory is owned by netcode runtime and StateRingBuffer route. Inlining into job was rejected as noisier without changing behavior.
Scalability potential: No quality behavior change. This is contract narrowing only; deterministic rollback hashing and snapshot layout are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. No allocation, copy, branch, job, completion, or layout change.
Problem: `AupPrecisionVaultViews` and `MockEntityArrays` exposed public mutable `NativeArray` fields. Search found they are used only in their owner files, so public exposure provided no cross-domain contract value.
Solution: Make view structs, mutable lanes, and public ensure methods internal. Public AUP scheduling/dump/tuning methods remain intact and still resolve Vault-backed buffers locally.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping public mutable views was rejected because it lets future callers retain or mutate owner-local Vault lanes directly. Converting all fields to private properties was rejected because these are internal job-staging structs, not external DTOs. Moving AUP data to managed arrays was rejected for zero-GC and AUP precision reasons.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged. AUP localization and origin-shift jobs still consume continuous quality where already implemented; only construction surface is narrower.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Same NativeArrays, Vault handles, Burst jobs, `[NoAlias]` routes, and telemetry rings.
Problem: `ConnectionSplineBatchRenderer.BatchState` is private nested class, but it declared its native buffers and other mutable fields as `public`. That is not external API leak, but it pollutes public native-view scans and normalizes mutable public field style in Core source.
Solution: Change batch fields to internal implementation lanes. Rendering behavior, shader upload, dictionary registry, and native buffer allocation remain unchanged.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting this renderer to DataVault lanes was rejected because it is visual batcher with local GPU upload buffers and would be larger ownership redesign. Leaving fields public was rejected because scan hygiene matters for SHINOBU_202 enforcement.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. No allocation, draw call, shader, job, SignalBus, or DTO layout changed.
Problem: `HardwareThermalService.ThermalSeverity` returned read-only view but called `TryResolveThermalSeverity`, which can allocate/acquire `BufferID.HardwareThermalSeverity` when generation handle is cold. That makes read property capable of becoming native memory owner.
Solution: Add `TryReadThermalSeverity` and route property through `IDataVault.TryReadHandle`. existing allocation path remains inside owner cold paths: `EnsureNativeState` and `SampleAndApplyCold` still use `TryResolveThermalSeverity` to create/update one-byte proof lane.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping allocation inside property was rejected because read accessors must not grow Vault buffers. Returning managed byte copy was rejected because interface already exposes native read-only view and copying adds unnecessary bandwidth. Removing shared severity buffer was rejected because policy/debug consumers need existing unmanaged proof artifact.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid accidental cold allocation from policy/UI reads. Middle/high/ultra retain same continuous thermal policy behavior and `GlobalQualityWeight` influence; only readback authority changed.
Hardware Impact: Hot reads remain O(1): one handle validity check plus `TryReadHandle`. Cold reads now return default instead of allocating Vault lane. No GC, no job, no `.Complete()`, no DTO layout change, no SignalBus route change, and no shader variant change.
Problem: `SignalBus<T>.TryReadFrameSnapshot` and `ModuloSimulationBucketer` public readbacks used `TryResolveHandle` through local resolve helpers. Those paths were not allocating, but verb collapsed reader and owner-write semantics in code that serves public `SnapshotCount`, `SnapshotGeneration`, `TryConsumeFrame`, and `EntityBuckets` reads.
Solution: Route signal snapshot reads through `IDataVault.TryReadHandle`; keep `TryOpenFrameSnapshotForOwnerWrite` on `TryResolveHandle`. Add `ReadEntityBuckets`/`TryReadVaultBuffer` for `ModuloSimulationBucketer.IsInitialized` and `EntityBuckets`, leaving owner setup/rebalance/job helpers on existing mutable resolve path.
Rejected Alternatives: Renaming or removing `TryResolveHandle` was rejected because owner write phases use it broadly. Copying snapshots or buckets into managed arrays was rejected because routes must stay zero-GC. Removing `IDataVault.CreateAlias` in same pass was rejected because exact executable search found no live consumer, but archived mandate history documents it as deliberate alias-accountability API; it needs route-carded deprecation, not blind deletion.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. `TryReadHandle` performs same O(1) descriptor/generation validation without allocation, job scheduling, completion, layout mutation, shader change, or authority-route change.
Problem: `DispatcherJobContext` is public schedule contract used across many domains, but it exposed two mutable native arrays: `MockTimeDilationSignals` and `JobDependencyTelemetry`. Exact source search showed external systems read scalar `Frame`/`ActiveBucket`, while native arrays are assigned by `SystemDispatcher` and consumed by Core default mock scheduling only.
Solution: Make two native array fields internal and keep `Frame`/`ActiveBucket` public. This preserves cross-domain schedule contract while removing public mutable Vault views from unrelated systems.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing `DispatcherJobContext` or making it private was rejected because public `IDispatcherSystem.ScheduleSimulation` depends on it. Exposing read-only wrappers was rejected because external systems have no live need for those arrays. Moving telemetry out of dispatcher-owned Vault buffers was rejected as unrelated to pointer/API surface defect.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Accessibility-only; no allocation, job, completion, BufferID, DTO layout, or SignalBus route changed.
Problem: `SignalThreadLocalWriteContext.Bytes` and `Headers` used `[NativeDisableParallelForRestriction]` with detailed stride-safety comments but lacked `[NoAlias]`, so Burst could still conservatively treat arrays as aliasing other native fields passed through producer jobs.
Solution: Add `[NoAlias]` to both fields. layout invariant remains: one worker index writes one fixed byte slice and one 64-byte header row; commit reads only after producer dependency.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing scratch buffer with `NativeQueue<T>.ParallelWriter` was rejected because it reintroduces CAS contention. Per-thread managed objects were rejected because they are not Burst-compatible and violate zero-GC. Adding atomics to every write was rejected because fixed-stride partitioning already eliminates false sharing for normal path.
Hardware Impact: 0 functional cost. This is compiler alias evidence for existing data-local batch work; no new memory, no schedule/readback loop, no `.Complete()`, no layout change, and no shader variant.
Problem: `SignalThreadLocalScratchpad` public reader APIs returned read-only signal/telemetry/tuning data, but internally opened same mutable `TryResolve` route used by owner write phases. route was not allocating after initialization, but public `TryGet*` surface still conflated consumer readback with writer access.
Solution: Add local `TryRead` helper using `IDataVault.TryReadHandle` and route `TryGetCommittedSignalsReadOnly`, `TryGetLatestTelemetry`, `TryGetTelemetryReadOnly`, `TryGetThreadHeader`, and `TryGetTuning` through it. Split committed-signal access into `TryOpenCommittedSignalsBufferForOwner` and `TryReadCommittedSignalsBuffer`.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing all scratchpad resolves was rejected because producer, commit, mutation, crash-dump initialization, and CSV load scratch paths require mutable or owner-initializing access. Managed copies were rejected because diagnostics and editor overlays must stay zero-GC. Replacing thread-local scratchpad with `NativeQueue<T>` was rejected because fixed-stride Vault scratch is deliberate Dear Lie that avoids CAS-heavy signal ingress.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep cheap read-only diagnostics and fixed-stride signal ingress. Middle/high/ultra retain same committed signal, telemetry, and tuning fidelity; continuous quality/capacity behavior is unchanged.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. `TryReadHandle` keeps O(1) generation validation and returns existing native view without allocation, job scheduling, completion, DTO layout change, SignalBus route change, or shader variant.
Problem: `JobSchedulingProfileCatalog.TryResolveBatchBounds` is public read query used by `JobAdmissionScheduleExtensions`, but it opened `SystemDispatcherJobSchedulingProfiles` through `TryResolveHandle`. lane is hydrated during cold boot, not by admission readers.
Solution: Switch only lookup path to `IDataVault.TryReadHandle`. Keep `LoadColdBootProfiles` on `EnsureGenerationHandle` plus mutable resolve because it writes parsed CSV/default rows into owner lane.
Rejected Alternatives: Renaming public method was rejected because API name is already consumed by admission code and defect is internal route. Managed profile copies were rejected because scheduler path must stay zero-GC. Allowing read lookup to create/grow lane was rejected because dispatcher cold boot owns profile hydration.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same admission batch bounds with no allocation. Middle/high/ultra retain profile-driven parallel batch sizing; continuous quality/cadence decisions are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. Same O(profile count) scan and same DTO layout; only handle verb changed from mutable resolve to read validation.
Problem: `IDataVault.TryReadHandle<T>` was documented as read route but returned mutable `NativeArray<T>`. Broad source search shows method is used across many sibling domains, so changing its signature immediately would force project-wide compile-wall event and risk unrelated agents' work.
Solution: Add `TryReadOnlyHandle<T>` returning `NativeArray<T>.ReadOnly` and document `TryReadHandle<T>` as legacy mutable transitional route. Migrate SHINOBU_202-owned public readbacks to new route: hardware metrics, thermal severity, simulation buckets, scheduler profile lookup, SignalWarden profiles, committed signals, telemetry, thread headers, and tuning.
Rejected Alternatives: Changing `TryReadHandle<T>` signature globally was rejected because it crosses Atmosphere, AI, Construction, Physics, Rendering, SaveSystem, UI, VFX, World, and Editor call sites. Managed read copies were rejected for zero-GC. Removing `TryReadHandle<T>` was rejected because staged route-card migration is required.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep zero-copy readback and avoid accidental mutation through newly migrated consumers. Middle/high/ultra retain identical telemetry, scheduler, and signal fidelity; quality curves and BufferIDs are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. new method reuses O(1) generation validation and returns read-only native wrapper without allocation, job scheduling, completion, layout mutation, or shader change.
Problem: `IMockContractImplementation.GetStateRef` returned mutable ref to static `MockDomainState` from read-looking accessor. This violates read-accessor purity and trains contract-only mock code toward global mutable state exposure.
Solution: Change interface and implementation to return `ref readonly MockDomainState`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping mutable ref was rejected because no executable consumer requires mutation through that accessor. Returning managed object wrapper was rejected because contract is blittable smoke-test state.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. 32-byte explicit DTO layout, bootstrap route, and assembly routing remain unchanged.
Problem: `NativeArenaArray<T>` exposed public `GetUnsafePtr()` and `GetUnsafeReadOnlyPtr()` raw process pointers. Exact executable C# search found no direct callers. separate `AsNativeArray()` mutable view is used by Gameplay, Physics, and Habitat systems, so flipping it in same pass would cross ownership boundaries.

Rejected Alternatives: Keeping unused public raw pointer methods was rejected because they are unnecessary pointer escape routes. Internalizing `AsNativeArray()` immediately was rejected because it would break real cross-domain consumers. Replacing arena arrays with persistent Vault buffers was rejected because this allocator is frame-lifetime scratch, not cross-domain persistent owner.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Visibility-only; no allocation, copy, job, completion, layout, shader, or SignalBus behavior changed.
Problem: `HectonRollbackNetcodeRuntime` public diagnostics returned value copies or read-only views, but local `TryReadOwned` helper still opened legacy mutable `IDataVault.TryReadHandle<T>` route. That preserved mutable view exposure inside readback-only code.

Owner write paths remain on `TryResolveOwned`; bound rollback simulation buffers remain mutable because jobs write or snapshot authoritative state.
Rejected Alternatives: Changing all rollback buffer resolution to read-only was rejected because prediction, remote input injection, Merkle reconciliation, and snapshot jobs mutate owner-owned lanes. Managed diagnostic copies were rejected because rollback telemetry must stay zero-GC. Changing broad legacy `TryReadHandle<T>` signature was rejected because that is project-wide compile-wall migration.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra rollback behavior is unchanged. Diagnostic visibility can scale independently, but `GlobalQualityWeight` does not change rollback BufferIDs, DTO layout, lockstep identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. helper still performs one O(1) generation validation and returns existing native wrapper. No allocation, copy, job scheduling, completion, shader variant, DTO layout mutation, or sibling assembly dependency was added.
Problem: `BurstTokenBucketJobAdmissionService.GetLaneBudgetMs` and `GetEstimatedCostMs` are public read queries, but they reused mutable resolve helpers for budget, job-hash, and EWMA cost tables. Refill, admission, and completion updates require those mutable helpers, but read queries do not.
Solution: Add `ReadLaneBudgets`, `ReadJobHashes`, and `ReadEwmaCosts` helpers that use `IDataVault.TryReadOnlyHandle<T>`. Route `GetLaneBudgetMs` and `GetEstimatedCostMs` through read-only tables and read-only cost resolver. Keep `ResolveLaneBudgets`, `ResolveBaseRefill`, `ResolveJobHashes`, `ResolveEwmaCosts`, and `ResolveBlackbox` mutable for owner mutation paths.
Rejected Alternatives: Converting all admission table access to read-only was rejected because refill debits/refills budgets and completion updates EWMA state. Copying budget/cost tables to managed arrays was rejected for zero-GC. Renaming public interface was rejected because behavior defect is internal route authority, not caller semantics.

Adding hot-path per-resolve offset checks was rejected because field layout is invariant and should fail at boot. Converting internal rows to public for verification was rejected as API surface expansion.

Problem: `VaultSovereigntyTelemetry.TryDump` could call `EnsureRing`, which allocates/grows ring before dumping, and diagnostic reads in alignment telemetry still used mutable views in some read paths.

Rejected Alternatives: Allocating during dump was rejected because dump/read routes are not owners. Returning mutable arrays for diagnostics was rejected because read accessors must not expose write authority.
Hardware Impact: 0 steady-frame cost. Crash/diagnostic route avoids allocation/growth and uses O(1) generation validation.
## Decision 345 - Transitional mutable read API cannot become warning wall
Problem: Marking `IDataVault.TryReadHandle<T>` obsolete would produce warnings in many sibling domains that are outside SHINOBU_202 ownership. If warnings are treated as errors, this Vault pass becomes compile-wall generator.
Solution: Keep `TryReadHandle<T>` source-compatible and documented as legacy mutable read-validation route. Enforce SHINOBU_202-owned surfaces through scanners and migrations instead of global attribute.
Rejected Alternatives: Obsoleting method now was rejected as cross-domain warning churn. Removing it was rejected because staged migration is not finished. Changing its return type was rejected as broad compile break.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime cost. Compile-wall risk reduced; no player code path changed.

# Rationale_SHINOBU_260
Status: POLISH PASS LOOP 25 NO-PY STATIC VERIFIED / TASK 12 BLOCKED BY DEPENDENCY / LOOP 22 BUILD PASS / LOOP 25 REBUILD NOT LAUNCHED BY USER PY/BUILD DISCIPLINE
## Decision 001: Resolve Duplicate SHINOBU_260 Prompt By ID And Role
Problem: `Docs/Tasks/CURRENT_BATCH.md` contains stale first `<AGENT_PROMPT id="SHINOBU_260">` for vocal synthesis and later correct `<AGENT_PROMPT id="SHINOBU_260" role="CREST_VERSION_QUARANTINE_DIRECTOR">`.
Solution: Select block matching both user-stated ID and role. Archive stale vocal status/rationale/log to `Docs/Archive/Batch_SHINOBU_260_VOCAL_STALE_20260521/` before replacing active memory files.
Rejected Alternatives: ID-only first-match extraction was rejected because it routes work into wrong domain. Ignoring duplicate was rejected because context compression would re-poison future iterations.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unaffected at runtime; this is compile-wall and agent-memory hygiene.
Hardware Impact: Prevents unnecessary C# recompiles and third-party asset churn on developer hardware. Estimated saving: seconds to minutes of avoided wrong-domain rebuild/import work.
## Decision 002: Treat Crest As Toxic Third-Party Leaf Until Proven Otherwise
Problem: Crest 4/5 coexistence can create namespace collisions, duplicated shader properties, GUID drift, and direct first-party references into third-party assemblies.
Solution: All investigation and future edits route toward physical archive, Unity-invisible quarantine for inactive Crest versions, strict asmdef leaf isolation, and first-party access only through unmanaged ocean kinematics contracts.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving both Crest versions visible to Unity was rejected because it preserves compile collisions and shader import ambiguity. Direct references from Hecton8.Core or Hecton8.Physics were rejected because they make third-party API churn core compile-wall trigger.
Scalability potential: Low devices use mock/deferred/cached ocean sampling when Crest is unavailable or over budget. Middle uses bounded delayed query batches. High/Ultra can allow richer internal Crest shader/compute work behind same contract without changing core dependencies.
Hardware Impact: Expected low-end i3/MX350 gain is primarily iteration and import stability; runtime savings come from deferred/capped ocean query batches, estimated 100-1000 microseconds avoided when synchronous Crest sampling would otherwise stall physics.
## Decision 003: Quarantine Crest 5 Outside Unity Visibility
Problem: active repository had Crest 4 in `Assets/Crest` and Crest 5 in `Packages/com.waveharmonic.crest`, with `Packages/packages-lock.json` still pinning embedded Crest 5 package even though `manifest.json` did not list it.
Solution: Created `Tools/Crest_Baseline_Archiver.py`, generated compressed backups under `.gitignore`-protected `Docs/Archive/Crest_Baseline_Backup/`, moved Crest 5 and Crest 5 first-party bridge/migration/parity scripts with their `.meta` files under `Docs/Archive/Crest_Version_Quarantine/`, and removed stale `com.waveharmonic.crest` lock entry through JSON parsing.
Rejected Alternatives: `Assets/~Quarantine_Crest5` was rejected because it remains under Unity's asset tree and violates user's "outside Unity visibility" constraint. Deleting Crest 5 outright was rejected because restore must remain possible from bit-for-bit backup.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra runtime behavior is unchanged; this removes compile/import volatility so later hardware-specific ocean LOD work happens behind one Crest 4 donor boundary.
Hardware Impact: Runtime frame gain is 0 microseconds because this is editor/build hygiene. Developer hardware gain is expected in seconds of avoided package import/domain reload work and lower chance of forced full recompiles on i3/MX350-class machines.
## Decision 004: Confine Crest To Dedicated Bridge Assemblies
Problem: `Hecton8.Plugins`, `Hecton8.Editor`, and `Hecton8.Project.Editor` referenced Crest and WaveHarmonic assemblies directly, so unrelated first-party changes inherited third-party ocean churn.
Solution: Created `Hecton8.Crest.Bridge` and `Hecton8.Crest.Bridge.Editor`, moved Crest-dependent render validator under bridge editor folder, removed Crest/WaveHarmonic references from shared asmdefs, and set Crest 4 asmdefs to `autoReferenced=false`.
