Clamping in managed callers was rejected because SignalBus/Vault data must be defended at mathematical kernel boundary.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra finite behavior is unchanged. Faulted scalar inputs collapse to safe defaults or zeroed projection without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, quality schema, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Adds finite checks to fixed one-row integrator and capped 32-signal evaluator. Expected cost is below 1 us on i3/MX350-class hardware; it prevents scalar NaN propagation into projection matrices and telemetry hashes.
## Decision 038 - Raw Signal Scalar Sanitizer
Problem: `math.max` can hide malformed raw signal scalar when paired scalar is finite, so earlier finite gate could miss evidence of NaN radius/severity lane before attenuation.
Solution: Add explicit `SanitizeSignalScalar` and `MaxFinite` helpers inside `EvaluateCameraTraumaJob`; every raw impact/seismic/mock scalar is finite-checked before any `math.max`, `math.abs`, amplitude sum, or radius max.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting `math.max` behavior across Burst backends was rejected because NaN selection semantics are not telemetry contract. Sanitizing after derived severity was rejected because it loses which raw lane was malformed.
Scalability potential: Finite low/middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged. Malformed raw SignalBus scalar lanes are now flagged and replaced with neutral scalar contribution without altering authority, DTO layout, or quality schema.
Hardware Impact: Adds fixed finite checks to 32-signal cap. Expected cost stays below 1 us; gain is deterministic black-box evidence and no NaN entering severity/radius expressions.
## Decision 039 - Bounded Fault-Proven Telemetry Lane
Problem: Static audit found three remaining failure surfaces: finite but oversized manual/directional vectors could overflow `lengthsq` after component finite checks; shake catch could disable presentation without writing 300-frame black-box dump; and signed telemetry cursor overflow could produce negative ring index during long endurance runs.
Solution: Clamp manual direction to finite presentation envelope before `lengthsq`, clamp directional memory/timer to normalized bounds before blend/integration, route shake exceptions through `FailClosedProceduralCameraJuiceFault()` with forced telemetry row and dump request, and convert telemetry cursor/frame/dump cursor lanes to unsigned modulo with dump header version `4`.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying on final projection sanitation was rejected because `huge * rsqrt(inf)` can corrupt state before output gate. Keeping broad catch that only logs was rejected because it violates black-box rule. Keeping signed cursors was rejected because 100-hour target cannot accept overflow-dependent negative indexing.
Scalability potential: Finite low/middle/high/ultra behavior remains continuous. Later Loop 28 restored Math-LOD tap admission so low quality can physically skip zero-weight Simplex taps while preserving smooth visual amplitude; quality still changes presentation fidelity/cost only, not DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Normal finite frame adds bounded vector clamps and continuous high/ultra noise taps; expected camera-only cost remains below 0.1 ms suspicion threshold but requires Unity Profiler proof. Fault frames now pay cold dump I/O only after failure and preserve forensic evidence instead of silently disabling route.
## Decision 040 - Vault Tuning Radius Route
Problem: CSV/profile hydration updated `CameraJuiceTuningDTO.LowTierRadiusMeters` and `UltraRadiusMeters`, but `EvaluateCameraTraumaJob` still used hard-coded `32..120m` radius curve for AUP attenuation. Designer-authored radius values were therefore not part of actual runtime impulse falloff.
Solution: Pass existing Vault tuning row into `EvaluateCameraTraumaJob` as `[ReadOnly, NoAlias] NativeArray<CameraJuiceTuningDTO>.ReadOnly`, finite-gate low/ultra radius fields, and lerp attenuation radius from Vault values with safe `32..120m` fallbacks. Keep smooth quality weights for visual continuity.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping constant radii was rejected because it made cold CSV bridge partial. Adding new SignalBus or BufferID for radius was rejected because tuning row already owns that presentation fact. hardware-tier branch was rejected; later Loop 28 uses quality-weight Math LOD admission only.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra now use authored radius curves continuously through `GlobalQualityWeight`, while noise richness remains scalar-blended. Quality still changes presentation fidelity only; it does not change DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, rollback identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Adds one read-only tuning-row load and finite checks in capped evaluator, below 1 us. It does not buy ALU savings; it fixes authoring truth and avoids another route for profile radius.
## Decision 041 - Smooth Visual Weight With Math LOD Tap Admission
Problem: Loop 26 removed high/ultra quality branch gates to avoid feature-pop semantics, but that made low-quality frames still evaluate all six `noise.snoise` taps. That violates explicit ALU shedding requirement for weak/mobile devices.
Solution: Keep smooth visual weights, move first high-octave onset to quality `0.30`, and admit Simplex taps only when their smooth weight is nonzero. Below `GlobalQualityWeight < 0.30`, integrator executes only damped sine/triangle math. Ultra grit taps are admitted only above smooth ultra window.
Rejected Alternatives: Always computing all taps was rejected because it burns mobile ALU for zero visual contribution. hardware-tier boolean was rejected because it would change behavior by device class instead of by continuous quality scalar. Abrupt amplitude steps were rejected because they would cause visible feature popping.
Scalability potential: Low tier pays no Simplex cost and keeps readable impact feedback; middle tier admits high taps gradually; high/ultra add grit with smooth amplitude. Quality changes presentation fidelity/cost only and never changes DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, rollback identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: On i3/MX350/Quest-class devices at quality below `0.30`, six `noise.snoise` evaluations are skipped per camera juice frame. Expected saving: 3-12 us depending Burst backend and CPU.
## Decision 042 - Unity Time Runtime Eviction
Problem: Static subagent audit found `Time.realtimeSinceStartup` and `Time.time` in SHINOBU_354 runtime owner for development budget logging and slow dependency cadence. They were not Burst shake math and not `Time.deltaTime`, but they weakened strict no-Unity-Time runtime proof.
Solution: Replace dev frame-budget measurement with `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp()` and throttle logs using dt-driven owner cooldown. Replace `Time.time` slow dependency cadence with deterministic slow-tick countdown.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Unity `Time` because code was non-critical was rejected; owner file is forensic surface for this mandate. Polling dependencies every SlowTick was rejected because it would increase cold dependency work cadence. coroutine/timer was rejected because it would reintroduce managed scheduling.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra camera trauma behavior is unchanged. dependency refresh cadence is now tick-count based and quality-independent; visual scalability remains in Burst projection route.
Hardware Impact: Runtime savings are negligible. Structural gain is deterministic proof: scoped SHINOBU_354 runtime files now have zero `Time.` hits, and development timing no longer depends on Unity global clock state.
## Decision 043 - Burst Budget Fault Artifact
Problem: 300-frame telemetry ring recorded `BurstExecutionMicroseconds`, but frame above 0.1 ms suspicion threshold did not set explicit fault bit or request dump after current row was written.
Solution: Add `CameraJuiceFlagBurstBudgetExceeded` plus fixed `CameraJuiceBurstBudgetMicroseconds=100` threshold. `RunProceduralCameraJuice` marks projection DTO after synchronous Burst section, and `RecordCameraJuiceTelemetry` services pending dump request after writing row so offending frame is in `Dump_SHINOBU_354.bin`.
Rejected Alternatives: Scheduling two tiny jobs and completing them for same-frame projection was rejected again because that would add hidden fence. Dumping before `RecordCameraJuiceTelemetry` was rejected because it can miss over-budget frame.
Scalability potential: Low quality already sheds Simplex taps through Math LOD admission; high/ultra may intentionally spend more ALU, but any section above 100 us becomes black-box proof artifact instead of silent drift.
Hardware Impact: Normal frames add one scalar compare and one rare flag write. Fault frames pay cold dump I/O only after telemetry capture; expected normal-frame cost is below 1 us.
## Decision 044 - Sidecar Audit Closure: Temporal Admission, Vault-Only AUP, Fault-Frame Dump
Problem: Sidecar static audit found four concrete surfaces after Loop 28: hard quality threshold tap gates could still be interpreted as binary quality switches; invalid native state dumped before sanitized fault values were copied into `_cameraJuiceLast*` and recorded; `TryResolvePlayerCameraJuiceAup` still had hot fallback to `_playerMovement.CurrentAup`; and OOP scanner missed hot `transform.localRotation` / `transform.localEulerAngles` shake routes.
Solution: Replace hard `math.step(qualityThreshold, quality)` tap gates with deterministic `TemporalAdmission01(sequence, salt, smoothWeight)`, so expected Simplex ALU scales with continuous quality weight and no hard quality threshold exists. Remove Gameplay AUP fallback; procedural route now reads only cached read-only `PlayerKinematicState` Vault row and otherwise fails closed. Move invalid native state dump ordering so sanitized state/projection is copied into `_cameraJuiceLast*`, recorded into telemetry ring, then dumped. Extend scanner to cover hot local rotation and local Euler mutations.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Gameplay fallback was rejected because it creates direct sibling dependency in hot AUP route. Dumping before telemetry record was rejected because it can omit fault frame. Keeping hard quality thresholds was rejected because project forbids binary quality switches even when visual amplitude is smooth. Ignoring local rotation/euler scans was rejected because camera shake can be rotational.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra presentation richness is now admitted by deterministic temporal sampling against smooth weights. Weak devices see lower expected Simplex cost; high/ultra devices converge toward every-frame high/grit taps. Quality still cannot alter DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, rollback identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Low-quality frames skip Simplex taps in proportion to smooth admission weight instead of always paying six taps or crossing hard quality threshold. Expected saving remains profiler-dependent; static path now has no hard `math.step(0.30/0.65, quality)` gates and no hot Gameplay AUP fallback.
## Decision 045 - Exact Zero Temporal Admission
Problem: `TemporalAdmission01` used `dither <= weight`, so mathematically zero smooth weight could still admit Simplex tap when 24-bit dither value was exactly zero. visual term was multiplied by zero later, but low-tier ALU proof was not exact.
Solution: Add explicit `weight <= 0f -> 0f` and `weight >= 1f -> 1f` exits, then use `dither < weight` for middle range.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying on rare 1-in-16,777,216 dither leak was rejected because mandate requires mathematical proof, not statistical excuse. Always computing taps and masking contribution was rejected because it burns mobile ALU for no visible output.
Scalability potential: Low tier now executes exactly damped sine/triangle only when smooth admission weight is zero. Middle/high/ultra still use deterministic temporal admission against continuous quality scalar.
Hardware Impact: Normal overhead is two scalar comparisons inside helper. Low-quality zero-weight frames now have hard guarantee of zero Simplex evaluations from this route.
## Decision 046 - Reproducible UX Scanner Report Fields
Problem: `OOP_CameraShake_Scanner` had been extended to catch hot local rotation/euler mutations, but future editor menu run would replace shared SHINOBU_354 UX object without `cameraRelevantFiles`, status, burst-budget proof, or concise manual proof field. current JSON on disk was correct, but tool was not reproducible source of that proof.
Solution: Add `cameraRelevantFiles` counter and emit `status`, `burstBudgetProof`, and `manualProof` in editor scanner output. scanner still preserves adjacent agents through shared multi-agent envelope and remains zero-dependency editor-only code.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving JSON as hand-maintained report was rejected because scanner is Task 19 proof artifact. Adding Roslyn or new editor asmdef was rejected because lexical scanner is enough for this bounded camera-shake inquisition and avoids compile graph expansion.
Scalability potential: Runtime low/middle/high/ultra camera trauma behavior is unchanged. This improves proof reproducibility only; runtime quality scalar still governs presentation fidelity and expected Simplex admission.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost is 0 us because scanner is `#if UNITY_EDITOR`. Editor scan cost gains one integer counter and few JSON fields; no player frame impact.
Source lines scanned 323; retained 277; overflow-important omitted 0.

Rationale_SHINOBU_355.md
# Rationale_SHINOBU_355
## Decision 01: Reuse Existing KCC Runtime Surface
Problem: repository already contains `HydrodynamicKccRuntime`, KCC DTOs, KCC Vault handles, rollback bytes, environment SDF buffers, and editor-only `HeadlessKccSmokeTests.cs` prototype. Creating new standalone runtime owner would duplicate KCC authority.
Solution: Integrate smoke-test Burst DTOs/jobs through partial `HydrodynamicKccRuntime` file and keep editor facade code as caller/reporting shell only.
Rejected Alternatives: new `HectonKccSmokeTester` MonoBehaviour or runtime manager would add second KCC ownership path and widen assembly dependencies.
Scalability potential: Low uses flat 32/64-byte DTO lanes and bounded history; Middle/High/Ultra keep same authority math and increase only diagnostic retention/report richness.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids scene load, Transform sync, and Unity Physics scene stepping; expected saving versus GameObject/PlayMode movement sweep is >100 us per 10,000-frame smoke pass frame equivalent on editor hardware, not claimed as profiler proof.
## Decision 02: Keep Hot Loop in Native/Burst, Reports in Cold Editor IO
Problem: fuzzer needs JSON/CSV/binary artifacts, but managed IO and strings cannot enter 10,000-frame loop.
Solution: Burst jobs write NativeArray DTOs and 300-frame telemetry; cold editor/test runner serializes reports after job completion.
Rejected Alternatives: Formatting strings or writing files from inside simulation code is not Burst-compatible and would allocate.
Scalability potential: Low keeps one compact binary dump; Ultra can render richer editor graph/gizmo from same fixed telemetry without bloating gameplay DTOs.
Hardware Impact: Hot-path heap stays 0 B by construction; editor IO cost is outside simulation and CI can isolate it.
## Decision 03: Floating-Origin Stress Must Not Mutate AUP Truth
Problem: Task 11 asks for 500-frame floating-origin shift, but project AUP doctrine says canonical `double3` AUP is truth and consumers localize by subtracting origin before float casts.
Solution: smoke job shifts `localOriginAup` every 500 frames and verifies `ResolveLocalFloat3(state.AUP_Position, localOriginAup)` stays finite. Authoritative `state.AUP_Position` remains absolute.
Rejected Alternatives: Subtracting 5000m from every Vault KCC position would fake origin shift by changing gameplay truth and invalidate rollback/history hashes.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all use same double AUP truth; only downstream diagnostic graph richness scales.
Hardware Impact: One `double3` add per 500 frames; on i3/MX350 cost is below measurement noise while protecting against catastrophic float truncation near 99km.
## Decision 04: Rollback Probe Splits Original Replay and Mutated Replay
Problem: Literal comparison of replay with deliberately modified historical input against original trajectory would always differ and create false desync on every valid correction.
Solution: fuzzer does two checks: unmodified twin replay must match original bit-for-bit, and mutated twin replay /B must match each other bit-for-bit after same modified input. Any mismatch writes `DesyncDetectedSignal`.
Rejected Alternatives: Distance epsilon checks hide bit drift; comparing modified replay directly to original confuses expected correction with nondeterminism.
Scalability potential: Low uses one entity rollback probe per frame; higher tiers can increase probe count without changing DTO route or authority.
Hardware Impact: Cost is isolated to offline QA; it avoids shipping nondeterministic rollback bug that would be far more expensive than probe.
## Decision 05: Smoke-Only Vault IDs Stay Local Instead of Editing H8Memory
Problem: SHINOBU_355 needs temporary buffers for history, rollback, telemetry, failure records, profiles, and mock desync. `H8Memory.cs` is open/dirty in workspace and is high-conflict core memory file.
Solution: Use existing production KCC `BufferID` lanes for state/input/SDF/faults and cast numeric smoke-only `BufferID` values `71810..71818` for editor/offline temporary lanes, documented in route card.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing `H8Memory.cs` for enum entries would create needless merge conflict and widen blast radius.
Scalability potential: Low keeps 100 phantoms and 1,000,000 history slots; High/Ultra can reserve formal BufferID range later after integrator consolidation.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids extra global enum churn and uses one Vault allocation pass; no runtime memory layout changes.
## Decision 06: Legacy Standalone Runner Removed From Editor Test File
Problem: `HeadlessKccSmokeTests.cs` contained previous standalone runner with private `new NativeArray` allocations and duplicate jobs. Leaving it would undermine partial-class integration mandate.
Solution: Replace file with facade-only NUnit/window/gizmo layer that calls `Shinobu355KccSmokeRunner`, which stages simulation buffers through `GlobalDataVault` and uses partial `HydrodynamicKccRuntime` jobs.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping old runner as "unused" would still compile duplicate QA logic and preserve invalid source patterns.
Scalability potential: All device tiers run same fuzzer kernel; editor presentation can scale independently from QA math.
Hardware Impact: Headless CI avoids legacy NativeArray runner setup and any scene/object path; expected saving is dominated by deleting Unity scene/physics bootstrap, not by facade itself.
## Decision 07: Critical Fault Fail-Fast With Deterministic History Fill
Problem: NaN or rollback desync must halt fuzzer, but `NativeArrayOptions.UninitializedMemory` means unfinished history slots cannot be left unwritten.
Solution: After `KccSmokeFailureNonFinite` or `KccSmokeFailureRollbackDesync`, job writes current AUP values into all remaining history slots, then breaks physical simulation loop.
Rejected Alternatives: Continuing corrupted physics would contaminate forensic data; breaking immediately would leave uninitialized history bytes for validation jobs.
Scalability potential: Low devices stop work early on fatal math; High/Ultra keep identical behavior and can use saved time for richer editor forensic display.
Hardware Impact: On i3/MX350 fatal failures avoid running remaining expensive SDF/rollback steps while still keeping memory deterministic for postmortem scans.
## Decision 08: Treat Invalid SDF as Breach, Not Safe Space
Problem: first smoke SDF sampler returned positive distance for out-of-volume positions. That could hide phantom leaving voxel cave and still report safe open space.
Solution: Add `KccSmokeInvalidSdfMeters`, validate SDF dimensions/backing length before trilinear reads, and map invalid/out-of-volume samples to `KccSmokeFailureEscape | KccSmokeFailureSdfInvalid`.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting bootstrap-generated dimensions was too brittle; bad future test profile could still drive Burst job into unsafe read or false pass.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra use same sentinel path. Higher quality can increase SDF resolution later without changing failure semantics.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays small scalar bounds check per sample in offline QA; trade removes undefined memory reads and false green reports.
## Decision 09: Rollback Proof Must Include Velocity and Flags
Problem: AUP-only replay comparison could miss velocity or collision flag divergence while position happened to quantize to same millimeter.
Solution: Apply replay collision flags during rollback resimulation and compare AUP bits, velocity bits, and flags through `ReplayStateMatches`.
Rejected Alternatives: Distance epsilon or AUP-only comparison hides deterministic drift in rollback state ring.
Scalability potential: Probe cadence remains low and can scale by frequency later; DTO layout and authority route are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Six extra scalar bit comparisons per sampled rollback frame; negligible on i3/MX350 compared with preventing multiplayer desync regressions.
## Decision 10: Editor Telemetry Must Remain Vault-Owned
Problem: editor graph cached telemetry in private persistent `NativeArray`, creating second native owner outside `GlobalDataVault`.
Solution: Retain editor/test `GlobalDataVault` after run and expose telemetry through `TryReadOnlyHandle` with generation handle. Dispose on assembly reload/editor quit or before next run.
Rejected Alternatives: Copying telemetry into another persistent native array was faster to code but violates one-owner memory routing.
Scalability potential: Low uses one 300-entry ring; Ultra can add richer editor views by reading same retained Vault handle without duplicating native memory.
Hardware Impact: Saves one 19.2 KB native copy per run and removes leak-prone native allocation route on low-end editor machines.
## Decision 11: Split OOP Report From Smoke Report
Problem: OOP scanner and smoke runner both wrote `Docs/Reports/QA_OPTIMIZATION_REPORT.json`, so whichever ran last erased other proof artifact.
Solution: Keep smoke summary in `QA_OPTIMIZATION_REPORT.json` and move static OOP scanner proof to `QA_OPTIMIZATION_OOP_REPORT.json`, referenced by smoke report.
Rejected Alternatives: JSON merge parsing in cold editor code would add brittle string handling and more managed churn for no runtime gain.
Scalability potential: Report sections can grow independently as QA coverage increases.
Hardware Impact: No runtime cost; avoids CI artifact races and lost evidence.
## Decision 12: One Heavy NUnit Entry Point
Problem: Two editor tests launched same 100 phantom / 10,000 frame pass, doubling CI time and report writes.
Solution: Keep heavy pass in `Shinobu355_KccSmoke_100Phantoms_10000Frames_NoNanEscapeRollbackDesync`; downgrade legacy facade test to route-constant assertion.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping duplicate heavy tests makes failures noisy and wastes editor job budget.
Scalability potential: Low-tier CI avoids redundant work; higher-tier machines can still run same single authoritative pass.
Hardware Impact: Saves one full smoke pass per test sweep.
## Decision 13: Keep NoAlias and Prove Same-Typed Buffers Are Distinct
Problem: `States` and `RollbackStateRing` are both `NativeArray<KinematicStateDTO>` and marked `[NoAlias]`; Burst can only trust this if scheduler never passes same backing lane twice.
Solution: Add cold runner assertion that Vault BufferIDs for states and rollback ring differ before resolving/scheduling job.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing `[NoAlias]` would protect against caller bug but reduce compiler's ability to vectorize known distinct lanes.
Scalability potential: proof scales as more smoke buffers are formalized; future route card can promote local IDs into reserved BufferIDs.
Hardware Impact: One editor assertion, 0 us inside Burst hot loop; preserves NEON/AVX aliasing proof for low-end CPUs.
## Decision 14: Editor Facade Belongs to KCC Editor Assembly, Not Tests
Problem: UI Toolkit window, telemetry graph, failure gizmo, runner, and layout assertions lived inside `Hecton8.EditModeTests`, making human control bridge test-assembly gated and duplicating editor responsibilities.
Solution: Move cold facade into `Assets/_Project/Scripts/Physics/KCC/Editor/Shinobu355KccSmokeEditorFacade.cs`, keep tests as thin NUnit callers, and let `Hecton8.EditModeTests` reference `Hecton8.Physics.KCC.Editor`.
Rejected Alternatives: Reflection from editor tooling into test classes or adding menu/UI code to NUnit files would preserve wrong owner boundary.
Scalability potential: Low-tier CI runs only thin NUnit entrypoints; editor tooling remains available as KCC domain tooling without relying on `UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS` ownership.
Hardware Impact: 0 us gameplay cost; avoids loading duplicated runner/UI code through test route and removes compile-wall trap around test-only define constraints.
## Decision 14b: Scanner Must Prove Tests Do Not Own Editor Facade
Problem: Moving source files without extending scanner would leave only human claim that KCC/Kinematic tests no longer own UI Toolkit or SceneView tooling.
Solution: Extend `OOP_Test_Scanner` to count `EditorWindow`, `SceneView`, `UIElements`, `VisualElement`, `Button`, and `ProgressBar` identifiers in KCC/Kinematic test files.
Rejected Alternatives: Broad `rg` over all tests is too noisy because unrelated domains still own their own test windows; SHINOBU_355 needs scoped proof for KCC/Kinematic test ownership.
Scalability potential: Future KCC test regressions become scanner-detectable without expanding runtime dependencies.
Hardware Impact: Cold Roslyn scan only; 0 us runtime or fuzzer hot path.
## Decision 15: Editor Runner Must Not Depend on NUnit
Problem: Moving runner to KCC editor assembly would either require new NUnit precompiled reference there or removal of `Assert` calls.
Solution: Replace runner/layout `Assert` calls with deterministic `FatalArchitectureException` checks; tests still use NUnit only at their outer boundary.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding `nunit.framework.dll` to KCC editor asmdef was rejected because editor facade is production tooling, not test framework extension.
Scalability potential: same runner can be called by menu, CI harness, or future command-line editor automation.
Hardware Impact: 0 us hot path; exception checks execute only in cold/editor bootstrap.
## Decision 16: Editor Window Uses Scheduled Job Polling, Not Direct Blocking Run
Problem: UI Toolkit window called synchronous NUnit-grade runner directly. That kept actual KCC math in Burst, but human facade still blocked editor main thread until full 100 phantom / 10,000 frame pass finished.
Solution: Add `StartScheduledRun()` and `ScheduledRun`, allocate/resolve same Vault lanes, schedule geometry/init/simulation/escape/drift jobs as dependency chain, and let `HeadlessKccSmokeTesterWindow` poll final `JobHandle` from `EditorApplication.update`. Finalization calls `Complete()` only after `IsCompleted`; disposal drains only during editor teardown.
Rejected Alternatives: `async Task` was rejected because AGENTS.md forbids managed task allocation for this path. Splitting 10,000-frame kernel into hundreds of tiny jobs was rejected because it would add scheduler overhead and weaken amortized batch-work requirement. Leaving direct button call was rejected because it failed human-control/background-pipeline intent.
Scalability potential: Low-tier editors keep responsive facade while worker threads run long pass. Middle/High/Ultra can add richer telemetry presentation without changing KCC truth route or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: Runtime gameplay cost remains 0 us; this is editor-only. Main-thread stall from button path is removed except for cold allocation/scheduling and final `IsCompleted` cleanup. Unity profiler proof is still pending because project compile/import remains externally blocked.
## Decision 17: Scheduled Editor Reports Must Not Masquerade As CI GC Proof
Problem: first scheduled editor route finalized reports with `ManagedBytesAllocated = 0`, which could be misread as same allocation proof as synchronous CI/NUnit runner. That is false evidence because scheduled editor facade is cold human tool and can include editor UI allocations outside Burst smoke loop.
Solution: Capture current-thread allocated bytes before scheduling and report delta after final handle completes. Keep this as editor evidence metric only and give scheduled route its own evidence class: `UNITY_EDITOR_SCHEDULED_JOB_PENDING_IMPORT_PROOF`.
Rejected Alternatives: Marking scheduled editor allocations as failure was rejected because editor UI/report allocations are outside 10,000-frame Burst hot path. Leaving hardcoded zero was rejected because it creates fake proof artifact.
Scalability potential: Low-tier editors get honest diagnostics without changing runtime truth. Higher-tier editors can add richer graphs while authoritative CI route remains synchronous measured runner.
Hardware Impact: Two cold `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()` calls in editor path; 0 us gameplay hot-path cost.
## Decision 18: Retain Telemetry Snapshot, Not Full Smoke Vault
Problem: Retaining entire editor/test smoke Vault after completion kept 128 MiB arena cap alive only to let editor graph read 300 telemetry rows.
Solution: Copy 300-entry `KccSmokeTelemetryEntry` ring into dedicated 1 MiB telemetry-only `GlobalDataVault` after job handle has completed, then dispose bulk smoke Vault. editor graph still reads through `TryReadOnlyHandle`; it does not own private persistent `NativeArray`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping full smoke Vault was memory-wasteful. Copying into private persistent `NativeArray` was rejected again because it creates second native owner outside Vault route.
Scalability potential: Low-tier editors retain only small proof artifact. Higher-tier tools can render richer graphs by reading same tiny retained Vault or by explicitly requesting larger telemetry Vault without touching gameplay DTOs.
Hardware Impact: Replaces retained 128 MiB cap with 1 MiB cap. Adds one cold 19.2 KB copy per smoke run; 0 us gameplay or Burst hot-path cost.
## Decision 19: Forensic Dumps Need Versioned Ordered Binary, Not Raw Ring Order
Problem: black-box dump wrote ASCII-ish header and then raw telemetry in modulo-array order. After ring wrap, that is not oldest-to-newest forensic sequence, and file does not prove entry size or version.
Solution: Write 32-byte little-endian header with magic `H8KCC355`, version, entry count, struct size, oldest frame, newest frame, and source hash. Emit telemetry rows by rotating circular ring based on failure frame or full default frame count.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving raw array order was faster but makes postmortem tools reconstruct state from implicit modulo behavior. Writing JSON was rejected because crash artifact must stay compact and unmanaged-row compatible.
Scalability potential: Low keeps tiny deterministic dump. High/Ultra can append additional fixed-size sections under new version without invalidating current rows.
Hardware Impact: Cold failure IO only. No added simulation cost; postmortem parsing becomes O(entryCount) with explicit layout.
## Decision 20: Caller Proof Must Precede Unsafe Phantom Scheduling
Problem: initialization job takes unsafe state pointers, but editor runner scheduled default phantom count directly. If future Vault capacity changes undersize lane, job could index beyond resolved array before any managed assertion catches it.
Solution: Add `ValidateSmokeBuffers(...)` after all Vault resolves, assert every native lane length, and pass validated phantom count into initialization, simulation, and escape verification jobs.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding per-index guards inside Burst hot loop would protect against caller bugs but would spend branches every phantom frame. Trusting `EnsureGenerationHandle` intent alone was too weak for unsafe pointer code.
Scalability potential: Future profile counts or phantom counts can scale by changing capacity first; runner fails fast in cold bootstrap if lane is undersized.
Hardware Impact: Cold assertions only. Preserves branch-free inner simulation loops on i3/MX350 and ARM64.
## Decision 21: CSV Parser Must Fail Closed On Overflow And Hostile Profile Ranges
Problem: span-based CSV parser could overflow integer accumulator before converting to double, producing finite corrupted coordinate.
Solution: Guard `whole * 10 + digit` before mutation, clamp exponent accumulation, reject AUP coordinates outside 250 km, reject speeds above 2000 m/s, reject non-finite or oversized input bias, and clamp speed scale to 0.01..4.
Rejected Alternatives: `double.Parse`/`float.Parse` was rejected for culture sensitivity and managed parser overhead. Silently clamping AUP coordinates was rejected because profile data should fail closed, not move phantoms into different cave.
Scalability potential: Low-tier CI rejects broken profiles before allocating debug effort. Higher-tier fuzzing can widen constants explicitly if test envelope changes.
Hardware Impact: Cold CSV ingest only; 0 us in 10,000-frame Burst loop.
## Decision 22: Scheduled Teardown Must Not Re-Enter Failed Finalizer
Problem: If scheduled editor finalization throws while writing report, copying telemetry, or dumping files, UI catch path calls `Dispose()`. Without guard, `Dispose()` would call same finalizer again and could mask original fault or throw recursively.
Solution: Add `_finalizeAttempted` to `ScheduledRun`. `Poll()` owns completion-window finalizer; `Dispose()` drains and disposes native memory but does not re-enter finalization once it has been attempted.
Rejected Alternatives: Swallowing finalization exceptions would hide broken proof artifacts. Retrying finalization in `Dispose()` was rejected because failure is deterministic in most file/asset cases.
Scalability potential: Low-tier editors get predictable teardown under IO failure. Higher-tier tooling can layer retry UI outside this runner without touching native job graph.
Hardware Impact: One cold bool branch in editor teardown; 0 us gameplay and 0 us Burst hot-path cost.
## Decision 23: Editor Failure Gizmo Must Still Obey AUP Locality
Problem: SceneView failure gizmo stored `double3` AUP correctly but drew by casting absolute 100 km-scale coordinates directly into `Vector3`. This is editor-only, but it creates bad precedent against AUP precision law and can make far-origin debug evidence visually noisy.
Solution: Keep absolute `double3` failure and previous AUP as forensic truth, add `s_gizmoOriginAup`, and render only `failureAup - previousAup` / `previousAup - previousAup` local deltas through `HydrodynamicKccMath.ResolveLocalFloat3`.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving direct cast was rejected because "cold editor path" is not valid excuse for violating same proof discipline smoke test is validating. Re-centering to SceneView pivot was rejected because pivot is presentation state, not deterministic KCC forensic origin.
Scalability potential: Low-tier editors draw same simple local marker. Higher-tier editor tools can layer richer absolute-AUP labels or sector overlays without changing KCC smoke DTOs.
Hardware Impact: Two cold `ResolveLocalFloat3` calls per SceneView repaint only when failure is visible; 0 us in 10,000-frame Burst simulation.
## Decision 24: Global Binary Ledger Needs QA-Only Payload Boundary
Problem: SHINOBU_355 had route card, status, and log proof, but global binary payload ledger did not contain QA-only smoke DTO/BufferID boundary. That leaves future agents no single ledger entry showing that `71810..71818` are disposable smoke lanes and not production truth.
Solution: Add `SHINOBU_355 Headless KCC Smoke Tester Boundary` to `BINARY_PAYLOAD_INTEGRATION_LEDGER.md`, including owner, evidence class, DTO sizes, Vault IDs, AUP route, Dear Lie route, and dump format.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing `H8Memory.cs` to formalize enum names was rejected again because file is shared compile-wall surface and task only needs offline temporary lanes.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra QA configurations can scale phantom/profile pressure using documented local range while production save/rollback identity stays unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Documentation-only change; no runtime cost and no assembly recompilation caused by core enum churn.
## Decision 25: Do Not Create KCC Runtime Assembly During QA Polish
Problem: cold SHINOBU editor facade lives in existing `Hecton8.Physics.KCC.Editor` assembly and calls runtime KCC DTOs/jobs. naive response would be to wrap entire KCC runtime folder in new runtime asmdef, but `HydrodynamicKccRuntime` is large production surface with existing editor tooling already consuming it.
Solution: Keep SHINOBU_355 inside existing KCC editor assembly pattern, add only missing editor assembly references required by cold runner (`Core.Contracts`, `Unity.Jobs`, unsafe dump permission), and let test assembly reference that existing editor facade.
Rejected Alternatives: Creating `Hecton8.Physics.KCC.Runtime.asmdef` was rejected because it would reshape compile graph for production KCC and could surface unrelated dependency walls. Moving runner back into NUnit files was rejected because it makes human editor facade test-owned again.
Scalability potential: QA/editor route remains isolated from gameplay truth and can scale test pressure without changing runtime assembly ownership.
Hardware Impact: No runtime cost. Compile-wall risk is narrower than creating new runtime assembly; Unity import proof is still pending behind external build gate.
Source lines scanned 209; retained 157; overflow-important omitted 0.

Rationale_SHINOBU_356.md
# Rationale_SHINOBU_356
Status: POLISH PATCHED / LOOP16 UNITY IMPORT BLOCKED BY CORE MEMORY DEPENDENCY / LOOP18 CORE MEMORY ROUTE CARD RECORDED / LOOP19 SCHEDULED PROFILE SOURCE FIX PATCHED / LOOP20 SOURCE GUARDS CLEAN
## 2026-05-23 Initial Architecture Decisions
Problem: batch prompt demands Jacobi power fuzzer, but repo already contains `PowerJacobiStressFuzzer`, `PowerGridJacobiStressFuzzerEditTests`, and production `PowerVoltageSolverJob`.
Solution: Extend existing QA fuzzer surface and keep it in `Hecton8.Power`. This follows partial/integration mandate without inventing second runtime owner.
Rejected Alternatives: new `HectonPowerGridFuzzer` MonoBehaviour or standalone manager would duplicate existing test runner and increase compile-wall risk under parallel agents.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all run same offline 1,000-iteration math; editor visualization and reports can scale separately without changing solver truth.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 benefit is from flat CSR/native arrays and one headless Burst job instead of managed graph object walks. No profiler proof yet; microsecond savings are static model only.
Problem: SignalBus matrix has power telemetry lane, but this fuzzer is offline QA and must not mutate live game state.
Solution: Format failure data in fuzzer DTO/report fields compatible with BrownoutSignal facts: node index/hash, AUP coordinate, failing array offset, and flags. Do not publish runtime signals.
Rejected Alternatives: Emitting `SignalBus<BrownoutSignal>` from fuzzer would make test failure into gameplay traffic and violate offline runner boundary.
Scalability potential: Low keeps raw dump only; Middle adds JSON/CSV report; High adds editor line graph; Ultra adds scene gizmo failure vectors.
Hardware Impact: No runtime device impact because fuzzer stays editor/CI/cold QA. Hot job remains native and Burst-compatible.
Problem: Prompt requires hostile CSR with infinite resistance and AUP double precision.
Solution: Generate CSR directly into flat arrays, represent infinite resistance as zero conductance for stable solver input, preserve explicit non-finite injection in dedicated fault fields/tests, and subtract `BaseOriginAup` in `double3` before float conversion.
Rejected Alternatives: Passing `float.PositiveInfinity` as conductance into production solver is invalid representation because solver consumes conductance, not resistance; it would test bad input encoding instead of infinite resistance behavior.
Scalability potential: Same graph shape works across all devices; presentation-only editor/gizmo fidelity scales by tier.
Hardware Impact: Avoids NaN propagation and avoids managed allocation; expected low-end gain over managed List/Node fuzzers is cache locality, not claimed without profiler artifact.
Problem: Vault buffer IDs initially used SHINOBU-style values above `100000`, but `GlobalDataVault.TryResolveHandle` resolves through flat metadata array first.
Solution: Move all fuzzer-owned buffer IDs to 35610-35629, below `MaxGenerationHandleCapacity=100000`, and keep every allocation routed through `EnsureGenerationHandle(..., UninitializedMemory)`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping high numeric IDs would let generation handles build through fallback metadata map while failing during resolution. Local `new NativeArray` persistent buffers were rejected because they violate Vault ownership mandate.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all use same vault-owned flat arrays; `GlobalQualityWeight` is clamped as metadata but does not reduce QA node, edge, or iteration truth.
Hardware Impact: On i3/MX350 this avoids handle-resolution failure and avoids approximately 20 MB of voltage-history zero-fill. On high-end machines saved memory bandwidth buys deeper editor visualization without changing solver truth.
Problem: 1,000-iteration fuzzer implemented as managed loop around `PowerVoltageSolverJob.Schedule().Complete()` would measure dispatch overhead and potentially GC, not solver stability.
Solution: Implement `EvaluateHeadlessJacobiFuzzJob` as one Burst IJob with internal 1,000-iteration double-buffered CSR relaxation loop, residual reduction, omega variation, early convergence, rollback replay, and fatal halt.
Rejected Alternatives: 1,000 separate jobs and managed frame loop were rejected due to scheduler overhead and harder GC proof. managed graph solver was rejected due to cache misses.
Scalability potential: Low uses identical math and records fewer editor visuals; Middle/High/Ultra can visualize more telemetry without changing job.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate is roughly 100,000 us saved from avoided dispatch/managed traversal in offline run on low-end silicon. No profiler artifact yet because compile/run is blocked by CPU guard.
Problem: Remainder drift and watt imbalance can exist even when residual convergence looks stable.
Solution: `VerifyPowerConservationJob` computes generated watts, consumed demand, energy delta, and stamps drift plus measured Burst microseconds into every fuzz telemetry entry.
Rejected Alternatives: Residual-only pass/fail and unused generated/consumed sums were rejected because they miss closed-network energy leaks.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra use same drift truth. Only report density changes by editor tooling.
Hardware Impact: One native linear pass over 5,000 nodes is cache-local and cheaper than managed aggregation; estimated low-end cost is under 5,000 us.
Problem: Failure autopsy originally dumped only one telemetry ring and only for math-corruption flags.
Solution: Dump both 300-entry frame ring and 300-entry `JacobiFuzzTelemetryEntry` ring to `Docs/AgentLogs/Dump_SHINOBU_356.bin` on NaN, divergence, or rollback desync.
Rejected Alternatives: CSV-only failure reports and exception text were rejected because they lack final omega/residual/hash context.
Scalability potential: Low keeps raw binary only; Middle adds CSV; High and Ultra can build richer editor readers from same dump.
Hardware Impact: Dump cost is cold failure-only. Low-end runtime impact is zero because fuzzer is offline QA.
Problem: shared `Docs/Reports/QA_OPTIMIZATION_REPORT.json` already contained another agent's report section.
Solution: Route fuzzer success report to `QA_OPTIMIZATION_REPORT_SHINOBU_356.json` and make `OOP_Fuzz_Scanner` merge `shinobu356JacobiPowerFuzzer` section into shared JSON.
Rejected Alternatives: Overwriting shared report would erase SHINOBU_355 evidence and create false integration history.
Scalability potential: Report merging scales by agent section; low-end devices never see this editor-only path.
Hardware Impact: Cold editor file IO only. No player or hot QA job impact.
Problem: prompt requires profile-driven fuzz input named `jacobi_fuzz_profiles.csv`.
Solution: Add `Assets/_Project/Data/jacobi_fuzz_profiles.csv` with cyclic-loop and disconnected-island profiles, load it first, and retain legacy `fuzzer_topology_profiles.csv` fallback.
Rejected Alternatives: Hard-coded default-only topology was rejected because CI profiles must vary graph stress without code changes.
Scalability potential: Low uses same 5,000-node profile; Middle/High/Ultra can add heavier profiles without changing solver code.
Hardware Impact: Cold parse only through `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` and native scratch; hot path remains zero managed allocation.
## 2026-05-23 Polish Pass Decisions
Problem: fuzzer lived inside `Hecton8.QA.Headless.asmdef` but referenced sibling Power/Physics/Thermal DTO surfaces, making compile-wall isolation impossible to prove without broad root Power assembly migration.
Solution: Replace foreign DTO dependencies in SHINOBU_356 fuzzer with local explicit-layout `JacobiFuzzPowerNodeDTO=32` and local AUP helper math. Keep fuzzer namespace/API stable for editor/test facade, but do not add direct sibling runtime asmdef references.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding root `Hecton8.Power.Runtime.asmdef` or moving `PowerGridJacobiContracts.cs` was rejected because it changes broad domain boundary under parallel agents. Keeping Physics/Thermal layout checks in Power fuzzer test was rejected because those owners need their own tests.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra QA behavior remains identical; saved compile-wall surface buys faster iteration and leaves presentation-only editor visualization scalable.
Hardware Impact: Runtime gameplay impact is zero because this is offline QA. Low-end developer hardware gains from reduced assembly dependency breadth; static gain is fewer sibling assemblies invalidated by SHINOBU_356 edits.
Problem: Several fuzzer Burst jobs used `FloatMode.Fast`, which can reassociate math or change NaN behavior while fuzzer claims rollback/desync proof.
Solution: Change every owned fuzzer Burst job to `[BurstCompile(CompileSynchronously = true, FloatMode = FloatMode.Deterministic, FloatPrecision = FloatPrecision.Standard)]`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Fast math for generation/setup was rejected because hostile graph generation and initialization participate in state hash and rollback comparison. Tolerance-based rollback compare was rejected because exact bit comparison is failure target.
Scalability potential: Quality does not scale solver iterations in this fuzzer because XML Task 05 requires identical high-fidelity QA math; deterministic math protects authority proof across low ARM64 and high x86 targets.
Hardware Impact: Deterministic Burst may cost ALU throughput versus Fast mode, but this is CI/editor QA, not per-frame gameplay. cost buys cross-platform reproducibility and prevents false rollback evidence.
Problem: Failure dump used ASCII prefix and lengths, not fixed ABI header, so black-box readers could not prove stride/schema without out-of-band knowledge.
Solution: Add `PowerJacobiStressDumpHeader=64` with magic/version/counts/strides/BufferID range, validate it in editor layout guard, and write it before both 300-entry telemetry rings.
Rejected Alternatives: CSV-only report and ASCII-only dump prefix were rejected because they do not provide byte-exact forensic structure.
Scalability potential: Low uses raw dump; Middle/High/Ultra editor tools can parse same header for richer visualization without changing job truth.
Hardware Impact: Adds exactly 64 bytes to cold failure dumps. No runtime frame impact.
Problem: OOP scanner claimed eradication while missing fuzzer runtime root and scanning broad Power namespace files by context string.
Solution: Expand roots to include `Assets/_Project/Scripts/QA/Headless/JacobiStressFuzzer`, restrict context to owned fuzzer files/types, strip comments/strings before token counting, write per-agent scanner report, and downgrade status to `PENDING_VERIFICATION_STATIC_SOURCE_ONLY`.
Rejected Alternatives: Manual shared-report overwrite was rejected because SHINOBU_355 evidence exists. true Roslyn AST scanner was not added because current editor assembly has no proven Roslyn dependency and adding one would increase compile-wall risk.
Scalability potential: Scanner is cold editor-only. Low hardware pays no gameplay cost; higher-end editor tooling can add AST parsing later behind its own assembly route.
Hardware Impact: Cold source scan only; manual equivalent scanned 55 files with 0 managed graph / 0 Physics / 0 GameObject hits.
Problem: Subagent audit found broader Power runtime issues (`PowerTelemetryEntry` union semantics, AUP distance precision, `IntegrateBatteryChargeJob` race, DataVault owner IDs, runtime reflection, ring dump order) outside SHINOBU_356's owned QA surface.
Solution: Record them as residual external Power-runtime risk, but do not patch production Power runtime in this pass. SHINOBU_356 removes its direct dependency on those surfaces so fuzzer evidence is not blocked by sibling ownership.
Rejected Alternatives: Fixing those production routes opportunistically was rejected because it violates assigned domain boundary and needs owner route cards/profiler proof.
Scalability potential: Not applicable to this QA patch; future Power owner work should address those findings with dispatcher/profiler evidence.
Hardware Impact: No direct device change from this pass. residual risks remain facts for Power owner, not hidden by SHINOBU_356 reporting.
Problem: Re-reading XML assignment showed Task 15 requires CSV profile limits in unmanaged Vault storage, while fuzzer only used cold temp parser result and value-copy config.
Solution: Add `PowerJacobiStressFuzzerBufferIds.TopologyProfile=35629`, resolve it through local Vault, write parsed profile row into that buffer, and pass Vault row into graph generation.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping profile as managed object or ScriptableObject was rejected. Adding new core enum entry was rejected because casted local BufferID preserves compile-wall isolation.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra can load different profile rows without C# recompilation; quality metadata does not change QA stress truth, gameplay truth, or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: Adds 32 bytes to local QA vault arena and removes profile ownership ambiguity. No gameplay device impact.
Problem: Failure dump header had `Flags` field but did not populate it, and `WriteDump` could silently skip forensic dump if unrelated CSV scratch buffer was unavailable.
Solution: Pass `result.FailureFlags` into `PowerJacobiStressBinaryDump.WriteDump`, set `PowerJacobiStressDumpHeader.Flags`, and remove scratch-buffer precondition from dump writing.
Rejected Alternatives: Inferring flags from telemetry rows was rejected because header is first forensic contract. Keeping scratch as dump dependency was rejected because black-box failure dumps must not depend on CSV formatting storage.
Scalability potential: Same 64-byte header supports low raw dump readers and high-end editor forensic visualizers.
Hardware Impact: Cold failure path only; change adds no hot-path work.
Problem: Editor facade still contained unused `MonoBehaviour` gizmo hook, which is unnecessary object-oriented Unity surface because SceneView drawing already provides visual proof.
Solution: Delete `JacobiStressFuzzerGizmoHook` and keep existing `SceneView.duringSceneGui` marker path.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping dormant component was rejected because it invites GameObject attachment and contradicts no-runtime-debug-object route.
Scalability potential: Editor visualization remains available without scene objects; hot QA remains unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes editor-only component surface. No runtime device impact.
Problem: scanner report listed broad Power/Test roots while reporting zero hits, but broad token-only sanity pass found one non-owned Power managed-node token and five non-owned GameObject test tokens.
Solution: Keep owned-context scan as SHINOBU_356 authority, but add `contextFilteredFiles`, `scopeNote`, and `ignoredNonOwned*` counters to scanner output. report now proves owned fuzzer/editor/test files are clean while preserving external noise as facts.
Rejected Alternatives: Claiming all broad roots are clean was rejected because `PowerRelayNode.cs` and unrelated legacy tests exist. Expanding SHINOBU_356 scope to rewrite those files was rejected as cross-domain sabotage.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra player paths are unaffected; this is cold QA evidence. Higher-end editor tooling can replace token scanning with Roslyn later behind separate route card.
Hardware Impact: Cold source scan only. No runtime device cost.
Problem: compile check became structurally desirable after ABI/signature changes, but project has no `.sln`, no generated `Hecton8.QA.Headless.csproj`, and no `.csproj` includes SHINOBU_356 fuzzer files.
Solution: Do not run broad `dotnet build`; it would compile unrelated generated projects and still not prove owned asmdef. Record target discovery and require Unity project regeneration or Unity test runner for real compile/import check.
Rejected Alternatives: Building `Assembly-CSharp.csproj` or `Hecton8.Core.csproj` was rejected because neither includes `PowerGridJacobiStressFuzzer.cs`. Running rebuild under CPU 98.8% was rejected by AGENTS guard.
Scalability potential: Not gameplay-facing. Developer hardware avoids false compile-wall burn.
Hardware Impact: Prevented broad build on saturated CPU; no player device impact.
Problem: Subagent audit found undefined `PowerJacobiStressFuzzerBufferIds.NodeDtos` reference in dump header path.
Solution: Replace it with declared `PowerJacobiStressFuzzerBufferIds.Nodes` and add layout offset guards for result/config/dump header fields that carry 8-byte AUP or forensic ABI data.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving this as compile-blocked unknown was rejected because it was source-visible and not dependent on Unity import.
Scalability potential: No gameplay change; fix protects low-end CI and high-end editor forensic readers equally.
Hardware Impact: Zero runtime cost; prevents hard compile failure.
Problem: Task 14 required asynchronous background pipeline, but editor facade called synchronous `RunDefault()` and blocked editor thread.
Solution: Add cold `ScheduledRun` wrapper that holds Vault-resolved views while offline job chain is pending, schedules graph generation -> injection -> init -> Jacobi fuzz -> conservation as dependency chain, and lets editor poll `JobHandle.IsCompleted` through `EditorApplication.update`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping modal synchronous progress was rejected. Moving fuzzer into runtime manager was rejected because this is offline QA and would create authority confusion.
Scalability potential: Low developer hardware keeps editor responsive; high-end machines still run full 1,000-iteration math and can visualize richer telemetry.
Hardware Impact: Avoids editor main-thread stalls during scheduled chain. wrapper stores views only; memory remains owned by local Vault and is disposed after completion.
Problem: Task 17 required AST scanning, but previous scanner was token-only and report said so.
Solution: Add Roslyn precompiled references to `Hecton8.QA.Headless.Editor.asmdef` and upgrade `OOP_Fuzz_Scanner` to `CSharpSyntaxTree` AST-primary scanner with token fallback only on parse failure.
Rejected Alternatives: Continuing to mark token evidence as enough was rejected. Adding runtime Roslyn dependency was rejected; this remains editor-only.
Scalability potential: Cold editor/CI only. No player path cost.
Hardware Impact: Cold scan CPU cost increases modestly, but prevents false source-evidence claims.
Problem: fuzzer injected hostile non-finite DTO fields but did not explicitly observe those fields in solver loop.
Solution: `EvaluateHeadlessJacobiFuzzJob` now checks `InternalResistance`, `MaxCapacity`, and `CurrentStorage` for non-finite/overflow/negative corruption and raises `FailureFlagMathCorruption` with first-bad-node capture.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing hostile DTO injection was rejected because assignment explicitly asks for corrupted topology/impedance stress.
Scalability potential: Same detection on all hardware. No binary quality switch.
Hardware Impact: Adds few scalar checks per node in offline QA only.
Problem: Task 19 mentioned `NativeMinHeap`, but SHINOBU_356 owns no heap/open-set algorithm.
Solution: Mark heap check as not applicable in status/log rather than inventing unused heap type. Existing project heaps belong to Pathfinding/Audio/Construction/Economy owners.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding dead heap just to satisfy generic prompt line was rejected because it would add unused code and fake architecture.
Scalability potential: No player path impact.
Hardware Impact: Avoids dead code and compile-wall expansion.
Problem: `FrameCount` was reported as requested 1,000 budget even when solver stopped earlier on fatal hostile input, creating fake 1,000-frame black-box proof.
Solution: Report actual executed Jacobi iteration count in `FrameCount` and update edit test to assert bounded actual count instead of exactly 1,000.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding outer fake frame loop was rejected because assignment stress target is 1,000-iteration Jacobi loop, not gameplay frame simulation.
Scalability potential: Same truth on all hardware; reporting no longer changes by quality or editor state.
Hardware Impact: Zero hot cost; removes misleading forensic metadata.
Problem: No QA-specific `SystemID` exists in current core enum, but fuzzer must tag Vault buffers with owner.
Solution: Continue using `SystemID.Power` intentionally because offline data shape is power-grid authority evidence; keep it local to disposable Vault so it cannot pollute global runtime ownership.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing `H8Memory.cs` to add QA owner ID was rejected as broad core-enum change under parallel agents.
Scalability potential: No gameplay path impact.
Hardware Impact: Avoids core compile-wall change.
Problem: Loop 12 readback found `ScheduledRun.Complete()` referenced `_allocatedBefore`, undeclared field, creating hard source-visible compile stop in async editor route.
Solution: Use local `allocatedBefore` sample already taken immediately before `_finalHandle.Complete()`. This measures completion fence window without claiming editor polling or file IO is part of zero-GC solver kernel.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding persistent `_allocatedBefore` field was rejected because it would include arbitrary editor polling allocations between schedule and completion and falsely fail fuzzer. Removing allocation measurement from scheduled completion was rejected because completion fence still needs cheap guard.
Scalability potential: Low developer machines avoid compile stop and keep editor responsive. Mid/High/Ultra machines still use same background job chain; no gameplay truth or DTO layout changes.
Hardware Impact: Zero Burst hot-path cost. It prevents C# import failure and avoids false managed-allocation flags from editor UI time.
Problem: editor UI labeled scheduled timing as `solver avg us`, but async path can only observe elapsed background-chain wall time from schedule to completion; it cannot sample exact CPU time inside already-running Burst job.
Solution: Keep result ABI unchanged, document scheduled route in source, and relabel UI as `solver/chain us`. synchronous CI `Run()` path still records isolated solver Complete wall time and owns performance flag.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding new result field was rejected because `PowerJacobiStressFuzzerResult=128` is already documented ABI and changing it would require broader report/schema update. Faking pure solver sample from async wrapper was rejected.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra editor presentation reports same truth route; quality metadata is preserved but does not change authority or solver coverage.
Hardware Impact: No runtime cost. Removes misleading performance evidence from editor facade.
Problem: AST scanner's GameObject invocation matcher only used `.EndsWith(".Instantiate")` and `.EndsWith(".AddComponent")`, which can miss generic/member forms such as `target.AddComponent<Foo>()` depending on Roslyn expression string shape.
Solution: Match `.Instantiate` and `.AddComponent` anywhere in invocation expression string after AST classification. Object creation detection remains AST-based through `ObjectCreationExpressionSyntax`.
Rejected Alternatives: Returning to token-only scanning was rejected because Task 17 requires AST evidence. Broadening scanner to all Unity API calls was rejected because SHINOBU_356 only owns Power fuzzer OOP/Physics/GameObject eradication evidence.
Scalability potential: Cold editor/CI only; no player device path.
Hardware Impact: Negligible cold scan cost, stronger static evidence.
Problem: scheduled route can only know elapsed chain wall time in `Complete()`, after `VerifyPowerConservationJob` has already stamped `JacobiFuzzTelemetryEntry.SolverMicroseconds = 0`.
Solution: Add cold post-complete native-loop stamp that copies final measured solver/chain microseconds and final mismatch flags into 300-entry fuzz telemetry ring before CSV/dump/report artifacts are written.
Rejected Alternatives: Measuring Stopwatch inside Burst was rejected because it is not available and would contaminate deterministic job math. Leaving telemetry at zero was rejected because black-box ring would disagree with result row.
Scalability potential: Same 300-entry forensic ring on all devices; quality metadata does not reduce proof coverage.
Hardware Impact: 300 native row writes in cold editor/CI completion only. No gameplay frame cost.
Problem: Runtime and edit-test layout validation used `Marshal.OffsetOf`, which is cold but still reflection/metadata route inside SHINOBU_356 proof surface.
Solution: Replace it with unsafe stack-local field offset arithmetic through `UnsafeUtility.AddressOf`, matching existing core diagnostics patterns.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing offset checks was rejected because Task 18 needs import/runtime guard. Keeping reflection was rejected because project mandate asks for reflectionless ABI proof where feasible.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra QA behavior is identical; guard no longer depends on managed reflection metadata.
Hardware Impact: Cold validation only. It removes reflection overhead and metadata risk from offline fuzzer entrypoint.
Problem: Hostile `float.MaxValue`, `NaN`, `-Infinity`, and demand overflow injections could be clamped before solver recorded which raw input caused failure.
Solution: `EvaluateHeadlessJacobiFuzzJob` now inspects raw initial potential and demand before `Sanitize01`, sets math/divergence failure flags, captures first-bad-node AUP/hash, and then clamps for containment.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying on DTO corruption checks was rejected because it did not prove every hostile input lane was observed. Letting raw infinities enter relaxation was rejected because it would poison later forensic state.

Status: POLISH PASS IMPLEMENTED - DOTNET BUILD BLOCKED BY CPU GATE
Owner: SHINOBU_357
Problem: assignment demands WAL integrity fuzzer, but repository archaeology shows `WalIntegrityFuzzerCore` already exists and is wired to Agent 256 rollback/backup validation.
Solution: Extend `WalIntegrityFuzzerCore` through partial file and keep new SHINOBU_357 surface isolated. This preserves one owner route for WAL QA and avoids duplicate backup-promotion logic.
Rejected Alternatives: new standalone `HectonSaveFuzzer` would duplicate existing WAL paths and increase compile-wall risk. Direct `SaveManager` surgery was rejected because runtime manager is broad and not required for offline WAL QA.
Scalability potential: Low tier uses same correctness path with smaller editor profiles; Middle uses default 100-iteration CI loop; High and Ultra can raise payload/profile limits without changing save truth layout.
Hardware Impact: On i3/MX350, avoiding duplicate fuzzer avoids additional runtime registration and scene load cost; expected gameplay-frame impact is 0 us because surface is editor/development-only.
Problem: WAL corruption findings must be consumable by adjacent systems without creating runtime coupling.
Solution: Build mock unmanaged save-status DTO with path hash, AUP sector/local fields, failed offset, and flags. offline fuzzer writes reports/dumps instead of publishing into `SaveEvents` or Submarine OS lanes.
Rejected Alternatives: Runtime signal publication from editor fuzzer would violate `SYSTEM_INTERCONNECT_MATRIX.md` lane ownership and could create false gameplay traffic.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all consume same DTO; editor presentation can draw richer gizmos without changing failure payload.
Hardware Impact: No runtime lane traffic. CI/editor-only report generation shifts cost outside frame budget.
Problem: fuzzer must verify catastrophic WAL interruption without putting managed dummy serializers on main-thread hot path.
Solution: Use Burst jobs for payload/corruption math, then perform unavoidable file-handle crash simulation as cold QA I/O around Agent 256 `SaveStateMerkleTree.TryValidateWalAndRollback`. Every accepted recovery is checked by `SaveBinaryStorage.Hash64` equality and byte-count equality against `.bak`.
Rejected Alternatives: pure managed `File.WriteAllBytes` fuzzer would test test harness more than save system. Rewriting production WAL pager was rejected because Agent 256 already owns validator route.
Scalability potential: Low uses bounded profile for edit tests; Middle uses 100 iterations at 10 MB; High can raise profile count and disk pressure; Ultra can run multiple profile rows while keeping same correctness route.
Hardware Impact: Low-end i3/MX350 avoids runtime frame cost because fuzzer is editor/development-only. 10 MB uninitialized buffer path avoids roughly 450 us of redundant clear bandwidth before overwrite.
Problem: task requires OOP fuzzer eradication proof without flagging scanner's own DTO field names as false positives.
Solution: Implement bounded-token scanner that requires non-identifier boundaries around `StreamWriter`, `JsonUtility`, and `BinaryFormatter`, and skip scanner source file itself. Report cold `FileStream` references separately from fatal serializer findings.
Rejected Alternatives: Raw substring search was rejected because `StreamWriterFindings` and `JsonUtilityFindings` would self-trigger. AST tooling was rejected because no existing Roslyn dependency is wired into this Unity editor path.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle run same scanner on save tests only; High/Ultra can widen directory coverage by adding roots without changing token semantics.
Hardware Impact: Scanner is editor-only; no gameplay cost. Source-file scan cost is approximately 42-55 us per file after enumeration on SSD cache.
Problem: AUP precision proof was required, but WAL fuzzer should not allocate managed coordinate objects or cast absolute positions to float.
Solution: Add Burst-side double sentinel that validates known 100 km-scale double bit patterns and flags `WalFuzzPrecisionLossCrime` if float round-tripping would hide precision loss.
Rejected Alternatives: Runtime reflection over serialized save objects and `BitConverter` inside hot job were rejected. Absolute float conversion was rejected because it is exact failure mode being tested.
Scalability potential: Low through Ultra execute same constant-time sentinel; profile scale changes payload/iteration pressure, not coordinate truth ownership.
Hardware Impact: Three double-bit checks are below 1 us on i3/MX350 and do not touch heap memory.
Problem: Verification was required, but machine already had dotnet workers running.
Solution: Stop at non-compiler proof: `git diff --check`, focused source reads, process/CPU checks, and status marked build-blocked instead of complete.
Rejected Alternatives: Launching another `dotnet build` would violate project CPU/dotnet protection rule and risk another agent's compile.
Scalability potential: code remains isolated to partial files and one existing test file, minimizing merge and compile-wall surface when editor imports.
Hardware Impact: Avoided additional compiler load while seven dotnet workers were already present.
Problem: first pass left SHINOBU_357 scratch ownership partially implicit and documented only telemetry Vault lanes.
Solution: Route payload, corrupt WAL, state, telemetry, hash scratch, and file-handle status through local casted DataVault IDs `73470..73476`, then document those IDs in binary payload ledger. `TempJob` allocation is retained only for editor/test fallback when `IDataVault` is null or allocation-locked.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding enum members to `BufferID` was rejected because it touches hot core coordination file and increases compile-wall/merge risk for no runtime ABI benefit. Keeping scratch as private NativeArrays was rejected because it violates Vault ownership law.
Scalability potential: Low runs smaller profile rows over same Vault route; Middle keeps default 100 iterations; High and Ultra can raise payload/profile pressure without changing save identity or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: Reusing Vault-backed uninitialized buffers avoids repeated allocator churn and saves prior 10 MB clear estimate of about 450 us on i3/MX350-class memory bandwidth.
Problem: headless Burst job had unsafe state pointer and treated corrupt WAL buffer as mutable even though it is input proof surface.
Solution: Replace raw state pointer with one-row `NativeArray<WalFuzzStateDTO>` and mark corrupt WAL buffer `[ReadOnly, NoAlias]`. Mix one corrupted byte into rollback hash probe so interrupted WAL byte stream participates in deterministic proof.
Rejected Alternatives: `NativeDisableUnsafePtrRestriction` was rejected because it weakens safety without measurable need here. Copying entire corrupt WAL buffer into second hash was rejected as bandwidth waste; one indexed probe is enough for headless determinism sentinel because disk recovery owns full hash truth.
Scalability potential: Quality affects profile/iteration pressure only, not truth ownership. same probe path executes on low, middle, high, and ultra hardware.
Hardware Impact: Removing pointer avoids aliasing ambiguity and keeps Burst job vectorization surface cleaner; corrupted-byte probe adds one byte load per iteration, below 1 us for capped 100-iteration job.
Problem: `.partial` WAL promotion relied on `File.Replace`, which can fail on unsupported platforms or metadata paths outside actual corruption target.
Solution: Wrap replacement with `TryReplaceOrMoveWal`; if replacement is unsupported or throws IO failure, delete old primary and move partial file into place. recovery proof still compares restored primary hash/bytes against `.bak` after Agent 256 rollback.
Rejected Alternatives: Blind `File.Move` over existing primary was rejected because it fails on older .NET/Unity targets. Retrying `File.Replace` in loop was rejected because it can hide real file-lock leaks.
Scalability potential: Platform fallback changes only cold QA crash-injection route, not runtime save identity. Low through Ultra use identical correctness checks.
Hardware Impact: Failure path is bounded to one delete plus one move; avoids manual cleanup loops and extra disk scans.
Problem: 64-byte false-sharing proof existed in code but not in automated editor tests.
Solution: Add edit-test layout assertions for `WalFuzzTelemetryEntry` and `WalFuzzFileHandleStatusDTO`, including explicit layout and cache-line size.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying on comments or log self-audit was rejected because layout drift must fail in Unity test/import, not in human review.
Scalability potential: DTO shape is stable across all quality levels and device tiers.
Hardware Impact: Cache-line aligned telemetry/file-handle rows prevent adjacent-worker invalidation if scanner grows into parallel verifier.
Problem: failed `.partial` WAL promotion could return `false` without deleting abandoned partial file.
Solution: Delete partial WAL immediately when `TryReplaceOrMoveWal` reports failure. next fuzz iteration starts from clean primary/backup pair instead of inheriting stale interrupted bytes.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying on outer catch cleanup was rejected because replacement helper returns `false` on controlled fallback failure and does not throw. Leaving partial files for postmortem was rejected because black-box dump already records failed offset and flags.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all keep same correctness route. Cleanup runs only on failure and does not alter save truth.
Hardware Impact: Failure path adds one delete check and possible delete; normal path cost is 0 us.
Problem: editor facade still looked more like standard Unity debug window than neighboring zero-GC-oriented save tuners.
Solution: Cache `IDataVault` in window lifecycle and format telemetry/scanner summaries through fixed `char[192]` scratch with indexed append helpers. UI Toolkit still requires managed `string` assignment, but assignment is now gated through `SetSummaryText` and changes only when content differs.
Rejected Alternatives: Polling `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` during every graph repaint was rejected because registry is cold identity. Full TMP `SetCharArray` replacement was rejected because this is UI Toolkit editor window, not runtime TMP surface.
Scalability potential: Editor cost remains isolated from runtime; high/ultra QA can run richer profiles without extra registry polling in facade.
Hardware Impact: Editor graph repaint avoids two cold registry property reads when cached; gameplay-frame impact remains 0 us.
Problem: first prompt re-extraction command used too-narrow XML regex that only matched `<AGENT_PROMPT id="SHINOBU_357">` and missed real tag because it also contains `role` and `chat_name` attributes.
Solution: Re-run extraction with `<AGENT_PROMPT[^>]*id="SHINOBU_357"[^>]*>[\s\S]*?</AGENT_PROMPT>`, yielding `PROMPT_FOUND=1`, `PROMPT_BYTES=22513`, and `TASK_COUNT=19`. Correct status/log evidence to record attribute-aware extraction instead of false rotated-batch absence.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping false rotated-batch note was rejected because exact block exists at line 6947. Rewriting task count to 20 was rejected because extracted SHINOBU_357 XML contains 19 `Task NN:` entries.
Scalability potential: Documentation correction has no runtime tier effect; it protects CI/integrator review from false evidence.
Hardware Impact: Static extraction only; gameplay-frame impact is 0 us.
Problem: compile gate briefly opened at 49.1% CPU with no active `dotnet/csc/MSBuild` rows, but later pre-build resamples hit 85.1% and then 99% CPU.
Solution: Do not launch `dotnet build`; keep verification to diff-check, source scans, and documented build-blocked status until CPU is consistently under 50% project threshold.
Rejected Alternatives: Starting compile during CPU spike was rejected because it violates AGENTS.md hardware protection rule and risks contention with other agents.
